title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text: This composite contains the Lonza P3 workflows from four sources. They differ in preparation of CD8 cells, experimental-guide and Cas9 input, controls, and post-electroporation culture. Use one complete source-specific option for each difference and confirm current lab-approved conditions before beginning.

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
Source files

Alex Monell — Cas9 Nucleofection_ATM
Kelsey Bennion — Electroporation of activated CD8
Giovanni Galleti — CB6.CRISPRCas9 KO
Nicole Sharping — 062923 CRISPRCas9 KO in primary T cells for in vivo transfer with Lonza - single guides

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
1. Prepare CD8 T cells

Enrichment or prior activation
Derived from: Alex Monell, Giovanni Galleti, and Nicole Sharping.
Enrich naïve CD8 T cells before electroporation, or activate cells 24 hours beforehand. These sources specify Lonza P3 buffer, DN100 for naïve CD8 cells, and DS137 for activated CD8 cells.


Complete isolation and activation route
Derived from: Kelsey Bennion.
Kelsey provides a full route from spleen and lymph-node collection through ACK lysis, negative magnetic CD8 selection, purity assessment, and anti-CD3/anti-CD28 activation for 18–24 hours.

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
2. Assemble RNP complexes
Derived from: Alex Monell, Kelsey Bennion, Giovanni Galleti, and Nicole Sharping.

Use 100 µM crRNA and tracrRNA with a stated 3:1 guide-RNA-to-Cas9 molar ratio.
For a Thy1-only control, combine 3 µL Thy1 crRNA and 3 µL tracrRNA.
For experimental conditions, use the source-specific crRNA and Cas9 amounts shown in the differences table.
Anneal guide and tracrRNA at 95°C for 5 minutes, then hold at room temperature in the dark for 1 hour.
Add 40 µM Cas9, gently mix and briefly spin down, then incubate at room temperature for 20 minutes.

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
3. Prepare cells and P3 buffer
Derived from: Alex Monell, Kelsey Bennion, Giovanni Galleti, and Nicole Sharping.

Prepare P3 buffer at room temperature: 3.6 µL Supplement 1 plus 16.4 µL P3 per reaction.
Prewarm R10 with 50 U/mL IL-2 to 37°C.
Count 2–10 × 106 cells per reaction, wash in sterile room-temperature PBS, and pellet at 5000 RPM for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove residual liquid completely and resuspend each pellet in 20 µL P3 buffer. Limit the cells’ time in P3 buffer.

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
4. Electroporate cells
Derived from: Alex Monell, Kelsey Bennion, Giovanni Galleti, and Nicole Sharping.

Mix 5 µL RNP with 20 µL cells in P3 buffer.
Transfer the 25 µL mixture to the bottom of a Lonza nucleofector strip well without introducing bubbles.
Run DN100 for naïve CD8 cells or DS137 for activated CD8 cells.
Immediately add 130 µL prewarmed R10 and rest cells for 10 minutes at 37°C and 5% CO2.

title: Cas9 Electroporation with Lonza 2
text:
5. Recover and analyze cells

Direct recovery and in vivo transfer
Derived from: Alex Monell and Nicole Sharping.
Recover cells from the strip, wash with an additional 150 µL R10, and add 700 µL prewarmed R10 to reach 1 mL total. Count with Trypan Blue; both sources note 20–50% T-cell loss. For in vivo transfer, resuspend in PBS at the desired concentration and retain cells for flow or Sanger validation.


Overnight recovery
Derived from: Giovanni Galleti.
Prepare R10 plus 15 U/mL IL-2 by combining 600 µL R10 plus 50 U/mL IL-2 with 1400 µL plain R10. Return cells to their original number of wells and culture overnight or for 24 hours.


Extended culture and validation
Derived from: Kelsey Bennion.
Kelsey describes cytokine replenishment every 48 hours, 25 U/mL IL-2 or TRM-polarization medium, and downstream collection for flow, genomic-DNA/Sanger, RNA/qPCR, and supernatant ELISA analyses.

title: Mouse CD8 isolation and CD3 activation
text:
1. Prepare activation plates
Choose one coating strategy and prepare the plate before beginning the isolation.

Direct anti-CD3 coating — Nicole_s protocols

Begin approximately 3 hours before plating cells.
Dilute anti-CD3 to 5 µg/mL in sterile PBS.
Add 1 mL per well of a six-well plate. The source uses three wells per spleen-plus-lymph-node isolation.
Tap the plate gently to cover the well surface.
Incubate at 37°C for approximately 3 hours.



Goat anti-hamster IgG coating — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse and t_cells

Begin at least 2 hours before plating cells.
Dilute goat anti-hamster IgG 1:30 in sterile PBS.
Add 550 µL per well of a six-well plate.
Tap the plate gently to cover the well surface.
Incubate at 37°C for at least 2 hours.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse also permits coating overnight at 4°C.

title: Mouse CD8 isolation and CD3 activation
text:
2. Harvest and homogenize tissues

Collect the spleen and desired lymph nodes into medium or buffer.
Mechanically dissociate the tissues to produce a single-cell suspension.
Centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes and remove the supernatant.


Tissue-processing differences

Nicole_s protocols: Homogenize spleen and lymph nodes in R10 using a filter in a dish. Rinse the apparatus with additional R10 and collect the wash.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Collect spleen plus inguinal, brachial, and axillary lymph nodes in R10; avoid mesenteric lymph nodes when possible. Pass cells through a 70 µm filter, place the filter over a 50 mL conical tube, and wash the dish twice with 1 mL RP5.
t_cells: Homogenize tissues in PBS using frosted glass slides and transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube.

3. Lyse red blood cells
Choose the timing used by the source workflow:

Nicole_s protocols: Resuspend in 1 mL ACK, incubate for 3 minutes at room temperature, dilute with 3 mL R10, and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Resuspend in 1 mL ACK, incubate for 4 minutes, add 40 mL MACS buffer, and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes.
t_cells: Resuspend in 1–2 mL ACK, incubate for 5–6 minutes at room temperature, neutralize with 3–4 mL MACS buffer, and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes.

Remove the supernatant completely before beginning negative-selection staining.

text:
5. Stain cells for negative selection

Resuspend the cell pellet in the selected biotin-antibody cocktail.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C, protected from light.
Wash with MACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes and remove the supernatant.


Staining-volume differences

Nicole_s protocols: Use 3 mL biotin-antibody stain per spleen-plus-lymph-node sample and wash with 10 mL MACS buffer.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Use 500 µL cocktail, scaling at approximately 100 µL per 10^7 cells when needed. Fill the tube with approximately 10–14 mL MACS buffer for the wash. The source also expresses the centrifugation condition as approximately 400 × g for 4 minutes.
t_cells: Use 500 µL cocktail, fill the tube with MACS buffer for the wash, and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes.

section: 6. Label depleted populations with streptavidin beads
text:
6. Label depleted populations with streptavidin beads

Resuspend the washed cells in 500 µL MACS buffer.
Add streptavidin magnetic beads:

100 µL: Nicole_s protocols
50 µL: Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse and t_cells

Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C, protected from light.
Wash with MACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend cells for column loading:

1 mL MACS buffer: Nicole_s protocols
500 µL MACS buffer: Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse and t_cells

title: Mouse CD8 isolation and CD3 activation
text:
7. Perform magnetic negative selection

Attach the appropriate MACS column to the magnet.
Equilibrate the column with 3 mL MACS buffer and discard this initial flow-through.
Apply the cell suspension to the column.
Collect the unlabeled flow-through. This fraction contains the enriched, untouched CD8 T cells.
Wash the column with 3 mL MACS buffer, combining each wash with the collected flow-through:

Two washes: Nicole_s protocols
Three washes: Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse and t_cells

Do not allow the column to dry during separation (Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse).
Centrifuge the collected flow-through at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes and remove the supernatant.

title: Mouse CD8 isolation and CD3 activation
text:
8. Count cells and assess purity

Resuspend enriched cells in culture medium and count them.
Assess viability when required.
Check CD8 enrichment by flow cytometry when possible.


Source-specific resuspension and purity checks

Nicole_s protocols: Resuspend in 6 mL R10 and count with an automated cell counter.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Resuspend initially in approximately 500 µL R10, count, and assess viability with Trypan Blue or another method. Stain a pre- and post-isolation aliquot with FITC-CD8β at 1:100, wash once with FACS buffer, and acquire by flow cytometry. The source notes that 90–95% purity may be assumed only when a rapid workflow is necessary.
t_cells: Resuspend in 500 µL TCM, count, and adjust to 2 × 10^6 cells/mL.

title: Mouse CD8 isolation and CD3 activation
section: 9. Plate and activate enriched CD8 T cells
text:
9. Plate and activate enriched CD8 T cells
Use the activation method that matches the plate-coating strategy from step 1.

Direct anti-CD3-coated plate — Nicole_s protocols

Remove the anti-CD3/PBS coating solution and leave the wells free of residual liquid.
Supplement the enriched cells with anti-CD28 at 2 µg/mL and IL-2 at 50 U/mL; the source describes IL-2 as a 1:2,000 dilution.
Plate 2 mL cell suspension per well. The source distributes 6 mL across three wells.
Handle and resuspend the cells gently.
Incubate at 37°C for 24 hours.



Goat anti-hamster IgG-coated plate — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse

Remove the coating solution.
Wash each well twice with 1 mL R10 and aspirate thoroughly.
Prepare anti-CD3 and anti-CD28, each at 1:500 in R10.
Add 1 mL cell suspension at 2 × 10^6 cells/mL to each well.
Add 1 mL anti-CD3/CD28 mixture to each well.
The resulting total volume is 2 mL, final density is 1 × 10^6 cells/mL, and each antibody is at a final 1:1,000 dilution.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 18–24 hours.

Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse also describes an anti-CD3-coated plate alternative: add anti-CD28 at 1:250 in the 1 mL antibody solution so that the final well concentration is 1 µg/mL after mixing with 1 mL cells.


Goat anti-hamster IgG-coated plate — t_cells

Wash each coated well twice with 1 mL TCM.
Plate 2 × 10^6 cells in 1 mL TCM per well.
Dilute anti-CD3 and anti-CD28, each at 1:500 in TCM.
Add 1 mL antibody mixture to each well and mix gently.
The resulting total volume is 2 mL, final density is 1 × 10^6 cells/mL, and each antibody is at a final 1:1,000 dilution.
Incubate at 37°C until the planned downstream processing time. The source does not specify an exact duration.

text:
10. Record the selected conditions
Document the following for reproducibility:

Mouse strain, tissue sources, and lymph-node groups
Cell count before and after selection
Depletion-antibody clones and amounts
Streptavidin-bead volume and column type
Number of column washes
Post-isolation purity and viability
Plate-coating method
Anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 clones, stock concentrations, and final concentrations
Cell density, culture volume, IL-2 condition, and activation duration

title: LCMV CL13 Titer Calculator
text:
LCMV CL13 Titer Calculator
This calculator is adapted from LCMV CL13 Titer calculator.xlsx. Enter the total volume of diluted virus needed; the required stock-virus and PBS volumes update immediately.
The target concentration is 1 × 10^7 PFU/mL, which delivers 2 × 10^6 PFU in 200 µL. One milliliter provides five 200 µL doses.

title: Propagate LCMV Clone 13
text:
Propagate LCMV Clone 13 virus
BHK media (500 mL):


500 mL DMEM (high glucose, liquid)


50 mL FBS (10%)


5 mL L-glutamine (100x)


5 mL Pen-strep (100x)


25 mL Tryptose phosphate broth (Gibco)


Day -1:


Plate BHK to be ~40-50% confluent the following day. Seed about 5x10 6 BHK cells in a T175 flask the day before infection. The cells will grow to a confluency of 40-50%, corresponding to ~1x107.


Note
BHK cells grow at different rates in different labs and seem to be pretty sensitive. Consider setting up flasks at target multiple confluencies to try to hit the right one on the infection day.
Day 0:


Take photos of the T175 flasks on the light microscope if possible - try to record what a good confluency looks like.


Pipet off media and infect with virus in a limited volume (6 mL for a T175, 3 mL for a T75). The MOI used in the field seems to vary; many people use 0.001-0.01, but Teijaro lab uses an MOI of 0.1.



The lore is that it is important to use a high titer virus to inoculate, but unclear where this line is drawn.


Teijaro adds 5 uL of 2x10 8 PFU/mL stock to 6 mL BHK media to hit a target of MOI 0.1 for 107 cells in a T175.


Allen lab has a stock at 2.58e8/ml (Floor 2 lab -80, rack 00156, box 01649). I added 4 ul per 6 mls of media per flask or 24 ul per 36 mls for 6 T175 flasks



Incubate at 37 Celsius for 90 minutes. Gently tilt and rock the flask every 10-15 minutes.


After 90 minutes, add 19 mL warm BHK media (total 25 mL final).


Incubate for 72 hours.


Day 3
Keep the virus cold for all following steps!


Pipet supernatant into 15 mL conical tubes. The supernatant contains the virus. Be careful, this is a LOT of LCMV. Have bleach handy in case of a spill.


Separate any remaining BHK cells that were aspirated from virus.



Spin at 2000 rpm in a benchtop centrifuge (~800-850 g depending on centrifuge in IMPL-K) for 15 minutes.


Collect the supernatant, transfer to a fresh tube.


Repeat for a total of two centrifugation steps.



Keeping the virus cold, aliquot and snap freeze in liquid nitrogen. Pre-chill cryo-tubes in cold room.


Protocol yields ~20-25 mL virus containing supernatant at a target of ~2x108 pfu/mL.



Infecting at 2x10 6 pfu/mouse (100 uL of 2x10 7 pfu/mL), this corresponds to enough virus to infect 2000 mice per T175 of LCMV Clone 13.



Titrate the virus. Make sure to titrate an aliquot that has been frozen and thawed to get a representative value for what the titer will be when you inject from a thawed aliquot (rather than titrating the supernatant directly).

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text: This composite brings together Plat-E transfection, retrovirus collection, and primary CD8 T-cell transduction workflows. Source protocols use different plate formats, reagent amounts, media, and downstream handling. Choose a single compatible source-specific route when the alternatives differ; do not combine quantities across routes without confirming the current lab-approved conditions.

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text:
Source files

Alex Monell — Transfection
Goldrath Lab — Transfection Protocol
Nicole Sharping — NES 042924 CD8 T cell transduction and double transduction
Maximilian Heeg — Make Retrovirus

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text:
1. Prepare Plat-E cells
All four sources use Plat-E packaging cells and specify medium without Pen/Strep during the transfection setup.

10 cm or 6-well production route
Derived from: Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg.

Plate Plat-E cells the day before transfection in medium without Pen/Strep.
For a 10 cm dish, use 2.5 × 106 cells in 10 mL medium. For a 6-well plate, use 0.5 × 106 cells per well in 2 mL medium.
On the following day, replace the medium with fresh Plat-E medium before adding the transfection mixture.



96-well screening route
Derived from: Goldrath Lab.

Plate 2–4 × 104 Plat-E cells per well in a 96-well flat-bottom plate, with a final volume of 200 µL per well.
Use the middle 60 wells for transfection and fill the outer 36 wells with 100 µL medium.
Use Plat-E medium without Pen/Strep. The source defines this medium as DMEM with L-glutamine, 10% FBS, 50 µM BME, and 10 mM HEPES.
At least one hour before transfection, remove 150 µL medium and replace it with 50 µL fresh, warm Plat-E medium without Pen/Strep.



Expanded 10 cm production route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.

For a full transduction timeline, thaw Platinum-E cells five days before transduction, wash, and expand them on a 15 cm plate in D10.
Two days before transduction, trypsinize, count, and plate 2 × 106 cells per 10 cm plate.

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text:
2. Transfect Plat-E cells
All sources use pCL-Eco helper plasmid, a plasmid of interest, OptiMEM or serum-free DMEM, Mirus/TransIT-LT1 reagent, a room-temperature incubation, and dropwise addition to cells. Use one complete format below.

Alex Monell 10 cm route
Derived from: Alex Monell.

Prepare Tube 1 with 5 µg pCL-Eco in 550 µL OptiMEM. Aliquot 600 µL into a 15 mL tube and add 10 µg transfer plasmid.
Prepare Tube 2 with 45 µL Mirus reagent and 655 µL OptiMEM.
Add 700 µL of Tube 2 mixture to each Tube 1 aliquot, incubate at room temperature for 20 minutes, then add dropwise to cells.



Goldrath Lab 96-well route
Derived from: Goldrath Lab.

Per transfection well, add 1 µL of 100 ng/µL pCL-Eco and 9 µL OptiMEM to Tube 1, then add 200 ng shRNA plasmid.
Per well, prepare Tube 2 with 0.6 µL Mirus reagent and 9.4 µL OptiMEM.
Add Tube 2 to Tube 1 last, mix, incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature, and add the mixture dropwise to cells.
The source notes that a 6-well format typically uses approximately 0.8–1.2 × 106 cells in 2 mL per well and scales the reagents approximately tenfold.



Nicole Sharping single- or double-plasmid route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.

Warm 700 µL serum-free DMEM to room temperature.
For a single transduction, add 6 µg plasmid of interest and 2 µg pCL-Eco. For a double transduction, distribute 6 µg total plasmid of interest among the plasmids and add 2 µg pCL-Eco.
Add 30 µL room-temperature TransIT-LT1, mix, incubate at room temperature for 20–30 minutes, then drip the mixture onto cells.
Incubate overnight and replace Plat-E medium with fresh R10 the next morning; retain subsequent medium for virus collection.



Maximilian Heeg 10 cm or 6-well route
Derived from: Maximilian Heeg.

For a 10 cm dish, mix 5 µg pCL-Eco in 550 µL OptiMEM, add 10 µg plasmid, then add a mixture of 45 µL Mirus and 655 µL OptiMEM.
For a 6-well plate, mix 0.5 µg pCL-Eco in 125 µL OptiMEM, add 2 µg plasmid, then add a mixture of 7.5 µL Mirus and 117.5 µL OptiMEM.
Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature and add dropwise to cells.

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text:
3. Collect or use retrovirus

Harvest-and-store route
Derived from: Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg.

The day after transfection, replace old medium with fresh T-cell medium (TCM).
On the next day, harvest the first virus-containing supernatant, store it refrigerated, and add fresh TCM.
On the following day, harvest the remaining supernatant and combine it with the first collection.
Spin at 1600 RPM for 4 minutes, aliquot or use immediately, and freeze stored virus at −80°C. For fresh virus, the sources specify filtration through a 0.45 µm filter.



Direct-use or small-volume harvest route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping and Goldrath Lab.

Nicole Sharping directs changing to R10 the morning after transfection and retaining that medium for transduction; before loading virus onto Retronectin, spin the viral medium to pellet floating Plat-E cells.
Goldrath Lab directs replacing 70 µL with warm T-cell medium on Day 3, harvesting 70 µL supernatant on Day 4, and harvesting/pooling the remaining 170 µL per well on Day 5. The source activates CD8 T cells on Day 4 for next-day transduction.

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
section: 4. Activate and transduce primary CD8 T cells
text:
4. Activate and transduce primary CD8 T cells
Derived from: Nicole Sharping. This is the only supplied source that specifies primary CD8 T-cell activation and Retronectin-based transduction.

On the day before transduction, coat a flat-bottom 6-well plate with anti-CD3 in sterile PBS (5 µg/mL for P14 or 10 µg/mL for wild-type CD8 T cells) for 3 hours at 37°C.
Isolate CD8 T cells, then activate approximately 5 × 106 cells per well in 2 mL R10 with 2 µg/mL anti-CD28 and 50 U/mL hIL-2 for at least 24 hours.
Coat non-tissue-culture-treated 6-well plates overnight at 4°C with 1 mL per viral group of 15 µg/mL Retronectin in sterile PBS.
Remove Retronectin, block with 4 mL R10 per well for 30 minutes at 37°C, and warm the centrifuge to 37°C.
Remove the block, load 1 mL virus per well for 30 minutes at 37°C, replace with a second 1 mL virus aliquot, and incubate for another 30 minutes.
Pellet activated cells, resuspend them in the remaining viral medium with 50 U/mL IL-2, transfer them to the virus-coated wells, and spin at 1600 RPM and 37°C for 45 minutes.
Culture overnight, replace medium with fresh R10 plus IL-2 the next morning, and maintain cells at 1 × 106/mL. The source reduces IL-2 to 25 U/mL at 5–6 days after activation.

title: Transfect and Transduce 1
text:
Similarities and differences among sources








Topic
Similarity
Difference and source attribution




Packaging cells and antibiotic
All sources use Plat-E/Platinum-E packaging cells; each uses or recommends medium without Pen/Strep for the transfection setup.
Nicole Sharping begins with a five-day thaw/expansion timeline, whereas Alex Monell, Goldrath Lab, and Maximilian Heeg begin with plating cells for transfection.


Plate format and density
Each source plates packaging cells before transfection.
Goldrath Lab uses a 96-well format (2–4 × 104 cells/well); Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg specify 10 cm and 6-well densities; Nicole Sharping specifies 2 × 106 cells per 10 cm plate.


Helper plasmid and reagent
Each source includes pCL-Eco and Mirus/TransIT-LT1 with a plasmid of interest.
Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg use 5 µg pCL-Eco plus 10 µg plasmid for 10 cm dishes; Goldrath Lab uses 100 ng pCL-Eco plus 200 ng shRNA per 96-well; Nicole Sharping uses 2 µg pCL-Eco plus 6 µg total plasmid.


Complex formation
All sources prepare a DNA/reagent mixture, incubate at room temperature, and add it dropwise.
Nicole Sharping specifies 20–30 minutes in serum-free DMEM; Alex Monell, Goldrath Lab, and Maximilian Heeg specify 20 minutes with OptiMEM-based mixtures.


Post-transfection medium
All sources change or replace medium after transfection before using or collecting virus.
Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg change to TCM and collect on Days 4–5; Goldrath Lab makes small sequential collections; Nicole Sharping changes to R10 and uses the resulting virus directly for transduction.


Virus storage and processing
All sources produce retroviral supernatant for downstream transduction.
Alex Monell and Maximilian Heeg specify a 1600 RPM, 4-minute clarification and −80°C storage; Maximilian Heeg additionally specifies 0.45 µm filtration for fresh virus. Nicole Sharping instead specifies pelleting floating Plat-E cells immediately before Retronectin loading.


Primary CD8 handling
Virus generated by each source can support a transduction workflow.
Only Nicole Sharping specifies anti-CD3/anti-CD28/IL-2 activation, Retronectin coating, two virus-loading incubations, spinoculation, and subsequent CD8 culture.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
Before starting

Review the antibody datasheet for recommended buffer, staining temperature, and incubation time. Some internalizing or recycling receptors may require staining at 37°C (Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS).
Mix antibodies thoroughly and briefly spin them down to reduce aggregates. An antibody master mix may instead be prepared and spun before staining (Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS).
Select cells containing a clearly identifiable positive and negative population.
Choose a dilution range broad enough to bracket the expected optimum.
Include an unstained sample and the required single-color compensation controls.
For tandem dyes, use the same antibody conjugate in the compensation control (Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS).

title: Antibody Titration
text:
Materials

Cells containing positive and negative populations for the target antigen
Antibody to be titrated
Optional co-staining antibodies
Calcium- and magnesium-free PBS
FACS buffer: PBS with 2% FBS
Fc block

Fixation and permeabilization reagents appropriate for the target

Optional Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer

BD Cytofix/Cytoperm kit for cytokines or other cytoplasmic targets

title: Antibody Titration
text:
1. Prepare cells

Count the cells and divide equal numbers among the titration conditions.
Wash once with PBS.
If cells are suspended in complete RPMI, wash thoroughly with PBS to remove FBS or BSA before using an amine-reactive viability dye (Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS).


Cell-input options

Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS: The viability-dye example is calculated for 10 × 10^6 cells per sample and uses eight tubes.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Combine suitable positive and negative cells when needed. The source example uses approximately 60 × 10^6 total cells and plates 2 × 10^6 cells per well.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
2. Viability stain and Fc block

Prepare the selected viability dye according to its product instructions.
Resuspend each sample in 50 µL Fc block.
Add 50 µL viability-dye mix.
Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Wash and remove the supernatant.


Viability-dye options

Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS: Prepare Live/Dead Blue mix for four samples by combining 19.5 µL water with 0.5 µL dye, then adding 380 µL PBS. Wash afterward with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Use APC-Cy7 live/dead dye at 1:500. Wash once with 100 µL FACS buffer.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
3. Design the dilution series
Prepare antibody solutions at 2× the desired final concentration when equal volumes of antibody solution and cell suspension will be combined.

Example plate series — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse



Well
Final antibody dilution




1
1:50


2
1:100


3
1:200


4
1:400


5
1:800


Control
Unstained



The source begins the serial dilution at 1:25 so that adding it to an equal volume of cell suspension produces a 1:50 final dilution.


Eight-tube series — Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS

Resuspend cells in 50 µL FACS buffer per tube.
Add 50 µL FACS buffer to every tube except tube 1. Add 5 µL Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer per test when appropriate.
Prepare at least 115 µL of a 2× antibody mix in the same staining buffer.
Add 50 µL antibody mix to tubes 1 and 2.
Mix tube 2 and transfer 50 µL from tube 2 to tube 3.
Continue mixing and transferring 50 µL through tube 7.
Remove and discard 50 µL from tube 7. Tube 8 remains the unstained control.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
4. Surface-antibody titration

Add the selected antibody dilution to each sample.
Add optional surface co-staining antibodies at their established titers.
Incubate for 20 minutes at 4°C in the dark unless the antibody datasheet requires another condition.
Wash and remove the supernatant.


Tube workflow — Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS

Add 50 µL cell suspension to each tube containing the prepared dilution.
After staining, wash with 2 mL FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes.
If the target antibody requires 20 minutes at 37°C, perform its titration under that condition before adding the remaining surface co-stain.



Plate workflow — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse

Resuspend cells in 50 µL surface-staining solution per well.
The source uses established CD45.2-BV510 and CD45.2-BV786 co-stains at 1:100.
After staining, wash twice with 100 µL FACS buffer.

Proceed to acquisition if fixation is unnecessary. For intracellular targets, continue with the appropriate branch below.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
5. Intracellular or intranuclear titration
Prepare intracellular antibody dilutions in the permeabilization buffer specified by the selected kit. Do not use Super Bright Complete Staining Buffer for intracellular antibodies (Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS).

Foxp3/transcription-factor workflow — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse

Prepare fixation buffer by combining one part fixation/permeabilization concentrate with three parts diluent. The source example uses 1 mL concentrate plus 3 mL diluent.
Prepare 1× permeabilization buffer by combining one part 10× stock with nine parts water.
Resuspend cells in 100 µL fixation buffer.
Incubate for 20 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
During fixation, add 100 µL permeabilization buffer to the first serial-dilution well and 50 µL to each successive well.
Add the antibody to the first well at 1:25, mix, and transfer 50 µL sequentially to generate 2× solutions for final dilutions of 1:50 through 1:800.
Leave the final control well without antibody.
Wash cells once with 100 µL permeabilization buffer, not FACS buffer.
Resuspend cells in the corresponding intracellular-antibody dilution.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Wash once with permeabilization buffer and once with FACS buffer.



Cytofix/Cytoperm workflow — Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse

After the surface-staining wash, add 100 µL Cytofix per well.
Incubate for 20 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Prepare 1× permeabilization buffer by combining one part 10× stock with nine parts water.
Generate the 2× two-fold antibody dilution series in Cytoperm permeabilization buffer as described above.
Wash cells once with 100 µL permeabilization buffer.
Resuspend cells in the corresponding intracellular-antibody dilution.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Wash once with permeabilization buffer and once with FACS buffer.



General fixation option — Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS

Add 150 µL BioLegend fix buffer and incubate for 10 minutes, or use the preferred fixation/permeabilization conditions for the application.
Wash with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes.
For an intracellular or intranuclear titration, repeat the serial-dilution approach using Perm/Wash buffer instead of FACS buffer.
Add any intracellular co-staining antibodies after fixation and permeabilization.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
6. Compensation controls — Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS

Vortex compensation beads thoroughly.
For each antibody fluorophore, combine one drop UltraComp eBeads with antibody at the selected titer. Use at least 0.5 µL antibody when the selected volume is lower.
Prepare an unstained control with one drop UltraComp eBeads.
For Live/Dead Blue, prepare a positive control with two drops ArC Amine Reactive beads plus 2 µL dye.
Prepare the Live/Dead Blue negative control with two drops ArC Amine Negative beads and no dye.
Incubate controls for at least 20 minutes in the dark.
Wash antibody-stained beads with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 4 minutes. Do not wash the positive or negative Live/Dead Blue controls in this source workflow.
When matching fixed samples, fix antibody compensation beads with 150 µL of 1% formaldehyde or PFA in HBSS for 15 minutes in a chemical hood. Do not fix the Live/Dead Blue controls in this source workflow.
Wash fixed beads with 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 1,600 rpm for 5 minutes.
Resuspend controls in 200 µL FACS buffer and keep at 4°C until acquisition.

For spectral cytometry, include an unstained-cell control to model cellular autofluorescence. Single-stained cells are optional but recommended. Beads are preferred when they represent the fluorophore appropriately.

title: Antibody Titration
text:
7. Acquire and select the titer

Resuspend samples in FACS buffer and keep them at 4°C until acquisition.

Giovanni_s Protocols/FACS: 200 µL per tube.
Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse: Samples are ready after the final permeabilization-buffer and FACS-buffer washes.

Acquire every titration sample with identical instrument settings.
Use established QC voltages when applicable (Kelsey_s Protocols/Mouse).
Gate the same positive and negative populations in every sample.
Compare signal separation, background, percentage positive, and staining pattern across the series.
Select the lowest antibody concentration that provides maximal or near-maximal separation without unacceptable background or nonspecific staining.
Record the antibody clone, fluorophore, lot, cell type, staining buffer, time, temperature, and selected dilution.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text: This page combines two Retronectin-based transduction workflows. The Retronectin loading volumes, spin duration, virus-production instructions, and post-transduction handling differ. Select one complete source-specific option for each difference and confirm current lab-approved conditions before use.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text:
Source files

Alex Monell — Transduction - High Quality
Nicole Sharping — NES 042924 CD8 T cell transduction and double transduction

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
section: 1. Prepare virus and activated CD8 T cells
text:
1. Prepare virus and activated CD8 T cells

Virus-production and detailed activation route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.

Thaw and expand Plat-E cells beginning five days before transduction, then plate 2 × 106 cells per 10 cm plate two days before transduction.
Transfect Plat-E cells with 2 µg pCL-Eco, 6 µg total plasmid of interest, and 30 µL TransIT-LT1 in 700 µL serum-free DMEM. For double transduction, divide the 6 µg total plasmid across the plasmids of interest.
Coat flat-bottom 6-well plates with anti-CD3 (5 µg/mL for P14 or 10 µg/mL for wild-type CD8 cells), then activate isolated CD8 T cells with anti-CD28 and 50 U/mL hIL-2 for at least 24 hours.



Activation-only route
Derived from: Alex Monell.
Begin with CD8 T-cell isolation and activation. Alex’s source does not include packaging-cell or virus-production instructions.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text:
2. Coat and block Retronectin plates

Alex Monell coating route
Derived from: Alex Monell.

Use a non-tissue-culture-treated 6-well plate.
Prepare sufficient Retronectin mixture for the number of wells plus one extra well, add 1 mL per well, wrap the plate carefully with parafilm, and incubate at 4°C overnight.
On the transduction day, remove Retronectin, add 4 mL warmed TCM dropwise to each well, and block for 30 minutes at 37°C.



Nicole Sharping coating route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.

Prepare Retronectin at 15 µg/mL in sterile PBS and add 1 mL per well of a non-tissue-culture-treated 6-well plate.
Seal the plate and incubate at 4°C overnight.
Remove Retronectin, add 4 mL R10 dropwise to block nonspecific sites, and incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C while warming the centrifuge to 37°C.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text:
3. Load virus and transduce cells

Alex Monell transduction route
Derived from: Alex Monell.

Thaw virus in a hot-water bath, then keep it on ice once thawed.
Remove blocking TCM, add 750 µL virus per well, and incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C. Replace with a fresh 750 µL virus aliquot and incubate another 30 minutes.
Pool cells, pellet at 1600 RPM for 4 minutes at room temperature, and prepare TCM plus IL-2 at the source’s stated 1:1667 dilution.
Add 500 µL cell suspension and 1.5 mL virus to each well. Spin at 1600 RPM and 37°C for 40 minutes, then incubate at 37°C for 24 hours.



Nicole Sharping transduction route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.

Collect viral medium from Plat-E cells and pellet floating packaging cells.
Remove blocking R10, add 1 mL virus per well for 30 minutes at 37°C, then repeat with a second 1 mL virus aliquot for 30 minutes.
Collect activated T cells, pellet them, and resuspend them in remaining viral medium with 50 U/mL IL-2.
Add cells to virus-coated wells, wrap the plate in cellophane, and spin at 1600 RPM and 37°C for 45 minutes. Incubate overnight, then replace medium with fresh R10 plus IL-2 the next morning.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text:
4. Follow up after transduction

Alex Monell sorting and transfer route
Derived from: Alex Monell.
On Day 3, collect cell populations separately, wash wells with MACS buffer, pellet at 1600 RPM for 4 minutes, resuspend in MACS buffer, filter cells, sort them into FACS tubes with FBS, wash sorted cells, resuspend in PBS, and count before preparing for transfer.


Nicole Sharping culture route
Derived from: Nicole Sharping.
Maintain cells at 1 × 106/mL with R10 plus IL-2. At 5–6 days after activation, reduce IL-2 to 25 U/mL. Nicole’s source describes proliferation through days 7–10 and viability through days 10–14 after activation.

title: Transduction Retronectin 3
text:
Differences between source protocols



Difference
Alex Monell
Nicole Sharping




Virus and T-cell preparation
Begins with CD8 isolation and activation; no Plat-E production procedure is specified. Source: Alex Monell
Gives a five-day Plat-E production timeline plus anti-CD3/anti-CD28/hIL-2 CD8 activation. Source: Nicole Sharping


Retronectin specification
Calls for a Retronectin mixture sufficient for wells plus one extra but does not state a final concentration in the source. Source: Alex Monell
Specifies 15 µg/mL Retronectin in sterile PBS. Source: Nicole Sharping


Blocking medium
Uses 4 mL warmed TCM. Source: Alex Monell
Uses 4 mL R10 and directs warming the centrifuge during the block. Source: Nicole Sharping


Virus-loading volumes
Uses two 750 µL virus incubations, then adds 1.5 mL virus with cells. Source: Alex Monell
Uses two 1 mL virus incubations, then resuspends cells in remaining viral medium. Source: Nicole Sharping


Spinoculation
1600 RPM at 37°C for 40 minutes. Source: Alex Monell
1600 RPM at 37°C for 45 minutes. Source: Nicole Sharping


Post-transduction plan
Day 3 cell collection, filtering, sorting, counting, and transfer preparation. Source: Alex Monell
Extended R10/IL-2 culture with an IL-2 reduction at days 5–6. Source: Nicole Sharping

title: Crispr KO validation
text:
If it is not possible to validate the KO of a Crispr/Cas9 with Flow (or western), one can check if a deletion was introduced on the genomic DNA of the cells.
For that you need: ## Materials - At least 100.000 cells from your treated and control T cells - Kit to isolate genomic DNA (e.g. QIAamp DNA Blood Kits) - Primers to amplify the target region (see details below) - High-Fidelity Polymerase (e.g. Q5) - A PCR purification kit (e.g. DNA Clean & Concentrator-5)

title: Crispr KO validation
text:
Primer design
You need to sequence a stretch of DNA ~700bp enclosing the designed editing site. The projected break site should be located preferably ~200bp downstream from the sequencing start site. This region upstream of the break site is used to align the sequencing data of the test sample with that of the control sample.
I use use CHOPCHOP to design these primers. Under “Options” -> “Primers” select a product size between 500 and 800bp and a minimal distance from primer to target site of 200bp.



CHOPCHOP options


Next, click “Find target sites” and select your guideRNA. Here you can select one of the suggested primers.



CHOPCHOP results


Alternatively, you can design the primers as described here

title: LsgA Cloning
text: The LsgA Plasmig can be used as a vector to express guide RNAs for Crispr/Cas9. The Plasmid already contains all the “helper” sequences and we only need to add the guide RNA for the gene. It can than be used to create retrovirus using the pCL-Eco packaging plasmid.

title: LsgA Cloning
text:
sgRNA design
Get your guide RNA Sequence from IDT or ChopChop or anywhere else. Do not include the PAM sequence. The length of the guide RNA sould be 20 nucleotides.






Tip



OPTIONAL: Add G to 20 nt sgRNA sequence if it does not start with G to increase transcription.


Design the fwd and reverse oligos:
5’ –CACCGNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN –    3’
3’     –CNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNCAAA –5’

The CACC and the CAAA are the overlapping sequences to the digested plasmid. The G and C are the optimal base before the guide sequence to improve the transcription. NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN is the 20 bp guide RNA.
Order the primers.

Chill approximately 5 ng (2 μl) of the ligation mixture in a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Add 50 µl of competent cells to the DNA. Mix gently by pipetting up and down or flicking the tube 4–5 times to mix the cells and DNA. Do not vortex.
Place the mixture on ice for 30 minutes. Do not mix.
Heat shock at 42°C for 30 seconds. Do not mix.
Add 500 µl of SOC media to the tube.
Place tube at 37°C for 60 minutes. Shake vigorously (250 rpm) or rotate.
Warm selection plates to 37°C.
Spread 50–100 µl of the cells and ligation mixture onto the plates.
Incubate overnight at 37°C

title: Making LCMV stocks
text:
Note



Production of LCMV viral stocks. Protocol adapted from Kay Chung via John Teijaro and modified by Thomas Mann.
The production of LCMV is carried out in BHK (baby hamster kidney) cells.

title: Making LCMV stocks
text:
Reagents:

BHK media (500 mL):
500 mL DMEM (high glucose, liquid)
50 mL FBS (10%)
5 mL L-glutamine (100x)
5 mL Pen-strep (100x)
25 mL Tryptose phosphate broth (Gibco)

title: Making LCMV stocks
text:
Procedure:

Day -1:

Plate BHK to be ~40-50% confluent the following day. Seed about 5x10 6 BHK cells in a T175 flask the day before infection. The cells will grow to a confluency of 40-50%, corresponding to ~1x107.







Note



BHK cells grow at different rates in different labs and seem to be pretty sensitive. Consider setting up flasks at target multiple confluencies to try to hit the right one on the infection day.




Day 0:

Take photos of the T175 flasks on the light microscope if possible - try to record what a good confluency looks like.
Pipet off media and infect with virus in a limited volume (6 mL for a T175, 3 mL for a T75). The MOI used in the field seems to vary; many people use 0.001-0.01, but Teijaro lab uses an MOI of 0.1.

The lore is that it is important to use a high titer virus to inoculate, but unclear where this line is drawn.
Teijaro adds 5 uL of 2x10 8 PFU/mL stock to 6 mL BHK media to hit a target of MOI 0.1 for 107 cells in a T175.

Incubate at 37 Celsius for 90 minutes. Gently tilt and rock the flask every 10-15 minutes.
After 90 minutes, add 19 mL warm BHK media (total 25 mL final).
Incubate for 72 hours.



Day 3






Warning



Keep the virus cold for all following steps!



Pipet supernatant into 15 mL conical tubes. The supernatant contains the virus. Be careful, this is a LOT of LCMV. Have bleach handy in case of a spill.
Separate any remaining BHK cells that were aspirated from virus.

Spin at 2000 rpm in a benchtop centrifuge (~800-850 g depending on centrifuge in IMPL-K) for 15 minutes.
Collect the supernatant, transfer to a fresh tube.
Repeat for a total of two centrifugation steps.

Keeping the virus cold, aliquot and snap freeze in liquid nitrogen. Pre-chill cryo-tubes in cold room.
Protocol yields ~20-25 mL virus containing supernatant at a target of ~2x108 pfu/mL.

Infecting at 2x10 6 pfu/mouse (100 uL of 2x10 7 pfu/mL), this corresponds to enough virus to infect 2000 mice per T175 of LCMV Clone 13.

Titrate the virus. Make sure to titrate an aliquot that has been frozen and thawed to get a representative value for what the titer will be when you inject from a thawed aliquot (rather than titrating the supernatant directly).

title: Growing a Listeria stock
text:
Note



This is a protocol that I got from Maurice, Nicholas J (nmaurice@fredhutch.org) for the Lm-OVA variants (N4, Q4, T4)

title: Growing a Listeria stock
text:
Procedure

Inject 3000-4000 CFU into hosts (I just start with the vial in ~3-4mL Brain-heart infusion (BHI) media, with no antibiotic and move to step 9)
Sacrifice mice between 48 and 60 hrs post-infection
Harvest and tease apart spleen in 5ml PBS+0.1% NP40
Plate 200ml of spleen solution onto BHI+erythromycin plate [spread out sequentially to get single colonies]
Incubate for 48 hours
There should be little to no growth after 24 hours – the presence of large colonies at this time point suggests contamination.
Do not grow past 48 hours – overgrowth may occur
Harvest a single colony into 200ml of BHI+ erythromycin (in mc tube)
Take several medium-sized colonies (growth will be heterogeneous)
Grow for 4 hr with shaking 37°C (set speed higher to ensure agitation in mc tubes)
Inoculate 4ml of BHI (no antibiotic at this step) with LM-OVA from previous step
Expand with shaking until broth is mildly cloudy

Add 4ml of bacteria to 26ml of BHI broth in a 50ml Falcon tube (or 200ml flask) (depending on growth kinetics, you could set this up as an overnight)
Expand with shaking for several hours until broth is cloudy, add erythromycin for the last 45-60min of culturing (once the OD is at about 0.6) (I don’t bother with erythromycin since these are stable/do everything sterile)
Read OD: should be at 0.6 – 0.8 before moving on to step 13 (OD can be pushed a little higher; if overgrowth occurs, just add BHI and allow to re-enter log-phase of growth)
Add 15ml of the 40% glycerol stock (40% glycerol stock is 20mL glycerol in 30mL BHI; I sterile filter mine and use fresh) to the 30ml of cloudy bacteria culture
mix gently on ice and aliquot 1ml in screw top cryotubes (keep on wet ice while aliquoting) (I like my LM to be on wet ice to facilitate glycerol uptake for a bit before moving them into the -80°C freezer).
Freeze -80°C

title: Molecular_Cloning_Workflow
text:
4.2 Procedure
1. Confirm the restriction sites, expected fragment sizes, recommended buffer, incubation temperature, methylation sensitivity, and heat-inactivation conditions.
2. Assemble the reaction on ice. Add water and buffer first, followed by DNA. Add the restriction enzyme(s) last and mix gently.
3. Incubate at the recommended temperature. Use 1 hour as the routine standard. A 30-minute digest may be sufficient for some enzymes (HF); difficult digests may be extended to 2–4 hours. Dhruv typically digests for 4 hours for a complete digest. This may not always be the best option since some enzymes exhibit star activity.
4. Run the digest on an agarose gel with EtBr (4ul for small gel in 100ul). Separate the desired linearized vector or insert from uncut plasmid and unwanted fragments. Typically 1-1.5% agarose gels work well for large fragments.
5. Excise the correct band using UV visualization when available. Purify the DNA with a gel extraction kit and elute in a low volume (20ul)
6. Measure DNA concentration before ligation or HiFi assembly.

text:
Download the original PDF

Renaissance School of Medicine
Department of Microbiology and Immunology
Center for Infectious Diseases
12/11/2025
Ananda Goldrath, PhD
Dhruv Khanduja
Dear Ananda and Dhruv,
We provide this detailed protocol and Listeria information sheet to labs that request Listeria mutants we have generated. We are providing you with Listeria monocytogenes expressing the internalin A S192N Y369S mutations (InlAM) that also expresses the gp33 epitope on the 10403s background strain. The InlAM is based on the work of Wollert et al., Cell, 2007. The Lm-gp33 strain was generated by Hao Shen and murinized by my lab. Please cite Sheridan et al., Immunity, 2013 when referencing the InlAM Lm in any publications. Please reach out for any clarifications or questions.
Listeria:
InlAM Lm (10403s)
InlAM Lm-gp33 (10403s)
Sincerely,

Brian S. Sheridan, Ph.D.
Associate Professor
Department of Microbiology and Immunology
Center for Infectious Diseases
Renaissance School of Medicine
Stony Brook University
246 Centers for Molecular Medicine
Stony Brook, NY 11794-5120
Phone: 631-632-4459
Email: brian.sheridan@stonybrook.edu
Listeria monocytogenes Protocol
L. monocytogenes is the causative agent of listeriosis, a food-borne disease of humans and animals. Typical human exposure occurs through ingestion of unpasteurized milk products, vegetables, or prepared meats. Listeriosis can present in healthy adults with symptoms of fever and gastroenteritis. Pregnant women and their fetuses, newborns and the immunocompromised are at great risk of developing severe infections including meningoencephalitis and septicemia that may be fatal. Infection during pregnancy can lead to fetal loss. Pregnant women or women trying to become pregnant should consult your institute’s occupational health division prior to work with this pathogen. Strains that are on the 10403s background are naturally streptomycin resistant. L. monocytogenes is susceptible to gentamicin, penicillin, and ampicillin and as such listeriosis is treated via administration of gentamicin plus penicillin or ampicillin. Lab acquired transmission could be through an aerosol exposure, a splash to the face causing ingestion or to an open wound or exposed mucous membrane, or a needle stick. No confirmed cases of lab acquired listeriosis have ever been reported. Excessively high levels of L. monocytogenes (~3x1011 cfu via consumption of contaminated food) are required for a healthy human to develop signs of gastroenteritis without any associated mortality (Dalton et al., 1997). L. monocytogenes is classified as a risk group 2 agent and is handled under BSL-2 and ABSL-2 procedures and containment.
Per IATA, we don’t consider that Listeria “is transported in a form that, when exposure to it occurs, is capable of causing permanent disability, life-threatening or fatal disease in otherwise healthy humans or animals.” In this context, an exposure constitutes “when an infectious substance is released outside of the protective packaging, resulting in physical contact with humans.” While it is not exhaustive, L. monocytogenes is also not indicated on the UN 2814 table of pathogens. As such, we ship L. monocytogenes as a UN 3373 designation.
We typically ship L. monocytogenes on Brain Heart Infusion (BHI) agar stabs/plates at room temperature. Colonies usually grow during shipment. If no colonies or growth are visible, place them in a 37°C incubator overnight and check for colonies the next day. We recommend colony purification to generate your stocks and that you confirm (via PCR) that the bacteria you requested was shipped.
• The EGDe strain L. monocytogenes internalin A mutation replaces inlA with inlAS192N-Y369S and expressed at native levels (Wollert et al., Cell, 2007).
• The 10403s strain L. monocytogenes internalin A mutation replaces inlA with inlAS192N-Y369S and made similarly (Xayarath et al., Mol Microbiol, 2009 and Sheridan et al., Immunity, 2013) • It is unknown whether these internalin A mutations make L. monocytogenes more pathogenic in humans. However, it increases the binding kinetics to human E-cad and attachment to Caco-2 cells (Wollert et al., Cell, 2007).
• L. monocytogenes strain EGDe (more pathogenic)
o No antibiotic resistance. Use standard aseptic techniques
• L. monocytogenes strain 10403s (less pathogenic; `expression of ova further reduces pathogenicity) o Naturally streptomycin resistant at 5 ∝g/mL (up to 200 ∝g/mL without impaired growth). o Ova expressing L. monocytogenes is also erythromycin resistant at 5 ∝g/mL.
▪ Ova expression is chromosomally inserted and does not require selection after confirmation.
▪ Our Lm-ova is a truncated Ova that does not express the OT-II epitope
o For quantifying bacterial burden, use plates with strept at 50 – 100 ∝g/mL.
Day -1:
• In the afternoon (or evening) inoculate 5 mL of BHI with 5 ∝L L. monocytogenes from stock aliquots • Culture L. monocytogenes ON at 37°C and 220 rpm
Day 0:
• Subculture the L. monocytogenes in the morning using a 1:10 dilution into BHI. Typically, 2 mL of ON culture into 18 mL of BHI for up to 10 mice. Depending on the size of the experiment you may need a larger culture.
• Shake at 37°C in a 50 mL conical flask at 220 rpm
• Incubate until OD600 reaches 0.8 (roughly 90 – 120 min)
• Pellet L. monocytogenes at 6000 rpm 15 min 4°C (we routinely use 4000 rpm at 15 minute in an eppendorf 5810 R centrifuge)
• 20 mL of L. monocytogenes culture at OD600 = 0.8 yields ~ 2x1010 CFU
• To generate glycerol stocks, resuspend pellet in 2 ml sterile PBS and 2 ml sterile 100% glycerol. Aliquot a few larger volumes (500 ∝l) for permanent stocks (from which future batches will be made) and smaller single use aliquots (25 ∝l) for working stocks. Stocks are maintained at -80°C.
• For i.v. infections in Balb/c or C57Bl/6: Above volumes can be adjusted as i.v. infections require a lot less L. monocytogenes. Resuspend pellet in PBS and serial dilute to appropriate titer. Different doses are reported in the literature, but we typically infect 1-2x103 CFU/mouse in 100 ∝L.
• For oral infections in Balb/c or C57Bl/6: Resuspend pellet in 0.5 mL PBS and infect with 50 ∝L (~2x109 CFU/mouse).
o Most labs gavage for oral infections. We use a feeding approach which prevents esophageal microabrasions and direct access of the bacteria to the blood stream. However, some strains or transgenics may have peculiar eating habits that may require gavage (e.g., CBy)
For Foodborne Infection Protocol
• Remove food and water from the mice cages for infections. Food and water deprive for approximately 4 hours prior to infection. The closer to the evening the better they eat. We also cover mice cages with a dark sheet during feeding, away from noise and traffic flow. It is best if a separate room is available.
• Remove 90% of bedding from infection cages to prevent mice from burying their food. You only need enough bedding to sponge urine.
• Place L. monocytogenes on small bread pieces (~0.5 cm3) in cages. The bread should be the smallest size that still absorbs the entire inoculum. Inoculate 1 piece of bread per cage for a single mouse.
• House mice individually during infection to be sure each mouse consumes a single inoculated bread piece.
• Mice fully consume inoculated bread in about 1 hr. Approximately 10% of mice take longer than 1 hr. We provide a maximum of 4 hours before marking mice which do not fully consume inoculated bread (which is very rare). This allows us to longitudinally track any mouse that did not consume a complete inoculum. Condense mice back into their original cages with their original cagemates so that social hierarchies are not disrupted.
Bug Counts (to confirm infection dose)
• Make 10-fold serial dilutions in PBS.
• Plate 10 ∝L of respective dilutions on BHI agar (with antibiotics where appropriate) using loop spreader. In this case, we have an approximate titer so you can plate the appropriate dilution +/- 1 – 2 dilutions.
Bug Counts from Tissue
• Filter sterilize 1% saponin in PBS
• Mush tissues (usually spleen, mes LN, and liver) through 70um mesh cap
• Spin at 4000rpm 15min 4°C
• Resuspend in 1% saponin: MLN in 2 ml, spleen in 3ml, and liver in 5ml
o Guts: Use gentleMACS to disassociate tissues in 9 parts PBS. After disassociation add 1 part 10% saponin (use lung 2 setting 2X)
• Incubate at least 30 - 60 min at 4°C
• Make 10-fold serial dilutions in PBS.
• Plate 10ul of respective dilutions on BHI agar (with antibiotics where appropriate) using loop spreader. Volume plated and dilution strategy may be adjusted for your needs.

Things to note:

Isofluorane must be checked out from 4th floor cabinet and cannot be left unattended at any point
You MUST change into scrubs before entering BSL2 and after exiting BSL2, must change into clean clothes before re-entering lab spaces (ie you take iso down to locker room with you)
My normal flow:

Drop of cooler outside AHR 249
Go downstairs and change into scrubs
Go up to 4th floor drug cabinet
Check out isofluorane
Go to 249 AHR – put on appropriate PPE over scrubs
After procedure/collecting samples: Leave cooler outside 249 near elevator (take iso with you to locker room)
Change back into clothes
Back up to 4th floor to check iso back in (record amount used)
Back to 2nd floor to retrieve cooler
Back to 220 for processing

ALL LCMV or INFECTIOUS experiments MUST be carried out in a BSC (even after clearance timepoint), if propagating or making stocks must also wear mask

title: 062923 CRISPRCas9 KO in primary T cells for in vivo transfer with Lonza - single guides
text:
CRISPR/Cas9 knock out in primary T cells and in vivo transfer

Materials


Lonza 4D-NucleofectorTM System
P3 primary cell 4D Nucleofector electroporation kit (Lonza, Cat# V4XP-3032 for electroporation wells, Cat# V4SP-4032 for cuvettes)
P3 buffer: make fresh on the day, mix 3.6 μl reagent 1 with 16.4 μl diluent per reaction (Lonza Nucleofector kit) *Though Lonza tech support said it’s good for a month in 4’C.
Recombinant Cas9 protein, 40uM, @ -80’C (Ordered Cas9-NLS purified protein (2.5 mg) from University of California Berkley MacroLab)
20bp gRNAs+80mer scaffold with chemical modification
R10 (RPMI + 10% FCS, glutamine, antibiotics, 50 nM BME, NEAA, HEPES)

Enrich CD8+ T cells – naïve or activated

If naïve, do CD8 enrichment prior to protocol
If activated, activate 24hr prior to this protocol.

CRISPR/Cas9 electroporation

To make a Cas9/RNA complex, mix guides plus tracr RNA as below in PCR tubes:

gRNA thy1 guide only control
gRNA thy1 guide plus guide of 1st target
gRNA thy1 guide plus guide of 2nd target
etc.




want to do 3:1 molar ratio of guide RNA to Cas9 enzyme.
Thy1 AC guide at 100uM concentration.
Experimental guides are at 100uM concentration.
Set up as follows:

Control

3uL thy1 AC crRNA guide from IDT
3uL tracr RNA (Alt-R® CRISPR-Cas9 tracrRNA, ATTO™ 550)

Experimental (x number of groups needed)

1.5uL thy1 AC crRNA guide from IDT



1.5uL guide of experimental guide (Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 crRNA from IDT)
3uL tracr RNA (Alt-R® CRISPR-Cas9 tracrRNA, ATTO™ 550)





Incubate in PCR machine at 95’C for 5 minutes, then immediately remove at put at RT in the dark for 1 hour for annealing.
Add 1.9uL 40uM Cas9 enzyme to each tube (-80’, middle shelf, middle rack). DO NOT MIX. Gently flick the tube to mix sgRNAs with Cas9 and spin down briefly to collect drops from the sides of the tube. Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature for complex formation.
Make a P3 buffer mix below per reaction and keep at room temperature.

1x buffer recipe, make enough for each rxn:

Supplement 1: 3.6uL
P3: 16.4uL


Take 10mL of R10 plus 50U/ml hIL2 (a 1:2000 dilution), and put into a waterbath to warm to 37deg.
Count cells, then spin down cells in large volume of STERILE, RT PBS to remove potential RNase contamination from FCS containing media before electroporation (IMPORTANT). Can do 2-10x10^6 cells per reaction.
Immediately after complex formation, transfer cells into Eppendorf tubes in 1 ml of PBS, and spin down on a tabletop centrifuge at 5000 RPM for 5min room temperature). It is important to prepare everything before resuspending the cells in P3 buffer to minimize the time that cells are exposed to the buffer.
Take supernatant from the cell pellet using pipets (make sure to take off all remaining liquid from cell pellet to not dilute out the small reaction volume of 25 μl). Resuspend cell pellet in 20μl P3 buffer per reaction
Transfer 5 μl of CRISPR/Cas9 RNP into the 20 μl P3 buffer with cells and mix gently.
Transfer the 25 μl cell/RNP mix to the bottom hole of a well of the Lonza nucleofector strip. Be careful to not create any bubbles. (keep time of cells in P3 buffer as short as possible as it is cytotoxic to the cells).
Electroporate cells by putting the nucleofector strip into the Lonza nucleofector and as depicted, start the program

Naïve CD8 T cells: use DN100 program in P3 buffer
Activated CD8 T cells: use DS137 program in P3 buffer

After electroporation (a few seconds) add 130 μl of 37°C pre-warmed R10 media into the well containing electroporated cells and rest cells for 10 minutes in the incubator (5% CO2, 37°C).
Resuspend the cells in the electroporation well using a pipette, and transfer the cell suspension into a fresh tube or well. To recover any remaining cells, wash the electroporation well with an additional 150 μl R10 media by pipetting, and transfer the media into the same collection tube. Add 700 uL pre-warmed R10 to make 1 mL total.
Count the cells with Trypan Blue 20-50% of T cells will be lost during the electroporation step.
For in vivo adoptive transfer, resuspend in PBS at desired concentration and adoptively transfer into recipient mice via intravenous injection. Keep some cells going in culture for future flow and KO validation with flow or Sanger sequencing (if naïve, activate as well).

title: Cloning with HIFI DNA Assembly_KL
text:
Cloning with HIFI DNA Assembly

The principle behind HIFI DNA Assembly is the joining of DNA fragments with ends that share the same sequence (15 – 40bp). There are several good animations on Youtube.
Prep your sequences of interest (Plasmid prep or g-blocks)
If using two plasmids, design primers with overhangs using Snapgene. BE CAREFUL, primers used in the same reaction need to have the same Tm WITHOUT the overhangs. In other words, the difference of Tm between the primers (without the overhangs) has to be max 5C. Use the NEB Tm calculator to calculate the Tm and not Snapgene if you are using the Q5 NEB Master mix for the PCR.
Run the PCR based on the Q5 master mix protocol BUT

-use 1min/kb for the elongation phase
-run the PCR at the Tm of the primers WITHOUT the overhangs

Optional: Add 1ul of DPNI to destroy the substrate for the reaction (because it is methylated). MIX well, incubate at room temperature for 5 min and then at 37C for 60 minutes. (Of note: DPN1 will work in the Q5 PCR buffer or cutsmart buffer. It doesn’t work in water)
Run the product in a gel and isolate the band that corresponds to the right band size. Let the gel run AS LONG AS POSSIBLE to avoid contamination of your band with residual template DNA. Elute with water preferably (to avoid problems with the downstream reaction).
Combine the DNA for the HIFI DNA Assembly reaction. 1:1 vector to insert for a total reaction of 50ng. You don’t have to use 10ul of the Assembly as long as it is 1x (I usually use 5ul of DNA and 5ul of HIFI). Have a mock reaction as a control that you add water instead of HIFI DNA Assembly
Transform two sets of bacteria, one with 2ul of the reaction product and one with 2ul of the DNA from the mock reaction
Next day you should see colonies in the plate with the product and no colonies in the other plate (in reality the majority of the time we see some colonies on the control due to leftover template but the experimental usually has 10x more colonies).
Midi prep a few colonies. Design primers to sequence the new vectors. Send them for sequencing to Genewitz. ALWAYS do this because there are frequent mutations that occur

Prepare protein standard

Use a 96-well flat bottom plate
Add 184 ul H20 to the first well of the first two columns.

Blocking

Staining

stain with primary Ab in TBS-T + 5% BSA over night at 4°C
wash three times
add secondary antibody TBS-T + 5% BSA, incubate for 1 hour at room temperature
wash at least three times

title: 091923 Western blot protocol NES
text:
Developing
I used Amersham™ ECL™ Prime Western Blotting Detection Reagent

Mix solutions A and B at 1:1, if primary ab is strong, can add PBS to dilute
Drain excess wash buffer from the washed membrane and place it protein side up in a suitable box or on a sheet of plastic sheet protecter or other suitable clean surface. Add detection reagent onto the membrane and make sure it completely covers the membrane
Incubate for 45sec at room temperature
Drain off excess detection reagent by holding the membrane edge gently against a tissue

title: Gut prep protocol
text:
IEL and Lamina Propria prep

3 minutes prior to sacrifice, inject mice retro-orbitrally w/ 200 uL antibody mix (15 uL CD8a-APCcy7 + 185 uL PBS)
Sacrifice mice, remove small intestine and spleen, place in ice cold RP5 or CMF, and trim off fat
Place paper towels on desk and wet w/ CMF
Wet gut w/ CMF, cut out Peyer’s patches and clean out the poop
Cut the small intestine in half lengthwise and then cut intestine into small (~1 cm pieces)
Place in flask and wash 2X w/ CMF, pour out contents carefully so no gut comes out
Dump out CMF carefully and replace w/ ~50 mL DTE, place on 37°C stir plate for 30 min
Pour contents into 50 mL conical with cell strainer
Wash out flask 1X w/ DTE and add to 50 mL conical

If preparing lamina propria:

Transfer contents of cell strainer back into flask and add ~30 mL of collagenase solution
Incubate for 45 min at 37° while stirring
Pour contents into 50 mL conical with cell strainer
Wash out flask 1X w/ DTE and add to 50 mL conical

Proceed as follows below for both IEL and lamina propria

Spin at 1600 rpm for 4 min
Make sure you see a pellet, then pour supernatant out and wipe top of conical
Resuspend each sample in 5 mL 44% percoll solution, make sure pellet is well resuspended
Place glass pasteur pipette in conical and add 2 mL 67% percol solution to top of pipette to make a bottom layer. Don’t disturb after adding!
Spin at 21°C at 2000 rpm for 20 min, set acceleration to 4 and brake to 0
Check for an interphase between the two layers and transfer it to 15 mL conical (usually about 3 mL)
Fill to top with PBS then spin at 2000 rpm for 5 min

If interphase remains, take out the top layer, add PBS, and spin again

Resuspend pellet in 250 uL of RP5
Count and stain IEL
Keep on ice and analyze by flow the next day

->store @4<sup>oC in fridge overnight

->store @4<sup>oC in fridge overnight
->DOE: add 77mg Dithioerythritol (CALBIOCHEM #233152)
->DOE: warm to 37 oC in water bath

->keep sterile

DPBS, bring this to 1X too, do not discard

title: 012725 NES - Flow cytometry staining
text:
Flow cytometry staining techniques
Nicole Scharping February 2025
Flow cytometry is an extremely useful technique that can provide you with a LOT of data at once, but it can be complicated. This is a straightforward set of protocols to stain and run samples fairly easily.
Table 1




Analyzer


Lasers


Colors available


Software






BD Fortessa



Blue (488)  Red (621)  Violet (405)


Yellow-green (561)




FITC/488/NBD/BODIPY/GFP/YFP PerCP-Cy5.5 APC/AxF647/660/MitoDR, APC-Cy7, AxF700


Pac Blue/BV421/V450, BV510/Ametrine, BV605, BV650, BV711, BV786


PE/RFP/Cherry, PE-594/MitoOr, PE-Cy7



FACSDiva




Recipes for FAC buffer (for analysis)

500 mL 1X PBS
2% (10 mL) FBS
1:1000 Sodium azide

Basic surface staining (includes Alternative Protocol: Fixation)

Aliquot your cells in a 96-well round or V bottom plate
Add 20-50uL FC block into wells with cells in media, put on ice for minimum 10min (longer is ok)
During the FC block, make up your staining cocktail in FACS Buffer (1XPBS + 2% FCS), make enough for 100uL per well.
Spin the plate down at 2000rpm for 1 min
Flick off the supernatant into the sink. Some like to use a vacuum and suck the individual supernatants off, I never found much utility in this.
Aliquot 100uL into each well as appropriate (you can use a multichannel if there’s a lot of samples). Resuspend up and down with a multichannel pipet. DO NOT reuse tips for multiple rows
Incubate on ice in the dark for 15 minutes.
Add 180 uL of FACS buffer to each well and spin down (this is a wash step).
Resuspend in 100 uL of FACS buffer and move to FACS tubes.
Make single color controls with beads (see protocol below)
Analyze on flow cytometer.


Alternate Protocol: Fixation
If you cannot run the samples immediately (remember, they are still live cells), you can fix them. Paraformaldehyde (4% made up in PBS) is the most common fixation method for flow cytometry. It is fast and works very well, while still preserving cellular structure. Some antigens are lost with PFA fixation.


After the wash step (step 8) spin, resuspend cells instead in 100 uL of 4% PFA in PBS. Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 20 minutes.
Add 180 uL of FACS and spin down.
Resuspend pellet in 100 uL of FACS buffer. Seal the plate with Parafilm around the outside, wrap in foil, and store at 4 deg for up to 7 days (could last longer)
Make single color controls with beads (see protocol below)

Cytoplasmic intracellular staining I (for cytoplasmic proteins)
includes Alternate Protocol: Intracellular Cytokine Staining)
For most intracellular (but non-nuclear) proteins, this protocol will suffice to stain fairly well. As always, though, this is heavily antibody dependent.

Surface stain the cells as normal.
After the wash step, spin down cells at 2000 rpm for 1 min.
First, resuspend cells instead in 100 uL of 4% PFA in PBS. Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 20 minutes. (This step helps preserve certain surface stains like Tim3, as well as ametrine expression in transduced cells)
Add 180 uL of FACS and spin down.
Resuspend cells in 100 uL BD CytoFix/CytoPerm, kept at 4 deg in a brown bottle.
Incubate at RT for 20 min.
Add 180 uL of BD PermWash (10X solution kept at 4 deg in a clear bottle, dilute into ddH20).
Spin down and flick off.
During the spin, make up a staining solution as you would for surface staining (100 uL/well), but make it up in BD PermWash rather than FACS buffer.
Resuspend cells in 100uL of staining solution per well and incubate at RT in the dark for 30 minutes.
Wash with 180 uL of PermWash and spin down.
Resuspend in 100 uL FACS buffer and move to FACS tubes.
Run on analyzers or parafilm the plate, wrap in foil, and store at 4 deg for up to 7 days.
Make single color controls with beads (see protocol below)

Alternate Protocol II: Intracellular cytokine staining
This protocol is used to detect the frequency of cytokine producing cells in a mixed culture, as well as the amount of cytokine produced (by MFI). Cytokines are measured by first stimulating the cells in the presence of a protein transport inhibitor (usually brefeldin A or monensin, which collapse the Golgi or late ER, respectively), then doing cytoplasmic staining using anti-cytokine antibodies. For some cytokines, like TNFa, IL-2, IL-17, and IFN-g, these assays work beautifully. For other cytokines, such as IL-4, -5, -10, and -13, the effects are much less so, relying on shifts of MFI rather than a large shift of cytokine positive cells. Stimulation times, protein transport inhibitor choices, and stimulation type for each of these cytokine should be determined empirically.

Harvest and stimulate your cells

Peptide mix

Plate cells in 96 well round bottom plate, spin down at 2000 RPM for 1 minute
Add 200uL T cell media per well with cells (there must be some APCs in the mix somewhere, purified T cells would not be able to use this method) in the presence 1:500 peptide (GP33 aliquots in Goldrath TC freezer) and 1:500 Protein Transport Inhibitor (mixture of brefeldin A and monensin)
Resuspend using multichannel
Stim for 4hr at 37deg (in incubator)


Surface stain your cells according to Basic Protocol.
Fix/perm the cells and stain your cytokine by the intracellular cytoplasmic protocol.
Resuspend in FACS buffer and analyze, or store at 4 deg in the dark for up to 3 days.
Make single color controls with beads (see protocol below)

Nuclear intracellular staining
This protocol allows for identification of cells based on their expression of transcription factors and other nuclear proteins. The staining reagents used to accomplish this, however, are very harsh, and can dramatically changing forward/side scatter profiles and potentially hiding some antigens. In addition, fluorescent proteins used in reporter constructs will leech out, deadening their signal. Including a 4% PFA fix before the nuclear fix helps decrease this effect.

Stain cells as in Basic Surface staining protocol.
After the wash step, spin down at 2000rpm for 1 minute.
First, resuspend cells instead in 100 uL of 4% PFA in PBS. Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 20 minutes. (This step helps preserve certain surface stains like Tim3, as well as ametrine expression in transduced cells)
Add 180 uL of FACS and spin down.
During the spin, dilute 1 part eBioscience Fix/Perm Concentrate into 3 parts Fix/Perm Diluent. Make enough for 100 uL per well.
Resuspend cells in 100uL of Fix/Perm and incubate 20 min at RT in the dark.
During the incubation, make up your nuclear stain (in the Perm Buffer), enough for 100uL per well.
After 20min, for the wash, add 180 uL of eBioscience 1x Perm buffer (diluted to 1x ddH2O) and spin down.
Resuspend cells in 100 uL staining buffer and incubate for 30 m RT in the dark.
Add 180 uL of Perm buffer and spin down.
Resuspend in 100 uL FACS buffer and move to tubes.
Analyze immediately or parafilm seal, wrap in foil, and store for 3-5 d at 4 deg.
Make single color controls with beads (see protocol below)

Single color controls
For single color controls, I use OneComp eBeads™ Compensation Beads. The beads include positive and negative population for each sample, as only ~half of the beads bind antibody (therefore the other half is your negative control). This only works for using antibodies from mouse or rat sources (rabbit antibodies or dyes do not work here). For flow on the Fortessa X20, something like FITC vs A488 are interchangeable. On a spectral cytometer, this would not be the case.

Vortex beads, then add one drop per tube. Make enough tubes for each fluorophore ‘color’ you have. If you have a reporter or dye than cannot be used as beads, still make a tube for these colors.
Add 1uL of antibody for the appropriate single color per tube. For tubes representing reporter or dye, pick an antibody with a fluorophore that would be read out in the same channel and add to tube. Vortex to mix.
Let single color control tubes sit in the dark at RT for at least 10min.
After incubation, add 200uL FACS buffer per tube. THERE IS NO WASH STEP. Samples are now ready to run.
