title: BTSSR viable Lymphocyte collection protocol 10222014
text:
PURPOSE:



To define a standard operating procedure for optimal fluid tissue (Blood) acquisition and for maintaining the quality of the fluid tissue (Blood) for the Biorepository Tissue Technology Shared Resources (BTTSR) of the UCSD Moores Cancer Center.





POLICY:



Policy on standard operating procedure for Peripheral Blood Leukocytes for Biorepository Tissue Technology Shared Resource.




WORKPLACE SAFETY:
Proper precautions on exposure to fluid tissue (blood) specimens, on handling tissue specimens, hazardous chemicals and biohazard as well as infectious waste by using the required Personal Protective Equipment when appropriate:
Eyewear
Mask
Apron
Gloves
Laboratory Gown
Proper hand washing: Hand washing should be done as often as possible especially after removing gloves and before handling food and before touching any clean surface. Hands should be washed with soap and warm water for at least 20 seconds.
Injury at work: Any injury must be reported to the appropriate staff or Project investigator within 24 hours to complete and sign an incident report.


Materials and/Supplies:

BD Vacutainer sodium Heparin blood collection tube
P-1000 pipetman
P-200 pipetman
P-1000,P-200 filter tips
Tube racks
10 ml serological pipets
5 ml serological pipets
Pipet man
Pre labeled 2.0 ml Cryovials
15 ml conicals
50ml conical
Eppendorf tube
Centrifuge
Density Gradient medium
Sterile disposable towels
Sterile gloves
Marking pens or pencils
Styrofoam containers
Chipped ice
-80 Freezer
LN2 freezer

Tissue Acquisition Policy

Fluid tissue (blood) acquisition are directed to the following:

Dr. Vandenberg – UCSD, Professor of Pathology and Director of Neuropathology. Director of Biorepository Tissue Technology Shared Resource of UCSD Moores Cancer Center 858-822-7661
Under our approved IRB protocol 090401 for human subject research
svandenberg@ucsd.edu
http://cancer.ucsd.edu
ccbr@ad.ucsd.edu
http://cancer.ucsd.edu/research-training/shared-resources/biorepository/Pages/default.aspx


Fluid tissue Collection (blood)

The patient must be consented on the IRB approved protocol. Plan and consent.
The consenting is performed by the research coordinator or the research associate.
Once the patient is consented the research coordinator or the research associate follow up for lab appointment and Phlebotomist collects blood 20 ml in sodium heparin blood collection tube
The research coordinator or the research associate will collect donor’s demographic data and Doctor’s details.
Confirm patient’s diagnosis and medical information from EPIC
De identified patient ID and assign Project Id # number.


Fluid Tissue Processing


Collection of Peripheral Blood Leukocytes from Venipuncture

Collect blood via venipuncture into sodium heparin blood collection (green top) tubes.
Warm density gradient medium (ie. Lymphoprep), dilution/wash medium (ie. DPBS or HBSS) and centrifuge to room temperature.
Aliquot 4 ml of room temperature density gradient medium into sterile 15 ml conical tubes (plan 2 tubes for each 10 ml tube of blood collected).
Wipe the outside of the blood collection tubes with 70% ethanol.
Carefully remove the caps from the blood collection tubes.
Decant blood into sterile 50 ml conical tube.
Add 8 ml of sterile room temperature wash medium to each blood collection tube.
Using a 10 ml pipette, transfer wash medium from blood collection tubes to 50 ml conical tube containing blood (approximately 1:1 dilution).
Mix diluted blood by inverting 50 ml conical tube 2-3 times.
Using a 10 ml pipette, carefully transfer 8-10 ml of diluted blood to each 15 ml conical tube containing density gradient medium. Deliver the diluted blood slowly to the top of the density gradient medium, being careful to not disrupt the medium/blood interface.
Centrifuge density gradient medium/blood at 1200 x g for 20 minutes at 20oC.
Remove tubes from centrifuge taking care to not disrupt the density medium/plasma interface. There will be multiple layers- red blood cells will be at the bottom of the tube below the density gradient medium, the density gradient medium will be above that, a thin layer of leukocytes (buffy coat) will sit atop the density gradient medium, and the diluted plasma will be the top layer.
Using a 5 ml pipette, collect the leukocytes from atop the density gradient medium. Transfer to a new sterile 50 ml tube. Combine leukocytes from all tubes from the same sample.
Add sterile wash buffer to final volume of 40 ml. Recover cells by centrifugation at 600 x g for 5 minutes at 4oC. Repeat 2x. Count cells.
Re-suspend cell pellet in ice cold heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum, 500 μl/starting tube of blood. Place on ice.
Using a 5 ml pipette and keeping the cells on ice, add freezing medium (ice cold FBS + 20% DMSO) dropwise with constant swirling to 1:1 dilution.
Aliquot cells into 3 cryovials. Place in -80oC freezer. Cells can be transferred to liquid nitrogen after 24 hours.

title: IF_Frozen_BioProtocol
text:
Download the original PDF

IF_Frozen_BioProtocol
                                     http://www.bio-protocol.org/e163   Vol 1, Iss 24, Dec 20, 2011



                       Immunofluorescence on Frozen Tissue Sections
                                              Jason Reuter
[Abstract] Immunofluorescence is commonly used to determine the cellular or tissue localization of a protein of interest. Immunofluorescence can also be used as a qualitative measure of protein expression.
Materials and Reagents
1. Primary antibody
2. Alexa fluor secondary antibodies (Life Technologies, Invitrogen™)
3. Horse serum (Santa Cruz Biotechnology, catalog number: sc-2483)
4. Hoechst 33342 nuclear dye (Life Technologies, Invitrogen™, catalog number: H1399)
5. ProLong gold antifade mounting reagent (Life Technologies, Invitrogen™, catalog
     number: P36934)
6. PAP pen (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: Z377821)
7. Nail polish (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number: 50-949-071)
8. 100% ice cold acetone
9. Phosphate buffered saline (PBS)
10. Formaldehyde
11. Methanol
12. Triton X-100
Equipment
1. -20 °C freezer
2. Humidified chamber
Procedure
1. Remove 7 μm cryosections from the freezer and immediately place them into ice-cold
     acetone for 10 min.
     Note: The optimal fixation conditions depend upon the antigen and the primary antibody
     used. Formaldehyde, acetone and methanol are all common fixatives.
2. Wash slides in PBS and aspirate around the tissue until the slide, not the tissue, is dry.
     Carefully, trace around the tissue with a PAP pen.
Copyright © 2011 The Authors; exclusive licensee Bio-protocol LLC. 1
                                     http://www.bio-protocol.org/e163   Vol 1, Iss 24, Dec 20, 2011

3. Block for 1 h at room temperature (RT) with 10% horse serum in PBS with 0.05% Triton
     X-100.
4. Aspirate blocking buffer and incubate sections in a humidified camber with primary
     antibody, diluted in 2% horse serum in PBS with 0.05% Triton X-100, for 1 h at RT. Use
     enough antibody solution to completely submerge the section, about 150 μl.
     Note: Follow manufactures recommendation for antibody dilution.
5. Aspirate primary antibody and wash in 150 μl of PBS/Triton X-100 buffer 5 times.
6. Incubate sections in a humidified chamber with corresponding secondary Alexa
     Fluor488/555 antibody for 1 h at RT. Dilute secondary in 2% horse serum in PBS with
     0.05% Triton X-100, using a 1:300 ratio. Use enough antibody solution to completely
     submerge the section, about 150 μl.
7. Aspirate secondary antibody and wash in 150 μl of PBS/Triton X-100 buffer 2 times.
8. Wash sections in 150 μl of PBS buffer 3 times.
9. Incubate sections for 2 min in Hoechst 33342 nuclear dye [2 mg/ml in PBS].
10. Aspirate secondary antibody and wash in 150 μl of PBS buffer 3 times.
11. Allow sections to dry, add ~2 drops of ProLong gold antifade reagent to each section and
     place a cover slip over section.
     Note: Be careful to avoid damaging the tissue by sliding the cover slip too much and do
     not introduce bubbles. Aspirate excess reagent.
12. Dry sections at RT for several hours or overnight protected from light. Once the slides are
     completely dry, seal the edges of the cover slip with clear nail polish. Slides can be
     stored at -20 °C, protected from light for several weeks.

text:
Ex vivo peptide re-stimulation to assess cytokine production by antigen-specific CD8 T cells
LLB 2020

Whole splenocytes (whole blood or tissue) - maximum concentration of 1x10^7 cells/ml (I plate 2x10^6 cells in 200ul). Doing a higher concentration won’t work.
Re-suspend cells in:

TCM + 1ug/ml of GP33-41 peptide + GolgiPlug (1:1000) + 1:100 of anti-CD107a (conjugated to your preferred fluorophore) and incubate at 37C for 5h.
Make the negative control (no peptide) by pooling a little bit of cells from all samples: TCM + 1ug/ml Brefeldin A + 1:100 of anti-CD107a

After 5h;

Spin down flick to remove supernatant
Stain with live/dead stain + anti-CD8 (and congenic markers etc) in PBS1x for 10-15min at RT.
Wash and re-suspend in Cytofix/Cytoperm (BD kit) 20 min @4C (in the fridge).

Wash off fix, and resuspend in FACS buffer. *Cells can be left in the fridge overnight (or for 2-3 days until acquisition).
On the day of acquisition, spin down and remove PBS/facs buffer.
Re-suspend cells in Perm Buffer 1X (eBioscience kit/FoxP3 kit) containing:

anti-IFNg (1/100)
anti-TNFa (1/100)
anti-IL-2 (1/100) – PE (*Important: IL-2 only works in PE)

Stain for 30min at 4C
Wash off stain, and re-suspend in volume for acquisition

Preparing Cells and RNP mix

Cultivate the required number of cells (see table below for cell amount) such that the cells are 70–90% confluent on the day of the experiment.
Rehydrate the sgRNA stock like this: 3 nmol of sgRNA powder plus 30 ul TE buffer. This will give you a 100 uM (100 pmol/ul) sgRNA stock solution (store at -80C).
Dilute sgRNA like this: 6 ul of 100 uM sgRNA stock plus 14 ul nuclease-free water.
Prepare plates by filling the wells with the appropriate volume of culture medium containing serum and supplements without antibiotics as described in the table below and pre-incubate plates at 37°C in a humidified 5% CO2 incubator.
Prepare this mix:



1.3 ul of diluted sgRNA guide (30 uM)
1 ul TrueCut Cas9 6 uM or 1 ul
12.4 ul Buffer R Incubate this mix for 20 minutes at RT



During those 20 min, prepare a suspension with your cells (50,000-150000 cells, depending on your cells (10 to 20 million cells/ml) in an Eppendorf, and prepare electroporator.
Wash cells once with PBS1x and once with Buffer R.
Resuspend the pellet in 10/100 ul of the CRISPR/Cas9 MIX
Proceed to Electroporation

Electroporation

Fill the NeonTube with 3 mL Electrolytic Buffer (use Buffer E for 10 μL NeonTip and Buffer E2 for 100 μL NeonTip).
Insert the NeonTube into the NeonPipette Station until you hear a click sound (Figure 1).
Transfer the appropriate amount of plasmid DNA/siRNA into a sterile, 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add cells to the tube containing plasmid DNA/siRNA and gently mix. See the table on back side for cell number, DNA/siRNA amount, and plating volumes to use.
Press the push-button on the NeonPipette to the second stop to open the clamp and insert the top-head of the NeonPipette into the NeonTip until the clamp fully picks up the mounting stem of the piston. Gently release the push-button, continuing to apply a downward pressure on the pipette, ensuring that the tip is sealed onto the pipette without any gaps (Figure 2A and B).
Press the push-button on the NeonPipette to the first stop and immerse the NeonTip into the cell-DNA/siRNA mixture. Slowly release the push-button on the pipette to aspirate the cell-DNA/siRNA mixture into the NeonTip.


Note: Avoid air bubbles during pipetting as air bubbles cause arcing during electroporation. If you notice air bubbles in the tip, discard the sample and carefully aspirate fresh sample into the tip again without any air bubbles.


Insert the NeonPipette with the sample vertically into the NeonTube placed in the NeonPipette Station until you hear a click sound.
Ensure that you have selected the appropriate electroporation protocol and press Start on the touchscreen (Figure 5).
The Neondevice automatically checks for the proper insertion of the NeonTube and NeonPipette before delivering the electric pulse.
The touchscreen displays Complete to indicate that the electroporation is complete.
Remove the NeonPipette from the NeonPipette Station and immediately transfer the samples from the NeonTip by pressing the push-button on the pipette to the first stop into the prepared culture plate containing prewarm medium with serum and supplements but without antibiotics (Figure 6).


Discard the NeonTip into an appropriate biological hazardous waste container.


Repeat Steps 5–11 for the remaining samples.


Change the NeonTips after using it twice and NeonTubes after 10 usages. Use a new NeonTip and NeonTube for each new plasmid DNA/siRNA or cell type.


Gently rock the plate to assure even distribution of the cells. Incubate the plate at 37°C in a humidified CO2 incubator.
If you are not using the Neondevice, turn the power switch on the rear to OFF.
Assay samples to determine the transfection efficiency (e.g., fluorescence microscopy or functional assay) or gene knockdown (for siRNA).
Based on your initial results, you may need to optimize the electroporation parameters for your cell type. Refer to the manual for using the 18-well or preprogrammed, 24-well optimization protocol on the Neondevice.

Checking the cleavage efficiency

Resuspend the pellet in 20 ul of 1x ThermoPol (New England BioLabs B9004S) in an eppendorf. Lyse at 95C for 10 min.
Cool the lysate at 4C (in ice) during 5 min.
Add 2.5 ul of Proteinase K 20 mg/ml and incubate at 55 C for 1 hr.
Inactivate proteinase K incubating 15 min at 95C.
Cool the lysate at 4C (in ice) for at least 5 min.
Use the AmpliTaq Gold 360 master mix kit from Life Technologies (REF 43988881, -20C, CRISPR box) to set up the PCR with the designed primers for each CRISPR.

Mix
AmpliGold 2x 25 ul
sgDNA 2 ul
Primers (10 uM F/R) 1 ul
DDW 22 ul
Program:
1. 95C 10 min
2. 95C 30 sec
3. 56C 30 sec
4. 72C 60 sec/per kb (30 sec for an amplicon of 500 bp)
Go 4 to 2, 40 cycles
5. 72C, 7 min
6. 4C, forever

Run 5 ul in a gel. You should see one single band at around 500 bp.
Use the GeneArt Genomic Cleavage Detection kit (Life Technologies Cat A24372) to digest your PCR product:
Combine in 2 different 8-well strip tubes (one will – and the other will be +)

Mix
PCR product 3 ul
10x Detection Reaction Buffer
1 ul DDW 5 ul
Program:
1. 95C 5 min
2. 95C-85C -2C/ sec
3. 85C-25C -0.1C/sec
4. 4C, forever

Following the completion of the re-annealing, proceed to enzyme digestion or store the reaction at -20C. Add 1 ul of Detection Enzyme to the test sample (+), mix well. Add 1 ul of DDW to the test sample (-), mix well.
Incubate at 37C for 1 hr.
Vortex briefly and spin down.
Place at 4C.
Immediately load the entire 10 ul on a 2% gel.

title: Virus production in 10 cm - PlatE
text:
Virus production in 10 cm-dish
Day 0: plate 2.5x106 PlatE (or PhoenixE) cells in a 10 cm dish (total volume 8ml) in DMEM complete media without P/S
Day 1: transfection with MIRUS TRANS-LT1 (MIR 2300)
Just before transfection, change the medium adding 12 ml of fresh new media and move the cells back to the incubator
In a 14-ml tube, add in this order

DNA: 10 ug transfer vector + 5ug pCL-Eco
OPTIMEM serum-dree medium to .4 ml total volume, mix well by pipetting and swirl the tube;
Add MIRUS reagent to DNA (3 to 6 ug of MIRUS/ug of DNA). Dispense MIRUS directly into the liquid, dropwise.
Swirl the tube, do not pipette or vortex
Let it stand at RT for 20 to 30 min
Gently add the DNA/OPTIMEM/Mirus complex to the cells, dropwise, in a circular motion.
Put the plate back in the incubator (5% CO2)
16hs after transfection, gently remove the medium and replace with 10 ml fresh medium for virus collection.
Collect the virus at 24 and 48h, store virus in the fridge and pool the fractions at the end; at the end, filter virus through a 0.45 um filter (do not use 0.2).
Store in the fridge and use virus within 24h
Store at -80C long term. Avoid freeze-thawing

Prewarm at RT optimum and MIRUS prior to using

- Harvest kidneys and Lungs and place in PBS 5% FBS or complete media and on ice
Kidneys:
- Make one cut with scissors to increase their surface area and cut 2x with tissue chopper (tissue shouldn’t be dry under chopper!)
- Transfer cut kidneys into pyrex conical containing a magnetic stirr bar and add 25ml of enzyme media (complete RPMI+0.5mg/ml Collagenase D)
- Stirr for 45min at 37C
- Filter through 70um cell strainer and mash with syringe plunger. Spin down, remove supernatant and re-suspend pellet in 5ml 44% Percoll** (transfer into 15ml round-bottom Falcon conical). 
- With a pasteur pipette go all the way to the bottom of the tube and slowly add 2.5ml of 67% Percoll
- Carefully place inside centrifuge and spin down at 2000rpm for 20min at 25C (NO brake!). 
- Collect interphase and place in 15ml conical. Fill up tube up to 15ml with RPMI5% FBS and spin down for 8min at 2000rpm.
- Remove supernatant and re-suspend pellet in suitable volume (1ml of complete RPMI) for counting.
- Proceed with counting/staining
** To make 100% Percoll: mix 9 parts of Percoll stock with 1 part of 10X PBS.
   - To make 44% or 67% Percoll, use 100% Percoll as explained above and dilute in PBS+5%FBS
Lungs:
- Cut x2 w tissue chopper and place in 25ml of enzyme media (complete RPMI+0.5mg/ml Collagenase D) in pyrex conical + stirr bar
- Stirr for 45min at 37C
- Filter through 70um cell strainer and mash with syringe plunger. Spin down, remove supernatant and re-suspend in 2ml ACK lysis buffer. Incubate at RT for 5min.
- Wash and spin down
- Re-suspend in counting volume (2ml). Count and continue with staining. 
Liver:
- Cut liver with tissue chopper
- Press through 70um cell strainer
- Re-suspend in 20ml cold PBS/3% FBS
- Spin for 7min at 1500 rpm, remove SNT, re-suspend in 20ml (wash x3 times)
- Spin again, remove SNT, re-suspend
- Spin again (last time)
- Re-suspend in Isotonic Percoll (34% final). 
    Per liver use 25ml of isotonic percoll.
    To make 100ml (4 livers) —>     62.5ml PBS1x
                                                      3.75ml PBS 10x
                                                      33.75ml Percoll
    *Make at RT. Use 25ml per liver
- Spin at 1750rpm for 12min at RT. Brake ON. 
- Harvest pellet (RBC + lymphocytes), aspirate fat and everything else. With vaccum! Pellet is very loose
- Wash in 10ml Facs buffer
- Re-suspend in ACK, leave for 4-5min
- Filter through mesh
- Count and stain

title: Gut prep protocol
text:
IEL and Lamina Propria prep

3 minutes prior to sacrifice, inject mice retro-orbitrally w/ 200 uL antibody mix (15 uL CD8a-APCcy7 + 185 uL PBS)
Sacrifice mice, remove small intestine and spleen, place in ice cold RP5 or CMF, and trim off fat
Place paper towels on desk and wet w/ CMF
Wet gut w/ CMF, cut out Peyer’s patches and clean out the poop
Cut the small intestine in half lengthwise and then cut intestine into small (~1 cm pieces)
Place in flask and wash 2X w/ CMF, pour out contents carefully so no gut comes out
Dump out CMF carefully and replace w/ ~50 mL DTE, place on 37°C stir plate for 30 min
Pour contents into 50 mL conical with cell strainer
Wash out flask 1X w/ DTE and add to 50 mL conical

If preparing lamina propria:

Transfer contents of cell strainer back into flask and add ~30 mL of collagenase solution
Incubate for 45 min at 37° while stirring
Pour contents into 50 mL conical with cell strainer
Wash out flask 1X w/ DTE and add to 50 mL conical

Proceed as follows below for both IEL and lamina propria

Spin at 1600 rpm for 4 min
Make sure you see a pellet, then pour supernatant out and wipe top of conical
Resuspend each sample in 5 mL 44% percoll solution, make sure pellet is well resuspended
Place glass pasteur pipette in conical and add 2 mL 67% percol solution to top of pipette to make a bottom layer. Don’t disturb after adding!
Spin at 21°C at 2000 rpm for 20 min, set acceleration to 4 and brake to 0
Check for an interphase between the two layers and transfer it to 15 mL conical (usually about 3 mL)
Fill to top with PBS then spin at 2000 rpm for 5 min

If interphase remains, take out the top layer, add PBS, and spin again

Resuspend pellet in 250 uL of RP5
Count and stain IEL
Keep on ice and analyze by flow the next day

title: Caecum_orthotopic_protocol_MRC
text:
Orthotopic Implantation of MC38-gp33 cells into the Caecum of Bl6 mice
Mouse colon cancer cells (e.g., MC-38 cells) will be grown to confluence using standard aseptic cell culture technique, harvested for injection, and resuspended in serum-free DMEM at a concentration of 4 x 10^7 cells/mL – Inject 200K cells in 20 ul serum-free DMEM.
Cecum injection:

After induction of anesthesia, under sterile conditions (sterile instruments, surgical PPE per policy), the middle abdomen will be shaved with an electric razor, and scrubbed with Betadine, after which the surgical site is wiped with 70% ethanol, and re-painted with Betadine.
The animal is then draped appropriately, and using sterile gloves and instruments, a middle abdominal incision will be made

1. 31G needle will be used to inject 20μl of cell suspension (up to 2x10^5 cells resuspended in serum-free DMEM) into the cecum wall between the mucosa and the muscularis layers under a binocular lens (23 magnification), with an approximate 30° angle and its tip introduced 5 mm into the cecal wall. The delivery of tumor cells will occur within the subserosa. Alternatively, 2-10 mm3 tumor pieces derived from subcutanous tumors will be sutured to the caecum wall using 3-0 Vicryl.\

Slight pressure with a cotton stick will be done at 32 mm from the injection point in the direction of the pipette axis. The pipette is pulled out and clean the area around the injection with 3% iodine to avoid seeding of unlikely refluxed tumor cells into the abdominal cavity. Any potential bleeding will be controlled by using a cotton swab.
The wound will be closed in two layers, with running 4-0 Vicryl, and nylon or polypropylene sutures for the skin. Mice will be monitored for anesthesia withdrawal as well as an increase or change in respiratory rate and/or pattern. The length of anesthesia will be approximately 20 minutes so the variance from normothermic conditions should be minimal. A heat lamp will be used if the mice do not begin to recover and move after 20 minutes of anesthesia. Care will be taken to ensure the mice do not overheat by keeping the lamp far enough away that it is comfortable for surgeon’s hands to rest there.
Respiratory rate and depth will be monitored until mouse is able to right itself after mouse is subject to surgery. The animal is then placed back into its cage, observed until fully recovered from anesthesia, and returned to its rack.

After 2w, I could get around 20-30mm3 volume tumors.

title: NES 070515 Immunofluorescence staining protocol
text:
Cut blocks of tissue to obtain spleen, lymph node, and tumor sections. Cryostat should be set to -20 degrees C, sections at 7um thickness

If getting tissue fracturing, adjust temperature [try warmer] and thickness of section
Can also try very briefly warming surface of OCT block by rubbing it with your thumb to decrease tissue fracturing

Fix slides in -20° acetone for 20 minutes at -20° (put back into freezer). Blot excess acetone off edges by pressing into a paper towel, and let air dry for 10 minutes (or until visibly dry). At this point you can store slides at -80° indefinitely (make sure slides stay dry).
To stain, let slides come up to room temperature, then draw a circle around tissue with a hydrophobic pen. Allow at least 10 minutes for hydrophobic line to dry.
Rehydrate tissue with staining buffer by adding ~200uL buffer to each tissue circle. Let sit at RT for 30 minutes. Make the staining buffer as follows:


Staining Buffer
100ml 1x PBS
1ml (1%) normal rat serum (as needed by antibody isotype)
1ml (1%) normal mouse serum (as needed by antibody isotype)
1g (1%) BSA
100ul (0.1%) Tween-20


Use aspirator to remove staining buffer, then blot with a kim wipe to get slide as dry as possible, making sure to not touch the tissue.
Aliquot primary antibodies (diluted in ~100ul staining buffer), and incubate in humidity chamber (foil-covered baking tray lined with damp paper towels) for 30 minutes at RT.
Wash slides first with a stream of PBS (using a transfer pipette) to get rid of excess antibody, then place slides in staining buffer and set on rotator to wash for 10 minutes. Gently blot next to sample area to remove excess liquid. If there is still excess liquid, it can be removed via aspiration. Renew the hydrophobic line if necessary (if staining with different secondaries on the same slide). Aliquot secondary antibodies (diluted in ~100ul staining buffer) and stain for 30 minutes at RT.
Wash slides again as previously, the counterstain with DAPI. DAPI stock is frozen at -20 at 5mg/ml stock concentration. To make a long-term working solution, dilute 50ul stock 1:50 in PBS (this solution can be stored in fridge for up to 6 months). Stain tissue with working solution for ~1minute.
Mount samples using prolong diamond anti-fade mounting media (add 3 evenly-spaced drops of mounting media to the coverslip, then place the coverslip on the slide). Let the mounting media cure for 24 hours (or at least overnight) at room temperature, protected from light.
Slides should be viewed with fluorescent microscope ASAP. For long term storage of stained slides, place them wrapped in foil at -80°.

title: fixation_permeabilization
text:
Download the original PDF

fixation_permeabilization
FIXATION AND PERMEABILIZATION IN IHC/ICC FIXATION: Fixation should immobilize antigens while retaining cellular and subcellular structure. It should also allow for access of antibodies to all cells and subcellular compartments. The fixation and permeablisation method used will depend on the sensitivity of the epitope and antibody themselves, and may require some optimization.
Fixation can be done using crosslinking reagents, such as paraformaldehyde. These are better at preserving cell structure, but may reduce the antigenicity of some cell components as the crosslinking will obstruct antibody binding. For this reason, antigen retrieval techniques may be required, particularly if there is a long fixation incubation or if a high percentage of crosslinking fixative is used. Another option is to use organic solvents. These remove lipids while dehydrating the cells. They also precipitate proteins on the cellular architecture.

4% Paraformaldehyde

Add 4% paraformaldehye to slides for 10 minutes only. Rinse with PBS or PBS 1% BSA
Note: Fixing in paraformaldehyde for more than 10-15 minutes will cross link the proteins to the point where antigen retrieval may be required to ensure the antibody has free access to bind and detect the protein.

Ethanol

Add 100-200ul per slide of cooled 95% ethanol, 5% glacial acetic acid for 5-10 minutes. Wash with PBS or PBS 1% BSA

Methanol

Add 100-200ul per slide of ice cold methanol. Place at -20oC for 10 minutes. Wash with PBS or PBS 1% BSA
Note: methanol will also permeabilize, but not in all cases as some epitopes are very sensitive to this. Can try acetone instead for permeabilization if required.

Acetone

Add 100-200ul per slide ice cold acetone. Place at -20oC for 5 to 10 minutes. Wash with PBS or PBS 1% BSA
Note: acetone will also permeabilize, no permeabilization step required.
PERMEABILIZATION Permeabilization should only be required for intracellular epitopes when the antibody required access to the inside of the cell to detect the protein. However, it will also be required for detection of transmembrane membrane proteins if the epitope is in the cytoplasmic region.
Solvents:

Acetone fixation will also permeabilize

www.abcam.com/technical

Methanol fixation can be used to permeablize but is not always suitable.

These reagents can be used to fix and permebilize, or can be used after fixation with a crosslinking agent such as paraformaldehyde to permeabilize the cells.
Detergents:

Triton or NP-40

Use 0.1 to 0.2% in PBS, 10 minutes only.
These will also partially dissolve the nuclear membrane and are therefore very suitable for nuclear antigen staining.
Note: as these are harsh detergents, they will disrupt proteins if they are used at higher concentrations or for longer amounts of time which will affect staining results.

Tween 20, Saponin, Digitonin and Leucoperm

Use 0.2 to 0.5% for 10 to 30 minutes.
These are much milder membrane solubilizers. They will give large enough pores for antibodies to go through without dissolving plasma membrane. Suitable for antigens in the cytoplasm or the cytoplasmic face of the plasma membrane. Also suitable for soluble nuclear antigens.
SPECIAL RECOMMENDATIONS:
Cytoskeletal, viral and some enzyme antigens usually give optimal results when fixed with acetone, ethanol or formaldehyde (high conc).
Antigens in cytomplasmic organelles and granules will require a fixation and permeabilization method depending on the antigen. The epitope needs to remain accessible.

text:
RNA Isolation from Sorted Cells
and
cDNA preparation

Sort ~50K cells of interest into 500 ul of Trizol. Careful not to dilute Trizol too much – Sort into media, spin down and resuspend in Trizol if necessary.
Extracted cells in Trizol can be kept at -80C.
Thaw Trizol:cells @ RT
Add 100 ul chloroform.
Vortex 15 seconds.
Incubate 2-3 minutes at RT.
Centrifuge 15 min at 12000 g at 4C – Work on ice from now on.
Transfer aqueous phase to new clean tube ~250 ul (if 500 ul were used).
Add 1ul glycoblue.
Add 300 ul isopropanol.
Incubate at -80C for at least 1h.
Centrifuge 20 min at highest speed 4C.
Remove supernatant.
Wash with 500 ul 75% ethanol (cold).
Centrifuge 15 min at 7400g 4C.
Remove ethanol and air dry (10 min).
Resuspend in 20 ul water.

Remove DNA contamination

Add 2ul of 10X TURBO DNase Buffer and 1ul TURBO DNase to 20 ul of RNA, and mix gently
Incubate at 37C for 20-30 min
Add resuspended Inactivation Reagent (2ul to 23 ul mix), and mix well
Incubate 5 min at RT, mixing occasionally
Centrifuge at 10000g for 1.5 min and transfer the RNA to a fresh tube

cDNA preparation – Assuming RNA comes from same amount of cells
Quantify with Qubit/Nanodrop

Use kit (pink box @ -20C): Mix 8 ul RNA, 1ul dNTP, 1ul random hexamer (50 ng/ul).
Incubate at 65C for 5min.
Prepare 2X reaction mix in order – Make MasterMix

10x RT buffer – 2 ul
25 mM MgCl2 – 4 ul
0.1 M DTT – 2 ul
RNase out – 1ul

Add 2X reaction to RNA.
Incubate at RT for 2 minutes.
Add 1ul superscript II to each tube.
PCR program:

RT 10 min
42C 50 min
70 15 min

Chill on ice.
Add 1 ul RNAse H and incubate 37C 20 min.

title: insitu_tetramer_CD8_Tcells
text:
PROTOCOL
1. Day 1: Fresh Tissue Sectioning and Primary Incubation

Use a scalpel to cut fresh tissue into small (approximately 0.5 cm wide by 0.5 cm tall) pieces. Separately glue each tissue to a plunger and embed them with 3 - 5 mL of 4% low-melt agarose in PBS. Label the plunger with the tissue information using a sticker. Put it in a chilled holder in an ice bucket to solidify.
Turn on the microtome and set the thickness of the sections to 200 µm. Install a razor blade on the microtome and insert the plunger mounted with tissue in the microtome bath.
Prepare phosphate-buffered saline with heparin (PBS-H) by adding 100 µg/mL or 18.7 U/mL heparin to PBS to preserve the RNA and to permit potential ISH applications downstream. Fill the microtome bath, covering the embedded tissue, with 100 - 120 mL of chilled, sterile PBS-H. Add PBS-H ice cubes to the bath to maintain the temperature at 0 - 2 °C. Start the microtome and cut the tissue into 200 µm sections.
Note: It is important to keep the tissues chilled on ice to minimize cellular activity within the tissues and because fresh tissue is easier to section when it is chilled. PBS alone can be used if there are no plans for downstream ISH.
ALTERNATIVELY: Use hand-held microtome
Alternatively, for tissues that do not cut well with a microtome (e.g., gut and lung), use a scalpel or razor blade to cut the tissue into thin strips as close as possible to 200 µm.
Label the lid of 24-well tissue culture plates with the experimental sample information and place the tissue chambers in the corresponding wells. Use a paintbrush to transfer the sections to a tissue chamber set in the well of a 24-well tissue culture plate containing 1 mL of chilled PBS-H.

NOTE: Reusable tissue chambers should be made prior to initiating staining. Tissue chambers can be made using a 14 mL polypropylene round-bottom snap-cap tube and wire mesh. Use a sharp razor blade to cut the bottom of a 14 mL polypropylene round-bottom snap-cap tube off. Cut the wire mesh in a circle to fit the hole at the bottom of the tube. Heat the wire mesh circle using a Bunsen burner until it is red-hot. Set the wire mesh circle down very quickly and push the tube onto the mesh. Check that the wire mesh is securely attached to the bottom of the tube and then carefully cut off the top of the tube at the 3 mL mark using a sharp razor blade. Put up to 3 tissue sections into each tissue chamber, or up to 1 cm2 of tissue per well. Keep at least one empty well between wells with different antibody combinations to avoid cross-contamination.

Proceed to the primary tetramer and antibody staining immediately after finishing the transfer of all cut sections into the tissues chambers. Keep the sections submerged and chilled in 1 mL of PBS-H at all times.
Incubate the tissue sections overnight with 0.5 µg/mL FITC-conjugated, peptide-loaded MHC-I tetramers diluted in PBS-H with 2% normal goat serum (NGS). Include mouse or other non-rabbit antibodies directed at extracellular epitopes of interest in this incubation (e.g., rat anti-CD8 antibodies diluted 1:500 in PBS-H with 2% NGS). Place 1 mL of diluted antibodies in each well.

NOTE: Care should be taken when selecting CD8 antibodies, as some can enhance and some can inhibit MHC tetramers binding to T-cell receptors4,21. The rat anti-human CD8 antibody described here is unstable and sometimes results in somewhat weak staining. It is used here for triple labeling because it is the only non-rabbit and non-mouse CD8 antibody tested that stained rhesus macaque CD8 T cells.

Use 1 mL of solution per well for the primary antibody and all subsequent incubations, and perform this and all subsequent incubations at 4 °C, with the plates on a rocking platform.
NOTE: Tissues should float freely in the chamber.

2. Day 2: Fixation and Secondary Incubation

After the primary incubation, wash the sections twice with 1 mL of chilled PBS-H for 20 min each wash. Do this by transferring the tissue chambers to a different 24-well tissue culture plate containing 1 mL of chilled PBS-H in the corresponding wells.
NOTE: Be careful not to drip contents from one experimental sample into another when moving between tissue chambers. For all subsequent incubations and washes, similarly transfer the tissue chamber to a clean plate containing the appropriate solution. Be sure to monitor the sections in the tissue chambers during the procedure to make sure that the sections do not get stuck to the sides of the tissue chambers. If they do, push them back into the solution.
Fix the sections with 1 mL of fresh PBS-buffered 4% paraformaldehyde for 2 h at room temperature (do not over-fix). Wash with cold PBS-H twice for 5 min.
Caution: Paraformaldehyde is toxic; wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
NOTE: If antigen retrieval and permeabilization is needed to detect intracellular epitopes, antigens can be retrieved by boiling the sections in 0.01 mol urea after the paraformaldehyde fixation.
Transfer the sections into 24-well culture plates containing 0.01 mol urea and place these plates in a microwave oven. Boil the sections three times for about 10 s each, for a total of 30 s.
NOTE: Be very careful, as boiling the solution can force the sections out of the wells. If this happens, use a paintbrush to push the sections from the sides of the tissue chamber or from the lid of the plate back into the bottom of the appropriate tissue chamber.
Prior to the secondary antibody incubation, permeabilize and block the tissue sections by incubating them in blocking solution containing PBS-H, 0.3% detergent (PBS-H-T), and 2% NGS on a rocker for 1 h at 4 °C. Perform subsequent antibody incubations with PBS-H-T/2% NGS.
For the secondary incubation, transfer the sections in the tissue chambers to wells containing rabbit anti-FITC antibody diluted 1:10,000 in PBS-H-T/2% NGS. Incubate overnight.
Perform counterstaining using mouse anti-CD20 antibody diluted 1:200 in PBS-H-T/2% NGS. For this option, retrieve the epitopes if needed, permeate the cells, and block prior to this incubation, as described above.

3. Day 3: Tertiary Incubation

After the second incubation, wash the sections three times in PBS-H at 4 °C for at least 20 min.
Perform a final incubation with the appropriate fluorescently labeled antibodies (e.g., goat anti-rabbit conjugated greenish yellow, goat anti-rat conjugated far red dye, and goat anti-mouse conjugated green dye antibodies diluted 1:5,000, 1:5,000, and 1:2,000, respectively, in PBS-H-T/2% NGS). Incubate overnight.
NOTE: At this point, the incubation can be extended for up to three days if needed. Keep the sections protected from light by wrapping the plates in tin foil during this incubation step and thereafter, as light quenches fluorophores.

4. Day 4: Mounting the Sections

Wash the sections three times in PBS-H for at least 20 min.
NOTE: If planning for downstream ISH19, fix the sections in 4% paraformaldehyde for 1 h to secure the tetramers and antibodies in place and then wash the sections twice with PBS-H for 5 min each.
Caution: Paraformaldehyde is toxic; wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
Use a paintbrush to transfer the sections to a microscope slide. Be careful not to poke the tissue too much. Coat each section with glycerol/gelatin containing 4 mg/mL n-propyl gallate or another mounting medium containing a fluorophore preservative. Cover with a coverslip.
Store the slides in a light-protected slide container at -20 °C. Rinse the tissue culture plates and remove the labels on the lids using alcohol.
NOTE: The plates can be reused.

5. Acquisition of Confocal Microscope Images

Capture high-resolution images with a confocal microscope, using the appropriate lasers and filters for each fluorophore (Figure 1A and B).
NOTE: In this example, a confocal microscope (see the Table of Materials) was used. Images were collected using the 561 nm laser at 20% power for the greenish yellow-labeled antigen-specific T cells, the 488-nm laser at 10% power for green-labeled CD20-expressing B cells, and the 640-nm laser at 15% power for far red-labelled CD8 T cells. The 20X objective and a numerical aperture of 0.8 were used.
Sequentially collect z-series at 3 µm (or other) intervals in the three channels in multiple 800 x 800 pixel fields. Construct a montage of the collected fields (Figure 1C-E). Name each montage image based on the information of the corresponding slide and save for analysis.
Perform quantitative image analysis using the respective confocal microscope analysis and quantification software or using ImageJ.

6. Quantitative Image Analysis
NOTE: Quantitative image analysis can be accomplished using confocal microscope analysis and quantification software or by using ImageJ software. Here, ImageJ was used as an example.

Open a confocal montage by dragging it to the ImageJ window (Figure 2A).
NOTE: ImageJ can directly open montages collected by many different confocal microscopes. If the montage cannot be directly opened by ImageJ, export the selected z-scan as a TIFF file to open it.
Duplicate the selected z-scan for analysis (“Image”-> “Duplicate”) (Figure 2B).
Split the different channels (“Image”-> “Color”-> “Split Channels”) (Figure 2C).
Draw the ROI for quantitative analysis in the corresponding channel to be objective and add it to the ROI manager by pressing “T” on the keyboard. Measure the area.
NOTE: The ROI manager of ImageJ shows the area in µm2 (Figure 2D).
Adjust the fluorescence brightness and contrast of the channel to be analyzed (“Image” -> “Adjust” -> “Brightness/Contrast”) (Figure 2E).
Flatten the ROI on the image (“ROI manager” -> “Flatten”) (Figure 2F).
Quantify the positive cells in the image using the “Multi-point” tool (Figure 2G).

title: TIL_prep_MC38_sc_MRC
text:
Lymphocyte Tissue Preparation from subcutaneous tumors
Miguel Reina-Campos 10/2019

Inject 3ug of iv antibody (ie 15ul CD8a-APC-Cy7 + 185ul PBS). 3-4 min after, sack the mice (cd).
Open skin by incision in the lower part of the back and use hands to expose tumor
Resect tumor and place in P24 well on ice, if tumor is large enough can be split into two:

Dry well for histology (frozen – OCT) is needed
RP5 media for flow

Collect draining lymph node by exposing it through the fat and remove it with tweezers
Collect spleen
Weight tumors before starting tissue prep

Start with tumor processing:

Mince tissue with scissors in a 50 ml falcon. Alternatively chop down with a razor blade in a P60 plate on ice.
Add Collagenase-I digestion in 5ml in the 50 ml falcon and incubate @37C for 30 min

Collagenase-I recipe – Prepare under the hood
-2ml HG (aliquoted in the -20 fridge) – Do not refreeze aliquot
-200ul 1M MgCl2 (J’s bench)
-200ul 1M CaCl2 (J’s bench)
-10ml Fetal Bovine Serum
-QS to 200ml w/RPMI 1640 1x
100x HG STOCK SOLUTION (STERILE): makes 500ml
59.58g HEPES
14.6g L-glutamine B-grade
500ml (QS to line) RPMI 1640 1x
use stir bar to mix
pH to 7.5 (will take 10-20ml 5N NaOH)
make 10ml aliquots
store @20oC in freezer long-term
While tumors are dissociating, process spleens and lymph nodes and leave them on ice

Filter digested tumors using a 70 um filter (reuse filter for same samples), rinse it with cold PBS. Use syringe plunger to dissociate tumor chunks through the filter.
Centrifuge at 1600 rpm 4 min
After centrifugation and filtration of tumors, resuspend pellet in 5ml 44% Percoll using a 10 ml pipette.

1x PERCOLL STOCK (STERILE): makes 500ml
450ml Percoll (Sigma P1644)
50ml 10x DPBS w/o Ca Mg
keep sterile
store @4<sup>oC in fridge long-term
if removed 50ml from original 500ml percoll bottle to make room for DPBS, bring this to 1X too, do not discard.
44% PERCOLL: makes 100ml
WILL NEED AT LEAST 5ml PER TISSUE (IEL+LP) PER MOUSE
44ml 1x Percoll (recipe above)
56ml RPMI 1640 1x
store @4<sup>oC in fridge overnight
DOE: bring to RT
67% PERCOLL: makes 100ml
WILL NEED AT LEAST 2ml PER TISSUE (IEL+LP) PER MOUSE
67ml 1x Percoll (recipe above)
33ml 1x DPBS w/o Ca Mg
store @4<sup>oC in fridge overnight
DOE: bring to RT

Add the 44% percoll-cell suspension into a 15ml Falcon tube
Insert a glass Pasteur pipette and deliver 67% Percoll to the bottom of the tube.
Spin 20 min at 2,000 rpm (NO brake) and collect interphase with Pasteur pipette into 15ml falcon tubes, fill up with RP5 and spin down at 2,000 rpm for 8min.
Re-suspend pellet in desired counting volume and continue with your staining.

Simultaneous Detection of EGFP and Cell Surface Markers by Fluorescence Microscopy in Lymphoid Tissues
Kim L. Kusser and Troy D. Randall Trudeau Institute, Saranac Lake, New York
SUMMARY Enhanced GFP (EGFP) is a powerful tool for the visualization of tagged pro- teins and transfected cells and is easily detected by fluorescence microscopy or flow cytom- etry in living cells. However, soluble EGFP molecules can be lost if cell integrity is disrupted by freezing, sectioning, or permeablization. Furthermore, the fluorescence of EGFP is de- pendent on its conformation. Therefore, fixation protocols that immobilize EGFP may also destroy its usefulness as a fluorescent reporter. Here we determined which methods of pre- paring murine lymphoid tissues immobilized soluble EGFP protein and retained its fluores- cence while simultaneously maintaining the antigenicity of various immunologically impor- tant molecules and best preserving the overall morphology of the tissues. title: PFA - 16 percent
text:
Edward Yang – 11/1/08
16% PFA – for 500 mL

Materials
350mL DI H20
80 grams of dry PFA
50 mL 10x PBS
Very large beaker (1 liter flat bottom)
500mL beaker (round)
Magnetic stir/ heat plate
Magnetic stir bar
Thermometer
pH meter
10-12N HCL
10-12N NaOH
Method – EVERYTHING is done in the chemical hood

Fill 500mL beaker with 350mL DI H20 and place into very large beaker. Fill large beaker with H20 until covering ~2/3 of 500mL beaker. Place thermometer in outer water bath.

Heat to between 60-70 degrees C. Do not exceed 70 degrees C as that is the flash point of PFA.

Weigh out 80g of dry PFA in the hood. Place magnetic stir bar (and start stirring) into 500mL beaker and then pour in dry PFA slowly.
Use plastic pipet to pipet in 1-2 pipet-full’s worth of NaOH. Watch temperature to make sure it’s at ~65 degrees C.

As PFA begins to go into solution, pipet in NaOH dropwise to improve solubility, conservatively.

Add NaOH dropwise until PFA completely goes into solution. The color of the solution should be completely clear/transparent.

Once in solution, pour in 50mL of 10x PBS, fill the rest up to the 500mL line with DI H20, and stir until mixed.

Turn off heat, pour out outer water bath, and fill with cold/RT water. Cool PFA solution until room temperature.
pH the solution to about 7.2-7.4 pH using HCL.
Sterile filter PFA using ~0.1 micron filter. Label with date and 16%.

text:

Lymphocyte_Separation_Media
Product Information
Lymphocyte Separation Medium Mediatech’s Lymphocyte Separation Medium is a sterile-filtered density gradient based on A Sterile, Iso-osmotic the adapted method of isolating lymphocytes using centrifugation techniques by Boyum. Polysucrose and Diatrizoate LSM is designed for the simple, rapid isolation of lymphocytes from diluted defibrinated Solution with Low Viscosity whole blood layered on a solution of sodium metrizoate and dextran or Ficoll® and centri- Designed for the in vitro fuged at low speeds for 30 minutes. Isolation of Lymphocytes from Migration of blood cells through the solution during centrifugation results in the forma- Diluted Whole Blood tion of density specific layers. Lymphocytes and other mononuclear cells form a distinct band between the serum and LSM fractions. Lymphocytes are recovered by aspirating the plasma layer and then removing the cells. Excess platelets, LSM, and plasma can then be removed by cell washing. For best results, use blood drawn less than two hours before. Do not use blood more than 24 hours from when it was drawn.
Procedure 1. Allow the LSM to equilibrate to room temperature and Figure 1. Separation of mononuclear cells thoroughly mix by gently inverting the bottle. from whole blood

Aseptically transfer 3 mL of LSM to a sterile 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Mix 2 mL of defibrinated or heparinized blood with 2 mL of physiological saline or balanced salt solution. Plasma & Mononuclear
Carefully LAYER the diluted blood over 3 mL of LSM in a LSM Cell Layer sterile 15 mL centrifuge tube, creating a sharp blood-LSM interface. DO NOT MIX! The quality of the separation is dependent upon a sharp interface RBC’s between the diluted blood and density gradient.
Centrifuge the tube at 400 x g at room temperature for 15 to 30 minutes. Centrifugation should sediment erythrocytes and polynuclear leukocytes and bond mononuclear lymphocytes above the LSM, as shown in Figure 1.
Aspirate the top layer of clear plasma to within 2-3 mm above the lymphocyte layer.
Aspirate the lymphocyte layer plus about half of the LSM layer below it and transfer it to a centrifuge tube. Add an equal volume of buffered balanced salt solution to the lymphocyte layer in the centrigue tube and centrifge for 10 minutes at room temperature (18- 25C) at a speed sufficient to sediment the cells without damage, i.e., 160-260 x g. Washing the cells removes LSM and reduces the percentage of platelets.
Wash the cells again with buffered balanced salt solution and resuspend in the appropriate medium for your applications. References 1 Boyum, A., “Separation of white blood cells.” Nature 204, 793-794, 1976 2 Boyum, A., “Isolation of mononuclear cells and granulocytes from human blood.” Scand.J.Clin.Invest. 21Suppl. 97:77, 1968. 3 Harris, R. and Ukaylofo, E.V., “Rapid preparation of lymphocytes for tissue typing.” Lancet 2, 327, 1969. 4 Thornsby, E. and Bratlie, A., “A rapid method for preparation of pure lymphocyte suspensions.” In Histocompatibility Testing, P.I., ed. Munksgaard, Copenhagen, p. 664-665, 1970. 5 Ting, A. and Morris, P.J., “A technique for lymphocyte preparation from stored heparainzed blood.” Vox Sang 20, 561, 1971.

title: Histology Ultimate Protocol-REVISED
text:
Epic Histology Protocol – for Spleen and Lymph Nodes
Tissue Processing

Materials

4% Formaldehyde/Paraformaldehyde(PFA) – see PFA protocol

Make fresh from high concentration stock each time
Use 15 conicals – enough to cover spleen/LN

5% Sucrose/ 4% formaldehyde (4mL sucrose, 3mL 37% formaldehyde, 20mL PBS)
10% Sucrose
30% Sucrose
OCT, Cryo-molds cassette, and dry ice
Fisherbrand Superfrost-Plus microscope slides
1x PBS

Method
Fixation and Dehydration

Sacrifice mouse and harvest spleen/ lymph nodes.
Drop organs into 4% formaldehyde/5% sucrose conicals IMMEDIATELY upon removal and place on ice.

Attach tubes to BellyDancer or something with rotation, or periodically rotate/tap to make sure fixative penetrates all directions.
Leave organs in fixative (4% formaldehyde) at least a combined 6 hours at 4°C

If sac’ing late in the day, okay to leave in solution overnight
Incubate in 5% Sucrose for at least 2 hours.





Aspirate out the fixative and pour in 9 mL of 10% Sucrose solution (w/ 4% formaldehyde is tissues have not been incubated for at least 6 hrs yet)

Incubate for 2-3 hrs at 4°C.




Replace 10% Sucrose with 30% Sucrose and incubate at 4 degree C° overnight or for the full day if it’s been fixed overnight already.


Embedding

Put processed organs into respective small Petri dishes with fresh OCT and use to:

Wash residual sucrose off by rolling around in OCT.

Fill up a Cry-mold cassette completely with OCT

Place the tissue at the bottom of the cassette, making sure that there are no bubbles

Place cassettes with tissues/OCT on a flat block of dry ice until OCT has turned opaque white
Store all blocks in labeled boxes in -80°C.

Fixation and Slide Preparation for Staining

Materials

Fixing reagent of choice: -20°C Acetone, 4% Formaldehyde (Stock 37% Formaldehyde w/ 5-10% methanol as preservative), 4% Paraformaldehyde (PFA, 100% pure formaldehyde)

See protocol for making 20% PFA (4% PFA easily degrades)

Coplin jars for acetone fixations
1X PBS (ridiculous amounts) – use 10X PBS for dilutions rather than 1X stocks
Coplin jars or slide holder chambers (for many samples) for washes
Glass slide holder (compatible with slide holder chamber)
Pap pen (creates liquid repelling barrier around sample)
Large Kimwipes
Thawed sample slides (no ice crystal damage): less than 5 minutes


Method

Fixation (pick one of following fixatives): After samples are thawed

-20°C Acetone – Harshest but cleaner fixation method, will destroy GFP and other very sensitive epitopes (protein pulldown/precipitation reaction)/ Note: acetone will smear off all permanent markers

Pour in enough acetone to cold coplin jar to cover sections on slides, AT MOST UP TILL THE FROSTED EDGE WITH WRITING (acetone will smear)
Carefully transport to -20°C and fix for 5 minutes
Carefully pull out slides individually and place on paper towels, allowing acetone to quickly evaporate
After evaporation, wash 3x with 1X PBS in coplin jars, 10-15 minutes each

4% Formaldehyde/ PFA – standard fixation (defer to this first)

Dilute high concentration formaldehyde/PFA stock to 4% in PBS

~50uL/section on each slide (Exp: 3 sections/slide = ~150uL)

Pipet ~50uL onto each sample at RT, careful not to damage section
Fix for 10 minutes
Wash 3x with 1X PBS in coplin jars, 5-10 minutes each time


Pap Penning and Preparation for Blocking/Staining

Lay out slides on paper towels and dry around the glass and individual sections using large Kimwipes (paper towels will form lint). DO NOT TOUCH SECTIONS WITH TOWELS!
Circle each individual section a few times with pap pen, allow to dry
Dip sections into PBS again to retain moisture

Blocking
Materials

Blocking Buffer – the Epic (Gelatin) Block (for 50mL)

1.5mL normal goat serum (3%)
1.5mL normal donkey serum (3%)
1.5-2.0 g BSA
1mL fishscale gelatin (advised to add after some PBS)
25ul Tween20 (0.05%)
50ul Triton-X-100 (0.1%)
250ul 10% Azide (0.05%)
Fill to the 50ml mark w/ 1x PBS
Optional: make ~5 tubes and aliquot into 15mL conicals and freeze to store

Fc Block
Vector Labs Avidin/Biotin blocking kit (if using biotinylated antibodies)
Hydration chamber (basically some sort of plastic sealable container with wet paper towels on the bottom – incubate slides so liquid does not evaporate)
Coplin jars or slide chambers (see fixation materials)
1x PBS

Method

Make master mix: depending on section size, add ~50uL Gelatin Block and ~5uL Fc block per sample

Pipet ~50uL onto pap pen circled section, making sure to cover section

Place slides into hydration chamber and incubate for at least 20-30 minutes

Ok to leave longer: this is a good stopping point if you need to take care of other stuff.

Only if using biotinylated antibodies – Avidin/Biotin block, perform in this order:

Tap slides on paper towel to remove blocking buffer
Apply 1 drop of avidin block onto each section – incubate 15 minutes

Tap slides on paper towel to remove blocking buffer

Apply 1 drop of biotin block onto each section – incubate 15 minutes

Rinse off/rehydrate each slide by dipping a few times into PBS (in Coplin jars)

Aspirate off extra liquid carefully using edges of Kimwipe. DO NOT TOUCH SECTION!

Slides are ready to stain

Staining
Materials

Epic (Gelatin) Blocking Buffer (see Blocking)
Antibodies (see list at end for antibodies and concentrations tested using this protocol)
Coplin jars or slide chambers (see fixation materials)
1x PBS
Hydration chamber (see Blocking)
37° Incubator

Method

Similar to Blocking, aspirate off extra liquid using kimwipes without letting slides completely dry out
Make master mix of respective Primary Ab (including biotinylated Abs) stains in the blocking buffer

Pipet Ab mixture onto sections ~50ul

Place slides into hydration chamber and seal lid
Incubate slides in hydration chamber in 37° incubator for 1 hour (after 1 hour, antibodies/proteins will start to denature)
After 1 hour, EITHER:

Put slides into PBS in coplin jars/slide chamber and wash 3x at 5-10 minutes each
OR, if working with a difficult Ab, move slides in hydration champer with Ab mixture still on into cold room and incubate for another 2-4 hrs. Afterwards, wash as in 5a.

If no secondary Ab is needed, move onto “Mounting”
Pipet on Secondary Ab mixture prepared same way as the Primary

Follow same steps as Primary Ab
Incubate for only 30-45 minutes at 37° (or else high background)

Wash slides 3x in 1x PBS, 5-10 minutes each time

Mounting and Sealing

Materials

Paper Towels
Kimwipes
Mounting Media – Invitrogen Pro-Long Gold Antifade Reagent (I prefer w/o DAPI)

Rest upside down to get rid of bubbles

Nail Polish (Sally Hansen brand, or anything that isn’t too thick)
Fisherbrand glass coverslips

Method

Using Kimwipes, wipe slides of all liquid and smear off some pap pen

Be very careful not to touch the section using Kimwipes
Leave slides in dark area like drawer to dry for a few minutes (not too long)

Apply very small drop of Mounting Media onto each section

NO BUBBLES – If bubbles form, aspirate off using a pipet

Carefully place on coverslips

Technique: place on one edge first and slowly lower onto the other

Carefully apply nail polish to edges of coverslip to seal onto the slide

Technique: do not move the coverslip; if nail polish is too thick, dilute it down with some acetone

Store slides in 4° until ready to view

Contact Information

If you are from the Goldrath Lab and are stuck with anything, you can contact me for assistance, wherever my awesomeness may be:
Edward Yang
edyang86@gmail.com
(626)242-5712
Random tips


37° incubation might not work for everything

For more sensitive staining such as KLRG-1 – stain for 1hr in 37° and then transfer to 4° for another 2-3hrs – overnight. Makes a big difference

Pay attention to appropriate fixation
This protocol works very well on staining for CD11c, CD45.1, CD4, and B220 thus far
CD8 staining can be a little weak
If cutting sections is difficult/rolling:

Use gradual pulling technique (similar to riding the block) by picking off one side of section first and pulling meticulously as it quickly sticks to slide
Warning: can be incredibly frustrating; use caution when cutting very important experiments

Lowering concentration of fixative can if these problems ensue, but higher risk of epitope degradation, especially if working with Thy1.1


Section a certain way… the longitudinal, not lateral, cuts for the spleen
Need a butt load of PBS – suggest using 10x
Be more careful w/ working in the light/sunlight after slides are stained
Everything is variable, whatever works works, and what works for some, will not for others


Microscope and Microscopy Core for Imaging

For confocal images, anything requiring AF647/APC, and stuff you want to publish, use the confocal microscopes at the UCSD SOM Microscopy Core: Olympus FV1000

Contact Jennifer Santini or whoever is the Managing Director of Microscopy Core
http://microscopy.ucsd.edu/ContactUs.html
http://microscopy.ucsd.edu/Reservations.html
She will guide you through all necessary training to use Microscope

Microscope settings

Pixels: no more than 10, any more is usually overkill (prone to bleaching)
1024x1024 is the size I use typically
Focus x2 scan on 512x512 yields best image/speed ratio

Can titrate up or down based on how dim/bright initial stain is

Blocking Solutions
   
Background or unspecific staining often occurs for IHC antibody staining. Here we list commonly used blocking solutions during antibody staining procedure to reduce background or unspecific staining.
Peroxidase Blocking Soluiton (3% H2O2 in PBS):
       30% H2O2 ————————- 10 ml

-after the blotting is finished remove chromatography paper and gel
-add 10 ml quikhyb solution hyb tube (incubate in oven while waiting for blot to finish to prewarm)
-add 25ul denatures salmon sperm DNA and coat sides of tube

-open typhoon program (change acquisition mode to storage:phospho)
-run and save (remember which squares your blots are on)

title: Listeria production
text:
Listeria production:
Ok, here’s the instructions from Phil on making freezes of Listeria
(this is how I make what I sent you):
Hope the cells got to you fine. I asked Ingrid, our lab manager, about
Freezing Listeria, and basically what you want to do is take what the saturated
frozen cultures that you have currently, and inoculate a large BHI culture to grow for
during the day (e.g., 200 ul into 100 ml) until it reaches a log phase OD 600 of ~0.2.
Then just freeze them directly in the BHI in aliquots (we do 1 ml aliquots). You can then take those and thaw them anytime to grow another culture to OD 0.1 to infect mice (I put 200 ul into 5 ml BHI, it takes about 2.5 hrs to get to OD 0.1). Hope this helps.
Here are instructions for growing Listeria:
Thaw a frozen stock (I usually stick in a 37 degree H20 bath). Dilute
1:50 in tryptic soy broth (no more than 1 month old). I usually make
10-20 mls. Grow at 37 until an OD600 of approx. 0.1 (this is mid log
phase) then stick culture on ice to stop growth. At a 1:50 dilution of
the frozen this usually takes between 1.5 and 2.5 hours. An OD600 of
0.1=2x10e8 cfu/ml. Perform serial dilutions in sterile PBS to inject
5000 cfu iv for B6 mice (for balbs the typical dose is 2000). Peak CD8
response for primary is day 7 I think. I often got about 8-13% of CD8s
in the spleen responding by tetramer or IFNg.
I do everything is in a BSL2 TC hood. Use disposable plastic 1 ml
cuvettes to OD bugs and I parafilm around the top of them. Bleach all
tips and pipets, etc in 10% bleach before disposing as biohazard. When
I do FACS staining of cells from infected mice, I flick plates into a 2
L beaker with bleach in the bottom and always use a plate with a lid
(until fixed of course). I know this is overkill compared to Bevan Lab
procedures, but there’s always someone pregnant around here!
<This protocol is from Max 2021>
Procedure
Growing a stock
Growing a Listeria stock
This is a protocol that I got from Maurice, Nicholas J (nmaurice@fredhutch.org) for the Lm-OVA variants (N4, Q4, T4)
Our former technician, who was a bit eccentric, wrote this (and it isn’t formatted for the N4/Q4/T4, which are chromosomally integrated) I’ll note where our practices differ in red:
Procedure

Inject 3000-4000 CFU into hosts (I just start with the vial in ~3-4mL Brain-heart infusion (BHI) media, with no antibiotic and move to step 9)
Sacrifice mice between 48 and 60 hrs post-infection
Harvest and tease apart spleen in 5ml PBS+0.1% NP40
Plate 200ml of spleen solution onto BHI+erythromycin plate [spread out sequentially to get single colonies]
Incubate for 48 hours


There should be little to no growth after 24 hours – the presence of large colonies at this time point suggests contamination.
Do not grow past 48 hours – overgrowth may occur

�. Harvest a single colony into 200ml of BHI+ erythromycin (in mc tube) Take several medium-sized colonies (growth will be heterogeneous)
7. Grow for 4 hr with shaking 37C (set speed higher to ensure agitation in mc tubes) �. Inoculate 4ml of BHI (no antibiotic at this step) with LM-OVA from previous step

Expand with shaking until broth is mildly cloudy
Add 4ml of bacteria to 26ml of BHI broth in a 50ml Falcon tube (or 200ml flask) (depending on growth kinetics, you could set this up as an overnight)
Expand with shaking for several hours until broth is cloudy, add erythromycin for the last 45-60min of culturing (once the OD is at about 0.6) (I don’t bother with erythromycin since these are stable/do everything sterile)
Read OD: should be at 0.6 – 0.8 before moving on to step 12 (OD can be pushed a little higher; if overgrowth occurs, just add BHI and allow to re-enter log-phase of growth)
Add 15ml of the 40% glyercol stock (40% glycerol stock is 20mL glycerol in 30mL BHI; I sterile filter mine and use fresh) to the 30ml of cloudy bacteria culture
mix gently on ice and aliquot 1ml in screw top cryotubes (keep on wet ice while aliquoting) (I like my LM to be on wet ice to facilitate glycerol uptake for a bit before moving them into the -80°C freezer).
Freeze -80C

FACS protocol sheet


You will need about 105 – 5x106 cells for FACS staining (optimal = 106) per sample
Spin the cells down

96 well plates or 15 ml conical tubes – 1800 rpm for 5 minutes
Eppendorf tubes – 30 seconds at max

You must first FC block (If you are staining for FC, proceed to next step)

Make master mix of 50 μl FACS buffer/sample plus 0.25 μl FC block/sample (e.g., if you have 8 samples, mix 400 μl FACS buffer + 2 μl FC block)
Resuspend your cell pellet in 50 μl master mix and vortex

title: RNA extraction with Trizol
text:
RNA extraction with Trizol (adapted from Kyla)


Thaw Trizol sample at RT.


Add 2ul glycoblue


Add chloroform


For 500ul Trizol, use 100ul chloroform
For 1000ul Trizol, use 200ul chloroform


Shake vigorously for approx 15s


Incubate 2-3 min at RT


Centrifuge 15 min at 12000g, 4C


Carefully transfer aqueous phase to a fresh tube (work on ice from this point)


Pipet in circular motion, avoid interphase by leaving generous amount of aqueous phase
For 500ul Trizol, transfer ~250ul
For 1ml Trizol, transfer ~500ul


Add isopropanol (flick, do not pipette)


For 500ul Trizol, add 250ul isopropanol
For 1ml Trizol, add 500ul isopropanol


Centrifuge 20 min at 12,000g, 4C


Then remove supernatant with pipette tip


Wash with 1ml cold 75% EtOH (make fresh using DNAse/RNAse-free water)


Flick to loose pellet


Centrifuge 15 min at 7,400g, 4C


Pipette of as much EtOH as possible. Use 10ul micropipettor for small volume
Dry 10-15 min


Resuspend RNA pellet in 10ul nuclease-free water


Incubate 10-15 min at 55-60C . Proceed to DNAse I digestion.


DNAse I digestion (from Turbo DNA-free procedure)


Add 1ul 10X Turbo Dnase buffer and 1ul Turbo Dnase to sample. Mix gently.


Incubate 20-30 min at 37C


Add 2ul of resuspended DNA Inactivation Reagent and mix well.


Incubate 5 min, RT. Mix occasionally.


Centrifuge 1.5 min at 10,000g


Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube. Avoid pellet.

title: ca-p transfection of Phoenix
text:
CALCIUM PHOSPHATE TRANSFECTION OF ΦNX CELLS TO PRODUCE VIRAL SUP.
Day 1: Plate 1 million Phoenix cells per petridish (Falcon 3004; this is a 6cm petridish with a surface area of 21 sq cm) in 4 ml Iscove’s containing 10% FCS + 2-ME + antibiotics. Culture cells ON as usual (no shaking/rocking) in a 37C incubator.
Day 2: Ca-P transfection (Gibco BRL 18306-019)
885 ul water
100 ul 10x HBS
vortex
15 ul 1M NaOH
vortex
Pipet 500 ul 1x HBS soln + 10 ul phosphate soln into tube 1.
Tube 2:
430 ul water
10-20 ug plasmid DNA (prefered conc: 1 ug/ul), mix gently
10 ul Calcium solution, mix gently
50 ul Calcium solution, mix gently
Bubble air in tube 1 and add slowly the mix from tube 2 into tube 1. This will become a milky suspension. Incubate 20 min at RT. Add 10 min before the transfection 4 ul of 30 mM Chloroquine (=15 mg/ml and filter sterile) to the Phoenix cells and mix gently by swirling.
Add the DNA-Ca-P mixture dropwise to the Phoenix cells and incubate them as usual ON at 37C.
Day 3: Replace medium by 4 ml FTOC medium and incubate the Phoenix cells as usual O/N at 37C.
Day 4: Harvest transient virus supernatant. Keep the virus 15 min on ice. Spin 5 minutes 1500 rpm or filter supernatant (to get rid of the few Phoenix cells present in the supernatant; For the FTOC experiments spinning will do the job) and make 0.5 ml or 1 ml aliquots of the viral supernatant. Freeze immediately at -80C. Because freeze steps reduce the transduction efficiency with 50% we thaw an aliquot only once. Phoenix cells are analyzed by FACS for eGFP expression the same day.
What is important, is to do the transfection at the END of day 2 and to replace the medium with FTOC medium at the BEGINNING of day 3. Whatever transfection protocol you will use, the cells won’t like it and therefore this period should be as short as possible. Furthermore, replacing the medium at the beginning of day 3 with FTOC medium gives you the full 24h to accumulate virus before harvesting the supernatant at the beginning of day 4.
The 4 ml FTOC medium will appear orange-yellow just before harvesting, so, I would not advice to decrease the volume any further. It may increase your virus titer but I don’t think many fetal thymocytes will survive the transduction in such exhausted medium. They already have a hard time surviving the transduction protocol as it is now.
What is also important is that the virus supernatant harvesting procedure is performed as fast as possible. After 15 min on ice immediately spin the supernatant and very quickly freeze at -80C.

title: Preparing mouse joints for histology
text:
Preparing mouse joints for histology
3.7% Formalin solution in PBS:

Dilute 37% Formalin 1 to 10 in PBS

14% EDTA solution:

Add 140 g free acid EDTA to 700 ml distilled H2O
On stir plate in the fume hood, add ammonium hydroxide 30 ml at a time until solution clears (about 90 ml total).
Add H2O to almost 1L. Check pH and adjust with ammonium hydroxide dropwise up to pH 7.2, then adjust final volume to 1L.

Sac mice, remove as much skin from legs as possible.
Harvest paws and knees; immediately fix in 3.7% formalin solution.
Fix for 1 day on shaker at RT.
Rinse with 14% EDTA solution.
Incubate in 14% EDTA solution on shaker at RT for 5 more days. Replace with new 5% EDTA solution daily.
Test if decalcified: bones should feel elastic. A test cut should not have resistance and not feel like cutting sand.
For paraffin embedding, place in 30%, 50%, and 70% ETOH for at least 30 min each prior to submitting to core lab.

title: Antibody purification
text:
Purification of Antibodies:
Equipment:
HiTrap Protein G column –
Peristaltic Pump or syringe
Collection tubes (FACS tubes work really well) with 100 ul of Tris pH 9.0
Protocol:
Important things to remember:
Peristaltic Pump:

Run Sodium Phosphate buffer pH 7.0 into the tubing to equilibrate it until it begins dripping out the side with the metal lock. Stop the flow.
Place column onto a metal stand
Attach the metal lock to the column using the red adaptor then continue the flow. This is known as adding it ‘drop-to-drop’, which prevents air from entering the column.
Run 5x the volume of the column (25 ml) of Sodium Phosphate buffer pH 7.0 over the column and save the flow through.
Begin running your antibody supernatant over the column…make sure to use a new collection tube once the supernatant reaches the column.
Once all of your supernatant has been collected, run another 5 volumes of Sodium Phosphate buffer pH 7.0.
Elute the antibody using 0.1M Glycine buffer, pH 2.8. 20 fractions of approximately 1 ml each is good. For this small a volume, 30 ml syringes work well to add the glycine. Just make sure to put the syringe on ‘drop-to-drop’ to avoid air entering the column.
Once eluted, attach the column onto the metal stand once again, and run 5 bed volumes of 20% EtOH through it. The column can be stored at 4°C until later use. The tubing can stay attached until later use.
Set up a 96-well plate with the following for each fraction (don’t forget pos and neg controls too!):

20 ul sample
20 ul biorad protein assay dye (Cat # 500-0006)
60 ul H20




Collect the fractions that turn the darkest blue – these contain the eluted antibody!
Use spin collection tubes to concentrate the antibody (see tube directions for how)
Use a protein assay kit (BioRad) to analyze the concentration of your antibody.

End Repair:
End-It DNA end repair kit (Epicenter ER0720)

2.5uL 2.5mM dNTPs

0.5uL End-it Enzyme mix
 
Incubate 45 minutes, 25degC in a PCR tube in the PCR machine.
Zymo DNA clean/concentrate, elute in 2x8uL 10mM Tris pH8.0, heated to 55degC, incubate on column at least 3 minutes per elution, 16uL total eluate. Alternatively add 3x volume SPRI or Ampure bead, wash twice with fresh 80% EtOH, elute in A-tail mix + H2O to 25uL.
 
A addition
25uL total:
16uL End-repaired DNA
2.5uL 10x NEBuffer 2
5uL 1mM dATP
1.5uL Klenow (3’-5’ exo(-), 5U/uL)
 
Incubate 30-45 minutes, 37degC in PCR machine
Zymo DNA clean/concentrate, elute twice with same 10uL pre-heated 10mM tris pH 8.0, 11uL total. Alternatively, add 3x volume SPRI buffer, wash twice with fresh 80% EtOH, elute in ligation mix + H2O to 13.5 uL
 
Adaptor ligation
Check Kappa Hyperprep kit for adaptor concentration to use
DO NOT ADD ADAPTER TO MASTER MIX – it will ligate and form dimers in the tube. Add individually to each reaction.
15uL total
6uL DNA
7.5uL 2x Quick ligase buffer
1.5 uL adaptor oligo
0.5 uL Quick DNA ligase (1U/uL); or high concentration T4 ligase (Fermentas/Epicenter)
 
 
Incubate 45 minutes, 20degC, PCR machine
+2uL USER enzyme (works in ligation buffer) - adapter has a hairpin, this enzyme cut a uracyl in the hairpin to linearize the strands
Incubate 37degC 15 minutes
Bring volume to 50uL with 10mM tris pH 8.0
Add 1.75X Ampure/SPRI beads
Mix, incubate 5’
2x fresh 80% EtOH rinse (don’t resuspend the beads, just run the EtOH down the side)
Remove ALL of the EtOH, allow beads to air-dry briefly
Resuspend beads in 15uL 10mM tris pH 8.0, incubate 10 with occasional vortexting
Gather beads with magnet and keep supernatant for PCR

title: Fugene 6 mediated transfection of Phoenix cell
text:
Fugene 6 mediated transfection of Phoenix cell for retrovirus production
Day 0

Inoculate Phoenix cells (4x10^6) in 10cm dish

Day 1

Warm medium (DMEM, 10% FCS, PSG; Optimem, serum free) to 37oC
Transfer 10 ug of plasmid into eppendorf tube
Dilute 30ul of Fugene in 170 ul of serum free Optimem (3ul Fugene: 1ug of DNA)
Add 3 (Fugene/media) into 2 (plasmid DNA) dropwise. Incubate at RT for 15min.
Change media of culture on Phoenix cells to 8 ml of DMEM, 10% FCS, PSG.
Add Fugene/DNA mix to culture dish dropwise.
Culture cells ON at 37oC.

Day 2

Aspirate media (remember this is now virus containing material-handle properly) and replace with 8ml of Optimem, 10% FCS, PSG OR media you intend to grow the cells you will be transducing with the virus with.

Day 3 and 4

title: pSTAT5 Protocol
text:
Download the original PDF

AD060409 pSTAT5 Protocol
Ananda Goldrath Laboratory Andrew/Mark pSTAT5 Protocol Protocol from BD adapted/optimized for 96 well plates by MPR, written up/also used successfully by ALD. BD Phosflow lyse/fix buffer Cat#558049 BD Phosflow Perm buffer III Cat#558050 (stored at RT in brown bottles). BD PE antiStat5 pY694 Cat#612567 (comes very diluted…make sure you have ~6ul for each sample)
Treat cells in 96 well plate in ~100ul volume (need room for fix buffer, do not exceed 125ul if in V bottom plate on ice. Mix well with multichannel. Make sure you have unstimulated cells as controls.
Place in 37 degree water bath on top of rack to ensure rapid transition to 37 deg temp. Careful to have water level just right so plate does not flood. After seeing MPR data, I decided on 25 min for IL2/15 treatment of PyMT TIL. You can tilt the plate slightly as you put in down to avoid air bubbles under your cell containing wells. Other times may work better or worse for your application. Mark used the 37 TC incubator instead of the water bath for all 37 steps.
At 25 min, remove from water bath, set on paper towel to dry, and add 1:1 amount of 2X lyse/f ix buffer. This is made by adding 1.5mls of water to 1ml of 5X lyse/fix concentrate (scale volumes up or down accordingly for the number of cells you have). Use multichannel and pipette up and down several times gently to mix. Media will change from red to yellowish. (Example, if you had 100ul of cells, add 100ul of lyse/fix)
Put back in 37 degree water bath for 10 minutes.
Remove plate, dry bottom by setting on paper towels, and spin down 500xg (~2000RPM in our centrifuge) for 8 min.
Flick off super and resuspend in 250ul of RT PBS (no ca2+/Mg2+)
Pellet as before.
Flick off super and resuspend in 100ul of 1X Perm Buffer III. This seems to be alcohol based, so transfer quickly before it drips out of the end of the tips (b/c of vapor pressure?) Let sit on ice for 30 min.
Pellet, flick of super, and resuspend in 250ul FACS buffer (PBS/BGS/azide). Repeat and flick off super again.
Resuspend in FACS buffer plus Abs.
Resuspend cells in 30ul (to conserve antibodies). I used the following mix: 19ul CD8aFITC (1/60 dilution) 110ul pStat5 PE (1/10) 10ul CD4 PerCP (clone GK1.5) (1/110) 19ul CD44APC (1/60) in 950ul FACS buffer. Looking at the results, I believe you could use 1/2 the CD44 (or use at ~1/100), but keep the FITC high at ~1/50) Stain 30‐60 min at RT in dark. Wash as usual and run samples.
Note that not all antibodies work on fixed cells, and those that do in general have to be used at a higher concentration than on live cells. There are some web resources for antibodies that have been successfully used on cells fixed in this manner, for example:
www.bdbiosciences.com/docs/Validated_Cell_Surface_Markers.xls
June 4, 2009

title: ChIP protocol
text:
Goldrath Lab ChIP Protocol
Fixation:
-Harvest cells (between 10-60 million but 40 million is optimum) and place them in 10mL media or PBS
-Add 270ul 37% formaldehyde (to make 1% formaldehyde) and incubate for 10 minutes and RT
-Stop the reaction with 1000ul 1.25M glycine (to make .125M glycine) and incubate for 5 minutes at RT
-Spin the cells down and wash once with ice cold 10 mL PBS. You can flash freeze the cells at this point if you wish to sonicate at a later time.
-Spin again and resuspend in 1000ul Lysis Buffer. Add fresh protease inhibitors (PIC cocktail and benzamidine) to the solution. Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
Sonication:
-Sonicate 8 times (amplitude 20%) for 10 seconds each time. Between each sonication rest the cells on ice for 30-60 seconds. Keep lysate on ice as much as possible and try to avoid creating bubbles. (use Branson 250 sonicator and 1/8 inch probe).
-Spin down sonicated lysate (5min at 13K rpm) to get rid of debris. Put the supernatant (the lysate) in a new eppendorf tube. The lysate can be stored at -80C or used immediately.
-To test the sonication efficiency take 50ul of lysate. Add 100ul of water and incubate overnight at 65C to reverse the crosslinks.
-Add 1 ul RNase A (stock at 100mg/ml) and incubate at 37C for 30 minutes. Add 2ul proteinase K (stock at 20mg/ml) and incubate at 55C for 1 hour.
-Extract DNA using Qiagen Qiaquik purification kit.
-Measure absorbance at 260nm (use a 1:50 dilution of DNA in 1X TE). Multiply by 2500 to get DNA in ug/ml.
-run 10ul of DNA on a 1% agarose gel to test sonication (should see a smear around 500-1000bp).
Immunoprecipitation:
-use 10ug of DNA/Immunoprecipitation (using more can decrease the efficiency of the pulldown).
-Dilute with 9 volumes of Dilution Buffer. Add protease inhibitors (PIC cocktail and benzamidine) to the solution.
-Add 2-10ug antibody and rotate overnight at 4C. Remember to save an input sample (no antibody added, leave at 4C until elution step).
-Add 30ul protein G agarose beads (preadsorbed against BSA and salmon sperm DNA from Cell Signaling Technology) to each IP and rotate for 2hours at 4C. Use tips with the ends cut off when handling the protein G beads.
-Spin down complexes for 30 seconds at 8000rpm and discard the supernatant. Resuspend the beads in 1mL WBI, rotate at 4C for 5minutes and spin as before.
-Repeat wash with WBII, WBIII and two times with 1X TE.
-Elute with 200ul Elution Buffer and shake for 30 minutes at 65C then reverse the crosslinks overnight at 65C. Remember to reverse crosslink your input sample as well (add 50ul of input to 200ul of Elution Buffer).
DNA extraction:
-Add 1ul of RNase A (stock at 100mg/ml) and incubate at 37C for 30minutes. Add 2ul of proteinase K (stock at 20mg/ml) and incubate at 55C for 1 hour.
-Spin down sample as before and transfer the supernatant to a new tube (this is the eluted DNA/protein complexes. Discard the beads).
-Extract DNA with Qiagen Qiaquik purification kit. Elute in 55ul elution buffer. Be sure to bind at 6000xg, other spins at max speed. Incubate elution buffer and column for 1 minute before spinning for maximum yield.
Reagents:
-Protease Inhibitor Cocktail Set V, EDTA-free (Calbiochem 539137-10VL), use at 1X
-Benzamidine (Sigma B6506-5G), use at 1mM
-Protein G agarose beads (Cell Signaling Technology 9007s)
