title: Updated Pancreas Single-Cell Dissociation for Flow
text:
Procedure

Euthanize by CO2 asphyxiation followed by cervical dislocation; remove the pancreas rapidly (about 1–2 minutes).
Place pancreata in 5 mL medium without FBS and keep on ice until all samples are collected.
Mince finely for 2 minutes. Return to a 15 mL conical and add 7.6 mL medium without FBS, for a total volume of approximately 12.6 mL.
Add 1.4 mL 10× dissociation buffer per pancreas.
Warm quickly to 37°C in a 37°C water bath for 10 minutes.
Transfer to a 37°C rocking incubator.
Incubate for 20 minutes at 37°C, rocking and triturating gently every 10 minutes.
Let tissue pieces settle. Transfer supernatant to a new 15 mL tube and centrifuge 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend in 5 mL medium with FBS and keep on ice.
Add fresh dissociation buffer to the remaining tissue. Incubate 20 minutes at 37°C, rocking and triturating gently every 10 minutes with LoBind tips. Add DNase as needed and repeat for three total collections.
Prepare 10 mL medium with FBS in a new 50 mL conical with a nylon strainer on top.
Pour harvested tubes through the strainer, mash through a 100 µm strainer with a plunger, and wash the strainer with 10 mL medium with FBS.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend in 5 mL medium with FBS.
Perform a viable cell count using AO/PI or Trypan Blue and save dissociation images.

title: Lymphocyte isolation from mouse tissues
text:
Lymphocyte isolation from mouse tissues
Materials

RP-5 (RPMI with 5% BGS)
CMF medium
DTE solution
Collagenase solution
44% and 67% Percoll solutions
PBS
Cell strainers
15 ml and 50 ml conical tubes
Glass Pasteur pipettes

Can use iterative takedown media calculator here: https://protocols.heeg.io/recipes/takedown/#interactive-calculator
IV Labeling for T Cell Resident Memory (TRM) Panels

3 minutes prior to sacrifice, inject mice retro-orbitally with 200 μl antibody mix containing 3 μg of the labeling antibody (e.g. 15 μl CD8a-APC-Cy7 + 185 μl PBS)
Sacrifice mice, remove small intestine and spleen, place in ice-cold RP-5 or CMF, and trim off fat

Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Preparation

Place paper towels on desk and wet with CMF
Wet gut with CMF, cut out Peyer’s patches and clean out fecal matter
Cut the small intestine in half lengthwise and then into small (~1 cm) pieces. Keep the tissue wet during the entire time.
Place in flask and wash 2× with CMF, pouring out contents carefully to retain tissue
Discard CMF carefully and replace with ~30-50 ml prewarmed DTE
Incubate on a 37°C stir plate for 30 minutes
Pour contents into a 50 ml conical tube with cell strainer

Kidney, Salivary Gland (SG), Liver, Lung, and Fat Processing

Clean organs, remove fat and capsule
Cut into small pieces in a 50 ml conical tube
Add prewarmed collagenase solution:

Salivary Gland, Fat & Kidney: 10 ml
Liver: 20 ml
Lung: 5 ml

Incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C (1 hour for lung)
Mash through cell strainer

Percoll Gradient Separation
Proceed as follows for both IEL and other organ preparations:

Centrifuge at 1600 rpm for 4 minutes to pellet single cell suspension
Verify pellet formation, then carefully discard supernatant and wipe top of conical tube
Resuspend each sample in 5 ml of 44% Percoll solution, ensuring the pellet is well resuspended

For liver, prepare two Percoll gradients per sample

Place a glass Pasteur pipette in the conical tube and add 2 ml of 67% Percoll solution to the top of pipette to create a bottom layer. Do not disturb after adding!
Centrifuge at 21°C at 2000 rpm for 20 minutes, with acceleration set to 4 and brake to 0
Locate the interphase between the two Percoll layers and transfer it to a 15 ml conical tube (approximately 3 ml)
Fill the tube with PBS, mix by inverting and centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 5 minutes


Tip
Ensure thorough mixing when adding PBS, otherwise the interphase might remain intact


Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μl of RP-5 media

Cell Type Marked for Depletion






Example Volume










NK1.1






NK cells






3 µL








MHC Class II






APCs (B cells, Monos, DCs)






3 µL








CD4






Helper T cells






3 µL








B220 (CD45R)






B cells






3 µL








Ter119






Erythroid lineage cells






3 µL








Ly-6G/Ly-6C (Gr-1)






Granulocytes (Neutrophils)






3 µL








MACS buffer








600 µL







Note: This cocktail targets major non-CD8+ T cell populations. Adjust cocktail based on specific experimental needs or available antibodies.

Negative Selection Staining & Bead Incubation

Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 µL of the freshly prepared Biotinylated Antibody Cocktail (adjust volume based on cell number if necessary, typically ~100 µL per 10^7 cells).
Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C (in the fridge), protected from light.
Fill the tube with MACS buffer (~10-14 mL). Centrifuge at ~400 x g for 4 minutes. Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 µL MACS Buffer. Add 50 µL of streptavidin magnetic beads.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C, protected from light.
Fill the tube with MACS buffer. Centrifuge at ~400 x g for 4 minutes. Discard the supernatant. During centrifuge step, wash MACS column (e.g. LS column) in the magnet by rinsing with 3 ml of MACS buffer. Discard flow through. Don’t let filter dry so add more if needed during centrifuge step.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 µL MACS buffer.





Magnetic Column Separation

Apply the cell suspension onto the column.
Collect the unlabeled cells that pass through the column. This fraction contains the enriched, untouched CD8+ T cells.
Wash the column three times (3x) with 3 mL of MACS buffer each time. Collect these washes and combine them with the initial flow-through.
Centrifuge the collected flow-through at 1600 RPM for 4 minutes. Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the purified CD8+ T cell pellet in a small volume (e.g., 500 µL) of R10. Count the cells using a hemocytometer or automated counter. Determine cell viability (e.g., using Trypan Blue).
Stop here and check CD8 T cell purity by flow (pre and post isolation)

We had 89% purity post isolation of CD8 T cells and 44e6 cells total. Resuspend to 2e6 cells/ml. Plate 1 ml.

Run flow to check purity (can assume 90-95% if in a hurry but always better to flow check)
Stain aliquot of cells with FITC-CD8b (1:100)
Wash 1x with FACS and run on flow.






Cell Plating and Activation

Retrieve the GAH-IgG or anti-CD3 coated plate from the incubator. Carefully aspirate the coating solution from the wells.
Wash each well twice with 1 mL of R10 to remove any residual unbound antibody. Aspirate thoroughly after the final wash.
Dilute anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 antibodies each 1:500 in R10 for GAH-IgG coated wells. Dilute anti-CD28 for the anti-CD3 plate coated wells at 1:250 so there will be 1 ug/ml anti-CD28 in final well.
Add 1 ml of the CD8 T cell suspension (containing cells) to each prepared well.
Add 1 ml of the anti-CD3/CD28 antibody (or just anti-CD28) mixture to each well containing cells (total volume per well = 2 mL). Gently pipette up and down or swirl the plate to mix.

Final concentration: 1 x 106 cells/mL
Final antibody dilution: 1:1000 (effective concentration depends on stock)

Place the plate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 18-24 hours.

CRISPR/Cas9 knock out in primary T cells via electroporation

To make a Cas9/RNA complex, mix guides plus tracr RNA as below in PCR tubes:

gRNA thy1 guide only control
gRNA thy1 guide plus guide of 1st target (Dand5)
gRNA thy1 guide plus guide of 2nd target (Sulf2)
want to do 3:1 molar ratio of guide RNA to Cas9 enzyme.
Thy1 AC guide at 100uM concentration.
Experimental guides are at 100uM concentration.

Control (sgThy1 control wells + sgThy1 and expt control wells)

3uL thy1 AC crRNA guide from IDT (Box ‘Nicole’ at -20ºC)
3uL tracr RNA (Alt-R® CRISPR-Cas9 tracrRNA, ATTO™ 550) (Box ‘Nicole’ at -20ºC)

Experimental (x number of groups needed)

1.5uL thy1 AC crRNA guide from IDT
1.5uL guide of experimental guide (Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 crRNA from IDT)
3uL tracr RNA (Alt-R® CRISPR-Cas9 tracrRNA, ATTO™ 550)

Incubate in PCR machine at 95C for 5 minutes, then immediately remove at put at RT in the dark for 1 hour for annealing.

During this time, take 10mL of R10 plus 50U/ml hIL2 (a 1:2000 dilution), and put into a water bath to warm to 37deg.
Gather materials in hood such as strips, cytokines for supplemented media
Make cytokine mixes
Make the P3 + supplement 1 buffer and get to RT. Make a P3 buffer mix below per reaction and keep at room temperature.
1x buffer recipe, make enough for each rxn:

Supplement 1: 3.6uL (made enough for eight samples, 28.8 ul)
P3: 16.4uL (made enough for eight samples, 131.2 ul)


Add 1.9uL 40uM Cas9 enzyme to each tube of tracrRNA and guide RNA complex (-80’, middle shelf, middle rack). DO NOT MIX. Gently flick the tube to mix sgRNAs with Cas9 and spin down briefly to collect drops from the sides of the tube. Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature for complex formation.
Do during Cas9 incubation:

Count cells, then spin down cells in large volume (use 50 mL conical) of STERILE, RT PBS to remove potential RNase contamination from FCS containing media before electroporation (IMPORTANT). Can do 2-10x10^6 cells per reaction. *We did 2-6e6 per condition.
Turn on Lonza 4D-NucleofectorTM System: select wells, pulse code (see below) and solution (P3 primary).

Immediately after complex formation, transfer cells into Eppendorf tubes in 1 ml of PBS, and spin down on a tabletop centrifuge at 5000 RPM for 5min room temperature). It is important to prepare everything before resuspending the cells in P3 buffer to minimize the time that cells are exposed to the buffer.
Take supernatant from the cell pellet using pipets (make sure to take off all remaining liquid from cell pellet to not dilute out the small reaction volume of 25 μl). Resuspend cell pellet in 20μl P3 buffer per reaction.
Divide cells out per sample and then add respective guide RNA complexes. Remember to aliquot a sample for no guide RNA control here (just receives shock and no guide RNA mix- positive control for Thy1 knockout)
Transfer 5 μl of CRISPR/Cas9 RNP into the 20 μl P3 buffer with cells and mix gently.
Transfer the 25 μl cell/RNP mix to the bottom hole of a well of the Lonza nucleofector strip. Be careful to not create any bubbles. (keep time of cells in P3 buffer as short as possible as it is cytotoxic to the cells). Chip Orientation:

Open square: Top
Closed square: Bottom

Electroporate cells by putting the nucleofector strip into the Lonza nucleofector and as depicted, start the program

Naïve CD8 T cells: use DN100 program in P3 buffer
Activated CD8 T cells: use DS137 program in P3 buffer

After electroporation (a few seconds) add 130 μl of 37°C pre-warmed R10 media into the well containing electroporated cells and rest cells for 10 minutes in the incubator (5% CO2, 37°C).
In the meantime, prepare a 6-MW plates with R10 and IL-2 at 15 U/mL
Dilute 1:3.33 the leftover R10 + IL-2 (50 U/mL): 600 μL of R10+IL-2 with 1400 μL of R10 plain (final 15 U/mL). Fill outer wells with PBS/media.
Resuspend the cells in the electroporation well using a pipette, and transfer the cell suspension into a fresh tube or well. To recover any remaining cells, wash the electroporation well with an additional 150 μl R10 media by pipetting, and transfer the media into the same collection tube. Add 700 uL pre-warmed R10 to make 1 ml total. Distribute the control sgThy1 cells across however many wells (can pool 2-3 wells into one cuvette and redistribution after electroporation). For that step, you omit the 700 ul and distribute 300 ul to well if one well -> one electroporation strip well or distribute 100 ul to each well if three wells -> one electroporation strip well
Count the cells with Trypan Blue as 20-50% of T cells will be lost during the electroporation step.
For in vivo adoptive transfer, resuspend in PBS at desired concentration and adoptively transfer into recipient mice via intravenous injection. Keep some cells going in culture for future flow and KO validation with flow or Sanger sequencing.
For cells in culture, split the cells over the original number of cells they were into (e.g., if three wells were originally pooled to do CRISPR on, then split them back into the original 3 wells) for culture
Incubate for overnight/24 hrs
Count cells prior to replacing media, replenish cytokines every 48 hours

sgThy1 1: 1.29e6 cells total
sgThy1 2: 1.62e6 cells total
sgThy1 + sgDand5: 1.65e6 cells total
sgThy1 + sgSulf2: 1.35e6 cells total

Replace IL2 media with Trm polarization media to some wells or replenish IL2 controls by spinning cells and replacing media as follows:

IL2 replenishment: (25 U/ml IL2)
Trm polarization media: 25 U/ml IL2, 10ng/ml IL15, 10 ng/ml TGFb, 10 nM RA)
IL2 stock: 100,000 U/ml so dilute 1:100 then add 25 ul per ml to get 25 U/ml
IL15 stock: 10 ug/ml so dilute 1:1000 (1 ul per ml) to get to 10 ng/ml
TGFb stock: 0.2 mg/ml so dilute 1:20,000 total or 1:200 then add 10 ul per ml to get to 10 ng/ml.
RA: 0.0015g/ml so dilute 1:1000 then 2 ul per ml to get to 20 nM

Incubate for 48 hours. 72 hours post electroporation, transfer cells to Eppendorf tubes.
Spin at 2000 RPM for 5 min and collect supernatant by pipetting off sup avoiding cells and save at -80 for ELISA.
Collect cells for flow, PCR of genomic DNA for Sanger sequencing validation of knockout, and for RNA extraction -> cDNA synthesis for qPCR validation of knockout.

title: RNA extraction & cDNA synthesis & RT-qPCR from CD8
text:
RNA extraction, cDNA synthesis, and RT-qPCR
Qiagen RNAeasy mini kit- Cell lysis and spin column

If purifying RNA from cell lines rich in RNases, or tissue, add either 10 µL β-mercaptoethanol (β-ME), or 20 µL 2 M dithiothreitol (DTT), to 1 mL Buffer RLT. Buffer RLT with β-ME or DTT can be stored at room temperature for up to 1 month.
Preassemble RNeasy® Mini spin columns with Waste Tubes (provided).
Make sure the ethanol has been added to buffer prior to starting
Harvest a maximum of 1e7 cells, as a cell pellet or by direct lysis in the vessel.
Add 350 ul of Buffer RLT supplemented with BME and pipette vigorously to disrupt the cell pellet. Can pause and freeze at -80 at this step. Keep cold.
If you freeze cells in RLT buffer, thaw at 37C quickly.
Apply 350 ul of cells/RLT buffer to a Qiashredder and spin at max speed for 2 min
Add 1 volume (350 ul if used 350 ul RLT lysis buffer) of 70% ethanol to the 350 ul of RLT that passed through the Qiashredder.
Mix well by pipetting, do not centrifuge.
Transfer up to 700 µL of the sample, including any precipitate, to a RNeasy Mini spin column placed in a 2 mL waste tube (supplied). Close the lid, and centrifuge for 15 s at ≥8000 x g. Discard the flow-through and reuse the waste tube.

Dnase digestion
Follow steps 1–4 of “Appendix D: Optional On Column DNase Digestion with the RNase Free DNase” in the QIAwave RNA Mini Handbook if using cultured cells to remove genomic DNA. These steps are:

Prepare DNase I stock solution before using kit for first time by dissolving lyophilized DNase I in 550 ul of RNase-free water. Do not open vial, inject water into vial using needle and syringe. Mix gently by inverting. Do not vortex. Let sit at RT for 10 min to dissolve.
For long-term storage, aliquot and store at -20. Do not refreeze aliquots.
After the sample has been spun through the RNeasy mini spin column, add 350 ul of buffer RW1 to the spin column. Close lid gently and centrifuge for 15 s at 8000g to wash column. Discard flowthrough
Add 10 ul of DNase I stock solution made above to 70 ul of buffer RDD for each sample. We made 800 ul total- 100 ul of DNase I and 700 ul of buffer RDD for 8 samples. Mix stock by inverting tube and centrifuge briefly to collect residual liquid from sides of tube. Do not vortex!
Add 80 ul of DNase I mix directly to RNeasy spin column membrane and incubate at RT for 15 min. Make sure to add DNase incubation mix directly to column membrane as digestion will be incomplete if it sticks to the column membrane.

Column wash and RNA elution

Add 350 ul of buffer RW1 to RNeasy spin column. Close lid gently, centrifuge for 15 sec at 8000xg. Discard flow through.
Add 500 ul of buffer RPE to spin column. Close lid gently, centrifuge for 15 sec at 8000xg. Discard flow through.
Add 500 ul of buffer RPE to spin column. Close lid gently, centrifuge for 15 sec at 8000xg. Discard flow through.
Place spin column in a new collection tube and spin at full speed for 1 min to dry membrane.
Place spin column in a new 1.5 ml collection tube with lid and add 30 ul of rNase free water directly to spin column membrane. Close lid, centrifuge for 1 min at 8000xg to elute RNA. If low amount of RNA, can incubate at RT for 3 min prior to 1 min spin.
For second elution step, add 30 ul of eluted RNA in step 10 back onto the column to increase RNA yield. Remember to incubate at RT for 3 min again before spin.

cDNA synthesis – Applied Bio High Capacity cDNA reverse transcriptase

Allow kit components to thaw on ice
Calculate the volume needed to prepare the fllowing reactions on ice
Prepare 2x reverse transcription master mix and place on ice when done. Make sure to make a no RT control where you don’t add reverse transcriptase and just add water to see how much junk there is.



10x RT buffer: 2 ul per 10 ul reaction
25x dNTP mix (100 mM): 0.8 ul per 10 ul reaction
10x RT random primers: 2 ul per 10 ul reaction
Multiscribe reverse transcriptase: 1 ul per 10 ul reaction
Nuclease-free H20: 4.2 ul per 10 ul reaction



Mix 2x mix gently
Pipette 10 ul of 2x RT master mix into each well/PCR tube
Pipette 10 ul of RNA sample into each well/tube. Pipette up and down to mix
Seal plate/tubes
Briefly centrifuge tubes to spin down contents and eliminate air bubbles
Place plate/tubes on ice until ready to load in thermal cycler.

Thermal cycler settings: Step 1: 25C for 10 min. Step 2: 37C for 120 min. Step 3: 85C for 5 min. Step 4: 4C for hold

Set reaction volume to 20 ul
Load and start run.

Flow to check for Thy1 knockout


Move cells from culture plate to v-bottom 96 well plate for flow


Wash 1x with FACS


Resuspend in 50 ul of master mix for 20 min at 4C



L/D APC-Cy7 (1:1000)


CD8b FITC (1:100)


Thy1.2 BV510 (1:100)



Wash 2x with FACS


Flow


qPCR
From this point onwards, work on ice.
Primer Dilution Prep

Determine how much primer is needed in qPCR reaction (1.25 ul FWD, 1.25 ul RVS primer per 1x master mix)
Dilute primers 1:5 in nuclease-free water
Vortex briefly and spin down each tube. These are your working primer solutions.

qPCR Reaction Setup
Prepare Reaction Mix:

Calculate the number of reactions needed per gene target (samples + controls + extras for pipetting error).
Prepare a master mix for each gene target (Target Gene and Housekeeping Gene) separately to ensure consistency. For N reactions, mix the following in a fresh tube:

SYBR Green Master Mix (2x): 12.5 μl * N
Respective Diluted Primer Mix: 1.25 μl * N
Nuclease-free water: (27 – MM which is 15 ul) = 12 ul ddH20

Vortex the master mix gently and spin down.
Aliquot 27 μl of the appropriate master mix into each well of your qPCR plate/tube.
Dilute cDNA samples 1:5 with nuclease-free water (3 ul of cDNA with 12 ul H2O)
Add 3 μl of cDNA sample to the corresponding wells. For NTC wells, add 3 μl of nuclease-free water instead of cDNA. Total reaction volume per well: 30 μl. For the no RT wells, add samples prepared in cDNA synthesis step and master mix. Total reaction volume per well: 30 ul.
Seal the qPCR plate/tubes securely. Briefly centrifuge the plate/tubes to collect the contents at the bottom of the wells and remove air bubbles.

qPCR Instrument Run

Place the plate/tubes into the qPCR machine.
Use Angelica’s standard SYBR Green protocol suitable for your master mix and instrument. A typical protocol is:

Initial Denaturation: 95°C for 2-10 minutes (check master mix recommendations)
Cycling (e.g., 40 cycles):

Denaturation: 95°C for 10-30 seconds
Annealing/Extension: 60-65°C for 30-60 seconds (ensure fluorescence data acquisition at this step)

Melt Curve Analysis: Standard melt curve program (e.g., 95°C for 15s, 60°C for 60s, then ramp slowly to 95°C with continuous fluorescence acquisition). This helps check for primer dimers or non-specific amplification.
Optimization: Cycling conditions, especially the annealing/extension temperature and time, may need optimization based on the specific primers, target sequence, and master mix used. Primer efficiency should ideally be validated.


Data Analysis
This describes the common Livak method (ΔΔCt).

Obtain Ct Values: Export the cycle threshold (Ct) values for all samples and controls for both the Target Gene and Housekeeping Gene from the qPCR software.

Validate Controls: Ensure NTCs show no or very late amplification (e.g., Ct > 35). Check No RT controls for minimal signal compared to cDNA samples.
Check Melt Curves: Verify single, specific peaks at the expected melting temperature for each gene.

Calculate ΔCt (Delta Ct) for each sample: Normalize the Ct value of the Target Gene to the Ct value of the Housekeeping Gene for each sample. ΔCt = Ct(Target Gene) - Ct(Housekeeping Gene)
Select a Control/Reference Sample: Choose one sample (or the average of a control group) as the reference calibrator (e.g., untreated sample, time point zero).
Calculate ΔΔCt (Delta-Delta Ct): Calculate the difference between the ΔCt of each sample and the ΔCt of the reference/calibrator sample. ΔΔCt = ΔCt(Sample) - ΔCt(Reference Sample)
Calculate Relative Expression Fold Change: Calculate the fold change in gene expression for each sample relative to the reference sample using the formula:


Note
If you calculate ΔCt as Ct(Housekeeping Gene) - Ct(Target Gene), the final formula becomes . Ensure consistency in your calculations.


Interpretation & Further Analysis: The calculated Relative Expression value represents the fold change in the target gene’s expression in a given sample compared to the reference sample, after normalization to the housekeeping gene.

Step 1: Open the Completed Run File

Open the CFX Maestro or CFX Manager software on the computer connected to your system.
Click on the View Post-Run Data tab or go to File > Open > Data File.
Select your completed .pcrd run file and click Analyze Data.

Step 2: View and Format the Data Sheets

By default, the software opens to the Quantification tab (showing your standard thermal cycling curves).
Click on the Melt Curve tab next to it.
Look at the lower half of the screen to find the data spreadsheets associated with that tab. You will see tabs like Melt Peaks, RFU Spreadsheet, and -d(RFU)/dT Spreadsheet. 

Step 3: Export All Data Sheets to Excel
The absolute fastest way to get all your thermal cycle and melt curve matrices at once is to export the entire workbook:

In the main top menu bar of the software, click on Export.
From the dropdown menu, select Export All Data Sheets to Excel.
Choose a destination folder (such as a USB drive or local directory), name your file, and click Save.

title: Caspase 3_7&7AAD ex vivo staining
text:
Caspase 3/7 & 7AAD Staining
Staining prep

Transfer the cells and supernatant to flow tubes
Wash wells 1x with media.
Combine samples for controls.
Spin down at 1200rpm for 5min.
Resuspend in 200uL and transfer into a 96 well round bottom plate for staining.
Spin plate down at 1200rpm for 5 min. Flick.

Surface staining for surface panel

CD4-PB (1:100)
CD14/19- BV510 (1:200)
Thy1.1- BV711 (1:100)
PD-1- BV786 (1:200)
CD8- PE (1:100)
FCGRIIB/STREP-APC (1:200)
CD44- APC-Cy7 (1:300)
Leave FITC and PerCP open for caspase and 7AAD

Caspase/7AAD staining
*As caspase/7AAD stain does not get washed out, cells continue to stain even after the incubation. Therefore, make sure all your comps and experiment are set up on the cytometer so you can directly run your samples. If this is not possible, incubate the samples in caspase and 7AAD stain in shifts (e.g. one tissue type at a time) as staining will continue and your last samples will be more stained than the first run ones. This is a technical difference and you could mistake it for biological.

Thaw caspase reagent.
Resuspend wells in 50 ul of counting beads and move to FACS tubes.
Make sure heat block is at correct temp. Heat block positive controls for 5 min at 95C.
Make 1:1000 stock solution of caspase (1 ul per 1 ml of FACS) and add 50 ul into sample (1:2000 final dilution—I promise!) Add to all samples except FMO.
When positive controls/comps are done on the heat block, add 50 ul of caspase solution and incubate tubes at 37C for 20 min.
Make 7AAD solution (1:500 dilution) and add 100 ul of 7AAD into 100 ul of solution caspase+cells, making a final dilution of 1:1000.
Let incubate for 5 min in drawer in dark at RT. Then go to flow!

Trypsin and count cells
Resuspend cells at 5e6/ml in cold PBS
Filter cells over a 100 um filter
Count cells
Add PBS to get to 3.5e6 cells/ml
Bring cancer cells on ice to mouse room
Shave mice
Inject 500k cells in 100 ul into mice subcutaneously- use other flank if PBS bleeds out

Day 7
P14 transfer

Harvest four spleens from P14 mice.
Homogenize spleen over 70 um filter
Centrifuge at 1600 RPM for 4 min and dump
Resuspend pellet in 1-2 ml ACK and incubate at room temp for 5-6 min
Neutralize with 3-4 ml of media
Take aliquot for flow
Wash aliquot 1x with FACS
Stain aliquot with surface stain master mix for 20 min at 4C

CD8b- BV510
CD45.1- BV786
CD45.2- FITC
VA2- PE

While aliquots are staining, count cells

7.74e6/ml, 40 ml, 75% viability
309 million cells from four spleens, 75% viability

At end of stain, wash cells 2x with FACS
Take to flow
Take lymphocytes 🡪 then frequency of Va2 in CD8b/CD45.1+ gate and calculate what percentage of CD8b+Va2+ of cells

0.95 (Va2)* 35% CD8b+CD45.1+ of (singlets 🡪lymphocytes) gate
0.33 * 309e6 = 101e6 P14

For cancer cell inoculation, calculate cell counts to reach 5e6 cells/ml and inject 1e6 cells in 200 ul per mouse via RO injection.
When injecting, remember to go at a 45-60 degree angle and go to the tear duct and angle behind the eye. You usually start to angle the needle down which does not work- remember to go in at an angle!
Measure tumors

Day 9, 13, 17, 21

Treat mice with 100 ug of the following antibody groups:

Anti-PD1
Anti-PD1 isotype (Rat IgG2a)
Anti-CTLA4
Anti-CTLA4 isotype (Syrian Hamster IgG)
Anti-PD1 + Anti-CTLA4
Dual isotype

Antibodies are resuspended in -80 at 1 mg/ml, so take 2 vials of each since I need to treat about 7 mice per group and each antibody is needed 2x.
Inject intraperitoneally 100 ul of 1 mg/ml (100 ug)
Measure tumor and record on IACUC sheet
crumbs: AntiPD1_CTLA4 in vivo blockade in B16-challenged mice

title: Making bone marrow chimeras
text:
Bone marrow chimeras
You will need ~20 million bone marrow cells to inject for each recipient mouse. Plan out congenic backgrounds so you will be able to distinguish recipient from donor mouse cells.
Day -1

Make low pH, antibiotic water for irradiated mice.

Add 2L of tap water to autoclaveable bottle.
Add ~0.48mL HCl and shake.
Dip pH indicator strip into bottle and adjust pH to be between 2.5 and 3.5 (pH ~3.0)
Autoclave on liquid setting for at least 20min.
Add 25mg (1.25mL of bottle in 4°) Polymyxin B and 1g Neomycin to the water after its cooled to touch.
Store water with foil in refrigerator.


Day 0

Irradiate bone marrow recipients two times with 4.5 Gy SIX HOURS APART. Each time, this is what the settings should be: 225 kV 17.7 mA config radpls pie, shelf 1, 4.5 Gy, 2 min 46 seconds

*This dose was optimized to yield 100% mouse survival and 85-95% chimerism.
Bone marrow recipient animals

Pepboy CD45.1+ Thy1.2+

Bone marrow donor animals

Fgl2-/- HSCs, CD45.2+ Thy1.2+
WT HSCs, CD45.2+ Thy1.2+



Euthanize the donor mice: 8 Fgl2-/- mice, 10 B6 mice
Spray the donor mice with 70 % ethanol and cut the abdominal skin, peel down over legs.
Remove the feet and harvest femur and tibia, scraping away muscle.
Transfer the legs to cold PBS.
Remove excess flesh from the leg bone using scissors and forceps and gauze.
Cut off the ends of the bones, and place the bones in PBS
Once all bones are collected, transfer to petri dishes with 10mL media.
Flush the bones using a 23-gauge needle for the tibia and 21 gauge for the femur with a 10 ml syringe. Refilling with petri dish PBS or fresh PBS as needed.
Once finished (bones should look white with no red in them), make a single-cell suspension of all the marrow and filter using a 70um filter. Wash each side of the petri dish 1-2x with PBS. Use another 50 ml conical for the washes. Count both tubes.
Pool cells from all mice and count cells.



Spin and filter once more. Resuspend to 40 million cells/ml (20 million cells per 500 ul per mouse adoptive transfer)
Inject 500ul of bone marrow cell suspension i.v through penile vein. If using retroorbital, resuspend so there are 20 million cells per 250 ul per mouse adoptive transfer.

Day 0 – Week 8

Allow mice to recover in sterile cages in sterile room with 150 mls antibiotic water
Replace antibiotic water 2x a week.
Six weeks post transplantation, recipient mice can be analyzed for the presence of donor-derived cells via flow cytometry.

Week 6 & 8

Bleed mice with 5mm lances, fill heparinized capillaries and dump in 5mL FACS tube with 4mL lysis buffer.
Spin tubes down, aspirate supernatant and add 4mL lysis buffer and resuspend.
Spin tubes down again, aspirate supernatant and transfer all volume to 96-well round bottom plate.
Add to 300uL with lysis buffer, and transfer 40uL to isotype well (combine so one isotype well per cage).
Spin plate down, flick.
Resuspend in 50uL antibody master mix.



CD4- PB (1:100)
CD8- PO (1:100)
CD3- BV786 (1:200)
CD45.1- FITC (1:100)
CD45.2- PE-Cy7 (1:100)
CD19- PerCP (1:100)
Fgl2- PE (1:300)
CD11b- APC (1:200)



Incubate at 4C for 30 minutes.
Wash 1x with 200uL FACS buffer.
Resuspend in 75uL FACS buffer, transfer to microtubes, flow.

NOTE: All BM transferred (including CD8 T cells) should be CD45.2; none should be CD45.1, in both WT and KO recipients.

title: Reporter-gene transduction of P14 into LCMV Armstrong infected mice for tissue embedding
text:
Reporter-gene transduction of P14 into LCMV Armstrong infected mice for tissue embedding
CD8 Selection and activation (GFP, tdTomato, mCherry, Ametrine plasmids)
Day 1

Dilute GAH IgG antibody 1:30 in sterile PBS
Aliquot 550 ul/ well in a 6 well plate. Distribute antibody + PBS across the wells
Incubate plate at 37C for 2 hours
Harvest spleen from P14 mice and homogenize over 70 um filter
Centrifuge at 1600 RPM for 4 min and dump
Resuspend pellet in 1-2 ml ACK and incubate at room temp for 5-6 min
Neutralize with 3-4 ml MACS
Count cells

125 million cells

Centrifuge at 1600 RPM for 4 min and aspirate supernatant
Add 40 ul MACS buffer for every 10 million cells

500 ul

Add 10 ul CD8 antibody biotin cocktail for every 10 million cells

125 ul antibody cocktail

Mix well
Incubate at 4C for 5 min
Add 30 ul MACS buffer for every 10 million cells

375 ul buffer

Add 20 ul biotin micro beads for every 10 million cells

250 ul beads

Mix well
Incubate at 4C for 10 min
Rinse LS column by adding 3 mls of MACS buffer when incubation step in step 17 has a few minutes left
Apply single cell suspension to column (avoid getting on edge of column)
If less than 500 ul, complete to 500 ul before adding to column
Collect flow through as this represents the unlabeled CD8 fraction (biotin antibodies label all other cells besides CD8 in this negative selection kit)
Wash column with 3 mls of MACS and combine with eluent in step 22
Count cells in this fraction- these are your CD8!

35 million cells

Dilute cells to 2e6 cells/ml

17.5 mls

Wash GAH-ab coated wells 2x with 1 ml TCM
Plate 2e6 cells in 1 ml TCM
Dilute anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 antibodies 1:500 in TCM
Stock concentration of anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 is 1 mg/ml, final should be 1 ug/ml (adding 2 ug/ml because diluted 2x)
Add 1 ml CD3/28 antibody mix to each well, pipette to mix
Incubate at 37C for 24 hours

Day 2
Retroviral transduction of P14

Prewarm centrifuge to 37C
Thaw virus in water bath
Make polybrene mix (70x). For 100 ul of viral solution use:

8 ul polybrene
10 ul BME
82 ul OptiMEM

Combine virus + polybrene mix. For 140 ul virus, add 2 ul polybrene mix (e.g. 2 ml virus, add 28.5 ul polybrene mix)
Transfer media from 6 well into 15 ml conicals, keep warm and separate between P14 backgrounds
Add virus mix to activated T cells
Spin at 37C for 1 hr, 2000RPM
Incubate plate at 37C 1-4 hours
Carefully remove virus mix
Spin down old media from step 5 and add same amount of fresh TCM (total volume is 4 mls per well in the end)
Incubate for 24 hours at 37C

Day 3

Perform sort

Use the following gating strategy to calculate number of P14 to adoptively transfer




Singlets Lymphocytes CD8/VA2 CD8/fluorescent marker

Can check for transduction efficiency using CD8/GFP/Ametrine for single AT but do not only use transduced cells in your calculation

Singlets Lymphocytes CD8 CD8/GFP/Ametrine Thy1.1/Thy1.2 for co-AT



Count cells after sort

GFP- 1.31e6 cells/ml, 1.5 ml, 86%
mCherry- 1.02e6 cells/ml, 1.5 ml, 77%
tdtomato- 8.46e5 cells/ml, 1.5 ml, 67%
Ametrine- 1.11e6 cells/ml, 1.5 ml, 83%

Dilute cells to 1e6/ml

GFP- add 450 ul
mCherry- add 130 ul
Ametrine- add 160 ul
Tdtomato- add nothing

Transfer 5e5 cells to mice via IV
Dilute LCMV Armstrong from stock of 4.58e7 PFU/ml by making a 1:45.8 dilution, 2e5 PFU/mouse in 200 ul, keep on ice

For 15 mice, mix 66 ul stock with 2.934 ml of PBS

Drop off samples in 249
Change into BSL2 clothes
Infect mice with diluted Armstrong with IP injection after mice have been given T cells via retroorbital or tail vein injection (~1 hr)
Use 5% in isoflurane chamber, keep line parallel in original position

Day 7 sac and spleen harvest for preparation for FFPE embedding for Xenium
  
Materials: 

6 well plate, 1.5mL epi, 15 mL conical 
Pre-chilled 1x PBS 
Ice 
Cold 10% NBF (Sigma Aldrich HT501128) 
Scissors, forceps 



Set shaker incubator to 4 degrees 
Prep 10 mls of 10% NBF in each tube for spleen
Prep 3 mls of ACK lysis in each tube for blood
Add cold 1x PBS to 6-well plates (one well/spleen) on ice to preserve tissues after harvesting 
Put PBS and 70% EtOH in fridge for Day 2 
Bleed mice under iso and collect blood in ACK lysis buffer

Surface stain mix

CD8b- BV786
CD45.1- BUV805
CD45.2- PE-Cy7
Keep BV510, FITC, PE, PE-CF594 open for fluorescent dyes


Put spleen in cold PBS in 6 well plate
After spleen is rinsed, add spleen to 10 ml of cold 10% NBF while still in mouse room
Incubate for 24 hours in shaker incubator (set to 4 degrees) 

Day 1 post fixation/tissue harvest
Materials: 

Pre-chilled 70% ethanol 
Pre-chilled PBS 



Remove tissue from NBF and wash with cold PBS twice 
After spleen is rinsed, add spleen to 10 ml of cold 70% EtOH while still in mouse room
Incubate for 24 hours in shaker incubator (set to 4 degrees) 
Can put tissue in cassette in a 50 ml conical or just in a conical with 10 mls of 70% EtOH. Before sending for embedding, make sure sample has been in 70% EtOH for at least 24 hours.

title: Human tumor sample collection, processing, and flow analysis
text:
TUMOR TISSUE PROCESSING
Sample ID:________ Patient ID:________
Collection Date/Time:________ Processing Date/Time:________
Processing Scientist Initials:_______
SAMPLE PREPARATION

Ideally at least one week prior to collection, identify samples and ensure sufficient amounts of antibody. Book flow time on cytometer for the day of processing
Day before or day of tissue collection, prepare 50mL conical tube with 25mL RPMI/10%FBS/1% Pen-Strep. If multiple samples, prepare multiple tubes (for both collection, as well as processing and flow steps below)
Record mass of tissue at time of collection, and record




POST-COLLECTION MASS OF TUBE (g): _______________


MASS OF FLOW TISSUE (g):_______________


SAMPLE PROCESSING

Prepare enzymatic processing tube: 50mL conical containing 4.7mL RPMI-1640 (no FBS/Pen-Strep, or L-Glut) + 200 µL Enzyme H + 100 µL Enzyme R + 25 µL Enzyme A (Tumor Dissociation Kit from Miltenyi).
Remove tissue from 50mL collection conical tube and place into petri dish, and dissect into small pieces using scalpel or sterile scissors. Transfer sample into gentleMACS “C Tube” using the enzymatic solution, making sure to transfer all tissue.
Tightly close tube, attach it upside down into one of the two sleeves on the gentleMACS dissociator (either sleeve may be used). Make sure tumor samples are near the rotor/stator and not adhered to the upper walls of the tube. Ensure tube is seated properly. You should hear and feel a “click” when the tube is properly attached.
Run gentleMACS program “h_tumor_01”.
Detach tube. Incubate for 30 minutes at 37ºC with continuous rotation. If tube rotator is not available, manually rotate/agitate tube every ~5 minutes.
Attach tube to gentleMACS dissociator, run program “h_tumor_01” (second time doing this).
Detach tube. Incubate for 30 minutes at 37ºC with continuous rotation. If tube rotator is not available, manually rotate/agitate tube every ~5 minutes.
Attach tube to gentleMACS dissociator, run program “h_tumor_01” (third time doing this).
Using sterile RPMI-1640, resuspend sample/wash out of C tube and cap, strain through a 70 µm filter and wash with ~20ml media.
Should have a (mostly) single cell suspension free of chunks of tissue. Centrifuge at 300xg for 5 minutes.
Resuspend sample in FACS buffer and aliquot sample to appropriate flow tubes for downstream staining. Proceed to flow staining as below.


TUMOR IMMUNE CELL ANALYSIS
Surface stain


Centrifuge samples for 5min at 300xg, and gently remove supernatant.
Resuspend samples in surface antibody solutions.
Incubate samples for 30min on ice in the dark.
Wash samples with 250μl FACS buffer, spin down 5min at 300xg, and gently remove supernatant.

Fixation, Permeabilization and Cytokine/TF staining

Resuspend cells with 100μL of eBioscience transcription factor fixation buffer per well, and incubate 30min. on ice in dark.
Prepare solution of 1x PermWash by diluting 10x PermWash to 1x in sterile H2O. Add 100μl 1x PermWash to each sample, spin down 5min at 300xg, and gently remove supernatant.
Wash cells with 100µl 1x PermWash, spin 5min. at 300xg, gently remove supernatant.
Add intracellular staining solutions as follows, and incubate 60min at room temperature in the dark.
While samples are incubating with intracellular stain, prepare individual compensation controls using eBioscience UltraComp eBeads with individual antibodies from lymphocyte panel, as well as unstained beads. Also prepare Sphero Rainbow beads (drop of positive and negative beads + 200μl FACS buffer). Rainbow beads are especially important to maintain consistency across donors and across collection timepoints.
Add 150µl 1x PermWash, spin down 5min at 300xg, gently remove supernatant.
Resuspend samples in 250μl FACS buffer, and transfer to flow tubes.
Flow samples

RUNNING AND ANALYSIS OF FLOW DATA

For all populations (lymphocyte, Treg, and myeloid), gate on singlets (FSC-A x FSC-H), cellular events (FSC-A x SSC-A), live events (Ghost Dye780 x SSC-A), dump negative events (Mouse CD8-FITC x SSC-A), and CD45+ events (CD45-PE-Cy7 x SSC-A).
After isolating CD45+ cells, go through and evaluate panels using individual analysis


LYMPHOCYTE PANEL:
CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, CD19+ B cells, NK cells (CD3- CD56+), and NK-T cells (CD3+ CD56+). We will then evaluate markers of T cell memory (CD45RO and CD26), T cell activation/exhaustion (PD-1 and TIM-3), as well as a PD-1 responsive stem-like population of CD8+ T cells (HLA-DR+ CD38+ Ki67+).
Treg PANEL:
To evaluate regulatory T cell populations, samples will be stained with CD45, CD3, CD4, CD25, GITR, CD127, and Foxp3
MYELOID PANEL:
CD45, CD11b, CD11c, CD14, CD15, CD16, CD33, CD40, CD103, HLA-DR, and will also be evaluated for expression of PD-L1.


Monocytes (CD11b+ CD11c+ CD14+ CD16lo HLA-DR+)
Macrophages (CD11b+ CD11c+ CD33+ CD14- CD16+ M1 macrophages and CD11b+ CD11c+ CD33+ CD14+ CD16+ M2 macrophages),
Dendritic cells (CD11c+ CD14+ CD16- CD103+ HLA-DR+, with CD40 expression used to identify activated DCs),
Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (CD11b+ HLA-DRlo/neg CD33+ CD14+ CD15- monocyte MDSC and CD11bb+ HLA-DRlo/neg CD33+ CD14+ CD15+ granulocytic MDSC),
Neutrophils (SSChi CD11b+ CD14lo/neg HLA-DR- CD14+ CD15+ CD16hi CD11+)
Eosinophils (SSChi HLA-DR- CD15+ CD16-).

title: Human PBMC Ex vivo Dynabead multiday stim_prolif&apoptosis
text:
Ex vivo anti-CD3/28 Dynabead stim of human PBMC to measure proliferation and apoptosis
Donor Vial info:
PBMC cell count:
If using fresh PBMC:
PBMC isolation from whole blood in CPT tube

Invert CPT tube 2-4 times
Centrifuge CPTs at 1800 G for 30 minutes at room temperature, 9-1 acceleration/deceleration (handle with care and keep tubes upright after centrifuging). 
Remove plasma layer being careful not to disrupt cell layer (cloudy layer between CPT gel and plasma).   
Pour remaining plasma and cells from CPT tubes into a 50 mL Falcon tube 


NOTE:  No more than 6 CPTs per 50mL Falcon tube, if you have more than 6 divide them evenly into 2 or more Falcon tubes (they can be combined at the lyse step). 


Rinse CPTs 2-3x using ≈ 7mL of RPMI by pipetting up and down.
Dispense each wash from the CPTs into the 50 mL Falcon tube along with the cells in step 4
Bring Falcon tube volume up to 50 mL using RPMI 
Centrifuge at 1500RPM for 5 minutes at RT, aspirate the supernatant, mechanically disrupt pellet by raking
Resuspend cells in 10 ml High Yield Lyse (Thermofisher) and incubate at RT for 10 mins.
Bring volume up to 50 mL using RPMI, mixing gently. 



Centrifuge at 1500RPM for 5 minutes at RT, aspirate the supernatant, mechanically disrupt pellet by raking, resuspend in 2 mL to count cells. Cell count: average dilution 1:5 in 4% trypan blue (80ul trypan plus 20uL cells)

If using frozen PBMC:
Thawing cryopreserved PBMC for immunophenotyping
Protocol modified from here: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6060642/

Place a cryopreserved PBMC vial in a 37°C water bath. Submerge the cryovial halfway and thaw for 60 seconds.
PBMCs were frozen at 6-7 million cells in 1ml of freezing medium for 1 min.
Add 1 mL of warmed (37°C) complete RPMI slowly dropwise to the thawed PBMCs against the side of the cryovial using a transfer pipette.
Pipette the thawed PBMCs into 5 mL (per vial so 10 ml if thawing two vials) of complete RPMI in a 15ml conical tube that has been warmed to 37°C (no pipetting). Make sure to wipe down the tube
Rinse the cryovials once with 1 mL of warm complete RPMI, pipette the PBMCs into the conical tube with the cell mixture.
Incubate the PBMCs for 5 minutes in the 37°C water bath.
Take aliquot to count cells.

Cell Count Pre-Rest:

Centrifuge the PBMCs for 10 minutes at 300xg at room temperature.
Pour off the supernatant. This will leave a small amount of complete RPMI behind that aids in pellet resuspension.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed complete RPMI. Mix by flicking or racking the tube (avoid pipetting up and down).
Incubate the PBMCs for one hour at 37°C in a CO2 water jacketed incubator (37°C, 5% CO2, 95% humidity). Leave the cap of the conical tube slightly loose so that gas transfer can occur.
Centrifuge the PBMCs for 10 minutes at 300xg at room temperature.
Resuspend in complete RPMI to 10e6/ml.
Take aliquot to count cells

Cell Count Post-Rest: 9.9e5/ml. 97% viability. 2.47e6 cells total.
Anti-CD3/28 Dynabead stimulation


Prepare CD3/CD28 beads (Invitrogen Dynabeads Human T-Activator CD3/CD28) 


Vortex 30 seconds 


Add beads to 1.5 mL conical (15 ul per 1 ml sample in manufacturer protocol)


Add 1 mL FACS 


Vortex 30 seconds 


Place on magnet 1-2 minute 


Remove supernatant


Add equal parts R10 to the bead volume used in step 4 (resulting concentration beads to R10 ratio is 1:1)


Add media to well of 48 well plate, correct up to 1 ml (1 ml – 100 ul cells – 15 ul beads = 885 ul of media


Plate 1-1.2 million cells in 100 ul into R10 in 48 well plate *Easier on cells to add media first then cells then beads*


Add washed beads to cells in media in 48 well plate. 15ul of anti-CD3/28 beads per well of 1 ml media.


Add protein, antibody of interest or PBS as a control to respective wells.


Incubate 1-3 days


After Stimulation cell processing and surface staining

Pipette up and down thoroughly to resuspend cells and transfer to flow tubes and place on magnet 1-2 min to remove Dynabeads 
Aspirate supernatant (including cells; leaving beads behind) and transfer to clean flow tubes 
Wash flow tubes still containing beads by washing well in 48 well plate with 500 ul of FACS, then transfer FACS used to wash well into the respective tube on the magnet
Take tube off magnet, vortex, and put the tube back on the magnet and let sit on magnet for 1-2 min 
Repeat steps 3-4 once more
Aspirate the supernatant while tube is still on the magnet as in step 2 and add supernatant to appropriate flow tubes already containing cells debeaded in step 2.
Discard tubes containing CD3/CD28 beads 
Spin flow tubes with cells at 1500 RPM for 5 min 
Dump supernatant, wash in 1 ml of FACS, and dump supernatant 
Add master mix. Ab at 1:100
Stain all samples in surface antibody cocktail at room temp for 20 minutes, covered in foil. Make comps and FMOs during this time.
Add 1 ml of FACS, spin, dump supernatant. Repeat.

Live/Dead staining

Stain each sample with 1 ml live dead (1 ul L/D Aqua per 1 ml PBS)

LIVE/DEAD™ Fixable Aqua Dead Cell Stain Kit, for 405 nm excitation Thermofisher, L34965 *Live/dead stain is on same channel as CD14, CD19 to serve as a dump channel on BV510*

Incubate at room temp for 10 mins, covered in foil.
Wash 1x with FACS

Ki67 staining

Make fixation buffer (1:3 fix to diluent)
Add 250uL/sample. Fix perm= 5mL fix, 15mL diluent
Incubate for 20min at 4C in dark.
At end of fixation incubation, wash 1x with 1X perm buffer (1:10 dilution with diH20)
Stain with nuclear fluorochromes for 25-30 min at 4C in dark in perm buffer.
Wash 1X with perm buffer. Wash 1X with FACS.
Resuspend samples in 100uL FACS, transfer to microtubes, and flow.

Caspase staining

Caspase staining cannot be performed on fixed cells. If performing intracellular staining, do not perform caspase staining.
Thaw caspase 3/7 reagent (CellEvent™ Caspase-3/7 Green Flow Cytometry Assay Kit Thermofisher, C10427)
While thawing, move caspase samples to flow tubes/microtubes and wash again. Aspirate or dump, as long as 100 ul is left in tube.
Heat block the samples that you want to have more cell death (eg- positive control, comp controls). Let samples sit on heat block at 65C for 5 min. An FMO for caspase 3/7 and an FMO for 7AAD is especially important here. Heat block both of them here.
Make caspase stock solution—add 1 ul of caspase reagent to 1 ml of FACS (1:1000 dilution), add 100ul of solution to each tube of 100ul FACS already there (1:2000 final dilution) and incubate at 37C for 30 min. *Manufacturer says 1:1000 but this is very bright, 1:2000 is better.
Make 7AAD stock solution (after diluting in DMSO)
After making the stock solution, add 2.5 ul of 7AAD to 500 ul of FACS (1:200 dilution). Add 50ul of this solution to each sample tube that already has 200ul FACS in it from caspase staining (1:1000 final dilution). *Requires flow samples to be run immediately after caspase 3/7/7AAD stain as there is not quech step afterwards. Have compensation and experiment ready to run samples. You can batch the time you add caspase and 7AAD by tissue type so some samples are not incubating while you’re running the other tissues. This step is especially time sensitive, plan accordingly or you will have overstaining with the reagents.

title: Running Gel_ATM
text:
Procedure

Low percentage agarose for large fragments

Use 0.5 - 1% for 6 kb of fragment for better separation, or 2% for 100 - 800 bp.

If doing 0.7%, get 0.7g of agarose into one of the gel flasks, put into weighing scale.
Add 100 mL of TAE buffer to the flask.
Put in microwave 2 min. Shake to dissolve crystals.
Pour the gel cage into the box.
Then put the boiling glass into water to cool until its safe enough to touch.
Pipette 4 µL EB into the cooled glass (10 mg/ml EtBR).
Add the comb to the top of the cage wide teeth down.
Add the solution to the cage. Let dry for about 30-45 min.
Put the dried gel into the gel running box with the holes facing up.
Fill with TAE buffer until the gel is fully submerged.
Add 10 ul of Generuler 1kb plus ladder.
Add a 1:6 dilution of 6x orange to the DNA you want to run in the gel. For instance 30 ul DNA, add 5 ul of 6x orange.
Put the DNA into one of the wells on the gel and keep track of which one it is.
Connect black wire to the top of the box (negative) and red to the bottom of the box (positive).
95 V, 30 A, 300 W. Time 30:00 min - Run

Cas9 Nucleofection
Introduction
Get started by giving your protocol a name and editing this introduction.
Materials
› Materials
› Lonza 4D-NucleofectorTM System
› P3 primary cell 4D Nucleofector electroporation kit (Lonza, Cat# V4XP-3032 for electroporation wells, Cat#
V4SP-4032 for cuvettes)
› P3 buffer: make fresh on the day, mix 3.6 μl reagent 1 with 16.4 μl diluent per reaction (Lonza Nucleofector
kit) [Though Lonza tech support said it’s good for a month in 4 °C.]
› Recombinant Cas9 protein, 40 μM, –80 °C [Ordered Cas9-NLS purified protein (2.5 mg) from University of
California Berkeley Macrolab]
› 20 bp gRNAs – 80-mer scaffold with chemical modification
› R10 (RPMI + 10% FCS, glutamine, antibiotics, 50 mM BME, NEAA, HEPES)
Procedure
CD8 Enrichment
1. If naïve, do CD8 enrichment prior to protocol.
2. If activated, activate 24 hr prior to this protocol.
Reconstitute Tracr
3. To reconstitute tracrRNA - if 20 nmol + 200 μl buffer
- new CRISPR tracr resuspend in 200ul of Duplex buffer
4. Resuspending crRNA - Check the resuspension calculator on IDT. I did 100 ul to get to 100 uM
CRISPR/Cas9 electroporation
5. To make a Cas9/RNA complex, mix guides plus tracr RNA as below in PCR tubes:

gRNA thy1 guide only control


Page 1 of 3


gRNA thy1 guide plus guide of 1st target
gRNA thy1 guide plus guide of 2nd target
etc.

- We want to do 3:1 molar ratio of guide RNA to Cas9 enzyme.
- Thy1 AC guide at 100 μM concentration.
- Experimental guides are at 100 μM concentration.
- tracrRNA at 100 μM concentration.
- Set up as follows:
Control

- 3 μl thy1 AC crRNA guide from IDT
- 3 μl tracr RNA (Alt-R® CRISPR-Cas9 tracrRNA, ATTOTM 550)
- We might need to add 1.5 μl buffer here too (idk ask Nicole)

Experimental (× number of groups needed)

- 1.5 μl thy1 AC crRNA guide from IDT
- 3 μl guide of experimental guide (Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 crRNA from IDT)
- 3 μl tracr RNA (Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 tracrRNA, ATTOTM 550)

6. Incubate in thermocycler at 95 °C for 5 minutes, then immediately remove and put at RT in the dark for 1 hour for
annealing.
7. Add 2.38μl 40 μM Cas9 enzyme to each tube (use –80). DO NOT MIX. Gently flick the tube to mix sgRNAs with
Cas9 and spin down briefly to collect drops from the sides of the tube. Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature
for complex formation.
8. Make a P3 buffer mix below per reaction and keep at room temperature.
1× buffer recipe, make enough for each run: [Lonza (in fridge)]
Supplement 1: 3.6 μl
P3: 16.4 μl
9. Take 10 mL of R10 plus 50 U/mL hIL2 (a 1:2000 dilution), and put into a water bath to warm to 37 °C.
Pipette media into well and collect in tube, then spin.
10. Count cells, then spin down cells in large volume of STERILE, RT PBS (4ml) to remove potential RNase
contamination from FCS-containing media before electroporation (IMPORTANT). Can do 2-10×10^6 cells per
reaction.
11. Immediately after complex formation, transfer cells into Eppendorf tubes in 1 mL of PBS, and spin down on a
tabletop centrifuge at 5000 RPM for 5 min at room temp. It is important to prepare everything before resuspending the cells in P3 buffer to minimize the time the cells are exposed to the buffer.
12. Take supernatant from the cell pellet using pipets (make sure to take off all remaining liquid from cell pellet to not
dilute out the small reaction volume of 25 μl). Resuspend cell pellet in 20 μl P3 buffer per reaction.
13. Transfer 5 μl CRISPR/Cas9 RNP into the 20 μl P3 buffer with cells and mix gently.

Page 2 of 3

14. Transfer the 25 μl cell/RNP mix into the bottom of a well of the Lonza nucleofector plate and mix gently. Be careful
to not create any bubbles. (Keep time of cells in P3 buffer as short as possible — it is cytotoxic to the cells.)
15. Electroporate cells by putting the nucleofector strip into the Lonza nucleofector and as specified, start program:
- Naïve CD8 T cells: use DN100 program in P3 buffer
- Activated CD8 T cells: use DS137 program in P3 buffer
16. After electroporation (a few seconds) add 130 μl of 37 °C pre-warmed R10 media into the well containing
electroporated cells and rest cells for 10 minutes in the incubator (5% CO2, 37 °C).
17. Resuspend the cells in the electroporation well using a pipette, and transfer the cell suspension into a fresh tube or
well. To recover any remaining cells, wash the electroporation well with an additional 150 μl R10 media by pipetting, and transfer the media into the same collection tube. Add 700 μl pre-warmed R10 to make 1 mL total.
18. Count the cells with Trypan Blue. 20–50% of T cells will be lost during the electroporation step.
19. For in vivo adoptive transfer, resuspend in PBS at desired concentration and adoptively transfer into recipient
mice via intravenous injection. Keep some cells growing in culture for future flow and KO validation with flow or Sanger sequencing (if naïve, activate as well).

Page 3 of 3

title: Taking down SI and Liver and embedding in OCT
text:
WEDNESDAY, 3/25/2026

To grab before going to the mouse room:
10 cm plates for disecting the gut in
PBS
Fixative BD cytofix cytoperm 1:2 dilution into PBS for a total of 15*5ml.
Syringe for pumping out the fixative.
The tips for the end of the syringe.
The labeled sticks to push through the guts.
Eye dropper to wet the labeled stick.
Plastic box for holding the rods after guts are on them. Fill with 4% PFA
15 - 15 ml conicals for liver. Fill these with PFA WHAT PERCENTAGE PFA
Put PBS in a 10 cm dish.
Get plastric box for rods ready.
Cut open mouses skin - dont knick the inside.
Then open the inside layer of skin
cut the lowest possible point, where the colon attaches to the butt
cut the point that connects to stomach.
Put the whole gut into the 10 cm dish
Take Liver, cut the different lobes apart.
Put 2 lobes in the flow plate.
Put the rest of the lobes in a PFA conical.
Take spleen and put in flow plate.
Back to gut.
cut off the colon from the rest
Grab the syringe and put tip on it. pull up the 2% fixative - 5 ml.
Hold top of gut with forceps while flushing it with the syringe.
Cut off some of the connective tissue after flushing.
Grab one of the long lebeled rods. Wet it with PBS with the eye dropper.
Grab the top of the gut again, slide it onto the rod.
Cut off the rest of the gut thats not on the rod.
Put the rod in the plastic box.
Wrap up everything downstairs, and go upstairs to the fume hood.
To grab once you get upstairs:
Grab one of the really big plates, put it face down.
Grab the good pair of scissors with the ballpoint.
Grab a little beaker, fill it with PBS.
Grab the box with the elongated rows for the guts. Fill it with 4% PFA. Label it 1 to whatever with a piece of tape.
Grab the pink base needles with the wax on the end for rolling.
Grab the 30 gage pins
6wp with 4% PFA in each well. Labeled for each gut.
For each gut:
Cut off the pieces of fat on the rod.
grab the end of the gut, drag it off the rod and into a straight line on the late.
Cut the cut through the middle, DO NOT CUT ALL THE WAY THROUGH THE OTHER END.
Grab the gut and dip it in the little beaker of pbs to clean it.
Lay the gut back onto the plate.
Lay the gut into the corresponding elongated well and make sure its straight.
Wait 1 hour (Probably dont need to wait tbh since it’ll take a long time for all the guts)
For each gut:
Grab gut and put it on plate straight.
Find the notch that hasn’t been cut yet.
Open the gut up so that the inside faces up on the plate. use the knitting needle rod things to roll the gut open on the plate.
You can now cut the bad end of the gut off.
Grab one of the pink base needles with the wax on the end.
ROLL FROM THE BOTTOM SO THE VILLI ARE FACING OUT
Once rolled, Take the gut off the wax needle with forceps.
Hold ends of the rolled gut with forceps and stick a 30 gage pin all the way through.
Place into the 6wp in the correct well.
Wrap 6wp in aluminum foil and put into cold room 4C overnight.
Once done, put 6wp into cold room

text:
Custom CRISPR Cas9 screens in the LsgA backbone
using Illumina-compatible libraries
Miguel Reina-Campos – Goldrath Lab
07/13/2022
Objective: Clone ~150 sgRNAs covering 50 genes (~3x sgRNAs/gene) in the LsgA vector for customizable screening pools in CD8 T cells

Order OligoPools

Forward library: 5’ Phospho-CACCNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN
Reverse library: 5’ Phospho-AAACNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN


Annealed oligos will look like this:
5’ Phospho-CACCNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN
NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNCAAA-5’ Phospho
*The 5’ Phosphate will allow ligation to occur using dephosphorylated BbsI-linearized LsgA vector.
Design your sgRNA sequences and upload to IDT to order oPools Oligo Pools
Order two different pools of single-stranded DNA oligos, Forward library and Reverse library.
Price: 10 pmol/oligo, 120 sgRNA sequences.
Each sequence is 24 nts * 120 = 2880 nts total, charged at oPools DNA Base 1 ($109 / pool) + $1.65 * 120 = $109 per pool and $198 for 5’ phosphorylation for a total of $307 per pool.


Vector Preparation: LsgA library vector



Digest and dephosphorylate 20 ug of vector with BbsI for 1h at 37C. Set up the following reaction:

100 ul reaction

10X rCutSmart Buffer 10 uL
LsgA vector (20 ug)
HF-BbsI (NEB) 3 uL
Alkaline Phosphatase Quick CIP (NEB) 5 uL
Water Fill to 100 uL

Run in a 0.8 % Agarose TAE Gel using wide combs
Purify linearized dephosphorylated oligo using QIAGEN Gel purification kit
Resuspend in ~40 ul of ddH2O

sgRNA oligo annealing

IDT oligopools come as a dried DNA pellet with 10 pmols of each oligo.
Resuspension in 100 ul of ddH2O generates 1 uM stock for each oligo. For a 155 oligo-pool, this makes a ~150 uM ssDNA.

Anneal sgRNA ssODN:

1 uL Forward library (Final concentration of each oligo ~100 nM)
1 uL Reverse library (Final concentration of each oligo ~100 nM)
1 uL 10X T4 Ligation Buffer (NEB)
7 uL ddH2O

Put the phosphorylation/annealing reaction in a thermocycler using the following parameters:


37oC 30 min
95oC 5 min
ramp down to 25oC at 6oC/min
keep at RT


Ligation

1:1 ligation ratios
Vector is 7Kb while oligos are 24 nts, which makes the vector ~300x bigger than the insert.
Include a “No insert negative control”
25 ng of 7kb dsDNA vector in 10 ul reaction makes for a ~550 pM

Dilute annealed library 1:200 (100 nM to 500 pM)
Set up ligation reaction in a total volume of 10 ul


Dephosphorylated BbsI-linearized LsgA vector backbone 25 ng (550 pM)
1:200 Annealed sgRNA library 1 uL
10X Ligase buffer 1 uL
ddH2O Fill to 10 uL


Test Transformation

A series of test transformations will be performed to verify correct inserts and successful ligations with low background. Two serial transformations will be performed, as a single transformation of the ligation product generates many mixed peaks during Sanger sequencing of colony PCR product.

Primary transformation with high efficiency chemically competent cells (Stbl3 cells).



Add 0.5uL ligation to 20 uL Stellar cells, and gently tap to mix.
Incubate on ice for 30 minutes.
Heat-shock 45s @ 42oC.
Incubate on ice for 2 min.
Add 300 uL pre-warmed SOC and incubate for 1 hour at 37oC.
Plate 200 uL on pre-warmed plates (save the remaining recovery at RT or 4C).
Incubate O/N at 37oC.
*Set up as many plates as needed - test transformation to obtain ~1k to 4k colonies per plate.
*Limit culture time to ~16h to prevent colonies from overgrowing

Got ~5k colonies per plate on the first try, with ~200 colonies in the vector-only plate (negative control). Vector only might self-religate in the absence of an insert (~50 to 200 colonies is normal background).

Plasmid prep: If your negative control shows <5% background colonies, it is safe to proceed.
Scrape plates with 1.5 mL of LB and purify plasmid and prepare midi-prep. This is the plasmid library prep used for large-scale transformation, although it could be also used for the screen - subsequent steps are needed for verification of equal sgRNA representation.
Secondary transformation with subcloning efficiency in Stbl3 cells.



Add 1ul of the prepared plasmid to 15-20uL of DH5a and gently tap to mix.
Incubate on ice for 2 minutes
Heat-shock 30s @ 42oC
Incubate on ice for 2 min
Add 980 uL SOC
Plate 1/50x (~20uL) in 6 different plates for each sample.
Plate 6 plates per
Incubate O/N at 37oC

Pick as many colonies from each plate as needed. The rule of thumb is to pick one colony for every 5 sgRNAs (~20%, ie 30 colonies for 155 sgRNas) – make minipreps and sequence using hU6. This QC makes sure the ration of the un-inserted religated vector is low, and that inserts are correctly cloned in the vector

Align the Sanger sequence output to the library vector map in your favorite cloning software (e.g. SnapGene) to ensure the sgRNAs were cloned properly
The 19 to 20bp corresponding to the unique protospacer sequence should not align it the vector. Search for this sequence in the list of sgRNAs in your oligo pool. If 70-90% of the sequences match to the correct library (you will likely see some oligo synthesis errors and sequencing errors), it is safe to proceed with the large-scale transformation.

*No sequences should perfectly align to the library vector at the protospacer region. This would indicate that the parental vector was incompletely digested and the stuffer sequence is present in the library.
**It is also extremely unlikely that any sgRNA appears multiple times in a random set of 10 colonies. Repeated sequences are an indication that one species from the oligo pool is very overrepresented.

Large Scale Transformation

If the test transformation worked, use the plasmid library prep from step 5c. to transform Stbl3 bacteria following this protocol:

Pre-warm LB/carbenecillin plates 3-4 hours ahead of time.
Thaw Stbl3 cells on ice
Add 10 ng plasmid to 50 uL Stbl3 cells
Heat shock at 42 C for 30 seconds
Leave on ice for 2 minutes
Add 950 uL of SOC media
Incubate at 37 C for one hour
Plate 10X LB Agar Carbenicillin plates



Scrape Plates

Add 15-25 mL LB for the initial scrape. Transfer to a clean collection tube. Add an additional 5-15 mL LB and transfer to collection tube. If you are scraping multiple plates, place your collection tube on ice. Once you are finished scraping, spin at 4,000 rpm for 20 min. The pellet should be tight. Pour off media and freeze pellet or proceed with plasmid preparation.

Plasmid Preparation

Qiagen or Sigma midi, maxi, mega or giga plasmid prep kits. Make sure columns are dry prior to the final elution. Wet columns will give a low recovery.

9) Prepare Samples for Illumina Sequencing

Illumina sequencing of the resulting plasmids is advised to ensure the resulting plasmid libraries from this protocol are correct, have a large fraction of sgRNAs that match perfectly to the expected library, and the relative fractions of each sgRNA are tightly distributed. You only need ~100 sequencing reads per sgRNA in the library to be able to validate the library (ex. 12K reads), so you can include your samples as a <5% spike- in other sequencing runs.
To sequence your libraries, follow Step 3 of the sequencing sample prep protocol with the following modifications:

If you are spiking into a sequencing sample with high diversity, such as an RNA-seq experiment, you can omit the Set A/B strategy and just sequence with Set A primer pairs and sequencing primer
For the PCR, perform one 100uL PCR per library. If you have cloned multiple sublibraries, PCR each individually with a different sample index to allow you to detect any cross-contamination or sample mix-ups (although be careful to not introduce this during the PCR!).
Substitute the genomic DNA input into the PCR with 100ng library plasmid.
Only perform 15 cycles of PCR.

Amplicon sequence:
TTCGATTTCTTGGCTTTATATATCTTGTGGAAAGGACGAAANNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNGTTTTAGAGCTAGAAATAGCAAGTTAAAATAAGGCTAGTCCGTTATCAACTTGAAAAAGTGGCACCGAGTCGGTGCTTTTTTGAATTC 3’

These primers are first used to amplify plasmid-coded amplicon from genomic DNA. IMPORTANT: These primers will amplify a 96 bp from the LsgA, and a 1962 bp from the LMG (containing the sgFdft1). Purify lower band by gel if necessary to clean.

LsgA_amplicon_F: 5’TTTCTTGGCTTTATATATCT 3’
LsgA_amplicon_R: 5’GACTAGCCTTATTTTAACTT 3’

PCR
Q5 2X
Vt=50
Touchdown PCR: 10 cycles starting at 61 C in -0.5 C delta
Everything else standard for Q5 protocol
Followed by 25 cycles at Ta 56
Extension times 7 sec
Purified with Qiaquick PCR purification kit

PCR for amplification of the plasmid region with addition of Nextera Handles (P5, P7 tags)

Nextera-Handle-F (P5tag):
5 ‘ TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAGTTTCTTGGCTTTATATATCT 3’
Nextera-Handle-R (P7tag):
5 ‘ GTCTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAGGACTAGCCTTATTTTAACTT 3’
This will amplify a 163 PCR product.
Use 2X Q5 high fidelity DNA polymerase protocol with 20 cycles.
Amplicon:
5’ to 3’
TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAGTTTCTTGGCTTTATATATCTTGTGGAAAGGACGAAANNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNGTTTTAGAGCTAGAAATAGCAAGTTAAAATAAGGCTAGTCCTGTCTCTTATACACATCTCCGAGCCCACGAGAC

Purify PCR product with AMPure XP beads 2X ratio and perform Indexing PCR:

(https://teichlab.github.io/scg_lib_structs/methods_html/Illumina.html)
Use Q5 2X polymerase
Vt=50 ul
16 cycles, TA = 58 C, extension 10 seconds
After PCR, AMPure XP purification with 2X beads ratio
Indices were taken from illumina-adapter-sequences_1000000002694-00.pdf
Sample 1 example
F501 (i5-index-handle): AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACACTAGATCGCTCGTCGGCAGCGTC
R701 (i7-index-handle): CAAGCAGAAGACGGCATACGAGATTCGCCTTAGTCTCGTGGGCTCGG
This will generate a 232 bp PCR amplicon (F501 R701 index example):
AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACACTAGATCGCTCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG’TTTCTTGGCTTTATATATCTTGTGGAAAGGACGAAANNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNGTTTTAGAGCTAGAAATAGCAAGTTAAAATAAGGCTAGTCCTGTCTCTTATACACATCTCCGAGCCCACGAGACTAAGGCGAATCTCGTATGCCGTCTTCTGCTTG
Green: i5, i7
Black: index,
blue: handle P5 and P7 Nextera,
yellow: internal primer used for genomic amplification,
purple: sgRNA sequence
‘: starts reading read 1.
Sequencing math:

10K cell outputs should provide a 64X sgRNA coverage
Every cell should have only one copy of the sgRNA -> 10K sgRNAs
500 reads per sgRNA * 10K sgRNAs = 5M reads per sample
Some samples have 100K, to 230K cells
19 samples * 5M = 95M 300 M minimum
For sequencing read length: the sgRNA sequence starts at 69 nts from the i5 index, and 106 nts from the beginning of the DNA fragment.

Miseq Reagent Kit v3 (https://www.illumina.com/systems/sequencing-platforms/miseq/specifications.html)
Experimental Setup LCMV infection Model


Enrich and in vitro activate P14 Cas9-eGFP donor cells (SOP)


Transduce (SOP)

LsgA pool + LMG-Fdft1 -> Fdft1KO-pool


Expand 1:6 in IL-2/IL-7 for 24h


Sort out Ametrine+/GFPhigh P14 cells:



500K per mouse. N=5 per group. Total 2.5 M per condition


Sorted in cold MACS 10% FBS


Keep 100K cell input for both samples (~650X coverage)



Transfer sorted P14 cells into B6 recipients and infect with LCMV (SOP)


Bleed at day 7 pi to check proportions of TE and TMP for proper expansion


Take Down at day 14 pi, and sort 10K Ame+ GFPhigh P14 from



Spleen P14 Cd19-pool X2


Spleen P14 Fdft1KO-pool X2


SI P14 Cd19-pool X2


SI P14 Fdft1KO-pool X2


Liver P14 IV- Cd19-pool X2


Liver P14 IV- Fdft1KO-pool X2




Experimental Setup MC38-GP33-41
500K Mc38-Gp33-41 implanted
Transferred 500K per mouse at day 10 post-implantation
Sorted cells at day 5 post-transfer

title: Contribute
text:
Clone the repository, add a protocol in markdown format and push it. The website is built automatically after every push. The link to the github repo is github.com/kpc002/protocols-website. Currently this repository is private, so message me if you want access.
If you see a mistake, you can modify the current site my clicking on Edit this page on the right side of each site.
The website is generated using quarto. See their website to learn more about the structure of the webpage.
